title: Super Ninja Fruit Fly Traps: bait useless for my fruit flies while Terro brand bait has worked well.
review: I tried 3 different brands of liquid fruit fly attractant: in this home for 25 yrs but had never had a fruit fly problem in my life, they must have come in w/fruit which we don't buy a lot of: found out one female lays 500 eggs...This product, Super Ninja Fruit fly traps- I put several of these pre-filled bottles out for days but SUPER NINJA FRUIT FLY TRAPS DID NOT CATCH A SINGLE FRUIT FLY, compared to Terro brand used in the red plastic tomatoes, which worked well. I even tried the Super Ninja bait in the red Terro plastic tomatoe containers as some ads claimed the color + shape of the vessel played a role in attracting bugs but still no luck. The excellent Terro brand even worked well in a clear glass baby food jar. Terro works well, I see several of the fruit flies in the liquid. However, the tomatoe shaped plastic holders can tip easy, its a sticky, stinky liquid for which the company in South America would not tell me if it has a percent of poison in it- many of their products do, + they only give the number of poison control, + insist that the formula is 'proprietary information'. But after trying 3 brands, will stick w/Terro even though it does not sell a large container of liquid (I do not need more plastic tomatoe holders plus glass baby food jars worked just as well) Have put the Terro liquid bait-filled plastic tomatoes in clear plastic cups (clear so insects could see the red fruit shape), as the tomatoes have many preferations, which is good, but they are light-weight, tip + spill easily. However, the flat rectangular shape of the bottles of the Super Ninja Fruit fly Traps, though the liquid they came with is useless, the bottles w/their flat walls can be attached to any flat surface or wall w/a sticky strip; That had been my intent when I ordered them so I did not have to worry about containers spilling or space to put them down in or my cat getting to one... As the Ninja contents have proved useless, I will empty + rinse them out so I can fill them w/Terro attractant. will report if the insects will use these glass containers. While I had planned to take advantage of the flat walls of the Ninja glass containers + a photo in the Ad may have suggested they could be stuck to a wall, I was surprised that they came w/a pre-attached silicone sticky strip pre-attached for that purpose (one should use a spatula to remove the sticky strip and bottle intact from the wall (they are silicone w/adhesive + residue can be easily removed). There was one other brand of 25 vials which also did not catch a single fruit fly- even when used in Terro's tomatoe shape, which I also do not recommend, 'Qualirey 20 Pack Fruit Fly Trap Refill Liquid'... Do not recommend the Super Ninja Fly Traps because the bait does not work, at least for my fruit flies in Connecticut; but I still need to substitute Terro liquid bait in their their rectangular glass containers a+ see if the insects will then use them before I formally recommend the containers themselves- they have a yellow funnel on top. However, $39.99 plus tax is a high price to pay for the 12 glass containers which I will need to empty out to use with Terro brand liquid- if the bugs will use that container w/Terro bait.

title: Stinky and Ineffective

I have no idea where these creatures came from or how they managed to establish a thriving civilization so quickly, having deep-cleaned my room and offering absolutely no food, water, or emotional support to these bugs. And yet, they have moved in and declared sovereignty. In a panic, I bought several traps. This one now lives on my work desk, because nothing says “professional” like taking meetings while insects launch themselves into your face like kamikaze pilots. The trap smells VILE, like rotting fruit and decay. I can smell it the moment I enter the room. The bugs are clearly obsessed with the scent, but instead of going inside the trap like advertised, they just loiter around it like it’s a sketchy bar. After more than 24 hours, one trap caught **five** bugs. The other caught **none**. Meanwhile, a different brand trap elsewhere has racked up a body count, which confirms this product’s only real function is making my room smell awful. Would not buy again unless I decide my room needs to smell like death **and** still have bugs.

title: Does not attract or trap fruit flies--dish soap or plug-in light works much better
review: DOES NOT WORK. I have a gnat infestation in my indoor office plants. Because they are in my office, where I spend 8 hours per day, I needed them gone, stat. I tried 3 different methods of gnat elimination: (1) Terro apple-shaped fly traps; (2) Shallow dishes of liquid dish soap; (3) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap. After 3 days, here are the results: (1) Terro apple-shaped fly traps: Easy to set up and fill with their "special" gnat-attracting formula which I am sure is just apple cider vinegar. The apple containers are small and cute. But, they don't work. I CAUGHT 1 (ONE) GNAT using 4 different traps placed on top of soil in my plant containers. (2) Shallow dishes of dawn dish soap: Easy to set up and fill. However, the liquid soap starts to dry out and harden after several days. They are a bit of a pain to wash out and refill, icks me out, plus I think it's a waste of dish soap. I CAUGHT 50 GNATS using this method--I used 4 different shallow containers placed on top of soil in my plant containers. (3) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap. This plug-in fly trap was super easy to set up. It's basically a blue light that attracts the insects and super sticky paper (comes with replacement inserts) to trap them. I CAUGHT 40 GNATS using this method. This trap is the furthest from my plants--it's about 6 feet away. If I move it closer, it will probably work even better. This is my favorite scent-free, mess-free method that actually works. If I didn't use the other 2 methods, I would have about 100 more gnats still flying around my office space, ick. Save your money and don't buy.

title: Don't Buy Terro Fruit Fly Traps
review: I will not ever buy this product again!!! It has not trap a gnat in over a week or two. The Sticky stickers work right away the same day they are put out.

title: They didn’t work for me.
review: We are having a slight fruit fly problem, and I put these throughout the house. Haven’t caught a single fly in a week and a half. I bought the uv plug in traps and those have been working great.

title: Not worth it!
review: Don't waste your money, four of them have been sitting out for 3-4 days now and the only one that has some fruit flies is right by my house plants. The other 3, 1 in the kitchen, one in the bathroom and 1 by my computer have nothing but I see them flying around the lights.

title: Dosent work for flightless fruit flies
review: I have over 100 flies in my reptile room becasue of some escapeses and in 3 days not one of them cought any.

title: Doesn't Work
review: I have it in a open central location in my kitchen and it's been almost 2 weeks and it hasn't caught a single fruit fly. Just doesn't work.

title: Raid brand worked better.
review: Did not work. The Raid brand works better. I thought this would be better but not for me.

title: Don't Waste Your Money
review: I was excited about these for the fruit flies that have gotten out of control at my apartment. I figured they would work as well as Raid brand ant lures so I got 4 for each room. But they do not work at all and have not caught one single fly. Using apple cider vinegar in a jar with a few drops of dawn dish soap actually works better.

title: Gnat-chella invitation
review: I love Terro Products so I was really excited to see this when I finally got tired of the repeat customers of about 5 gnats in my kitchen. No matter how many I killed it was like they renegerated. OK, Terro here we go. I put the traps (cute) down before bed, spread 4 of them around the kitchen and dining room. Woke up, excited to see what I had caught...NOPE!! GNAT-CHELLA was going on in my kitchen. Gnats on the walls, gnats on the paper towel roll!! It was like I had sent an invitation to come hang out! NOT ONE GNAT in the traps. One gnat ON the trap but he was like yeah, I'm good out here! Since I can't return the product now that I have used them, I am out some beans. I ordered that light one so lets see what my gnat problem becomes next. For now, back to swatting...sigh.

title: Not a good product to remove fruit flies
review: Not worth any star. Please do not buy this product. Iam looking for a refund.

title: Useless
review: Completely useless, these flying annoying little monsters keep flying around like the traps are not even there.

title: Do not waste $$$$
review: does not work and does not kill fruit flies. juice disappears rapidly and no bugs caught or killed.

title: Not Useful
review: not a single fly was caught after a week. I made my own trap as others have, in a cup with apple cider vinegar and a few drops of dish soap, and it is much more effective.

title: Doesn't catch Gnats....
review: Hasn't caught a single gnat in them, apple cider vinegar and a drop of soap has been catching them wayyyy better. Can't refund unfortunately.

title: Didn't work
review: Bought the package of 4. Used all 4 and only captured 2 gnats. They would crawl on top of the traps, but wouldn't go in them. So I made my own traps with apple cider vinegar, dish soap and sugar. Caught a lot of them that way.

title: Eliminating fruit flies by making more of them?
review: This is a terrible product. I bought 4 of these and then my wife bought another 4 unbeknownst to me. Will these kill fruit flies? Absolutely. So why the 1 star review? They'll make more fruit flies than they'll kill. They don't kill off all of the fruit flies. The ones that survive reproduce and make even more fruit flies. We went from having a dozen to dozens of dozens. Our kitchen is crawling with them. The traps allow the fruit flies to move in and out freely so the flies that don't die just reproduce more resistant flies. How did I end up fixing this Terro created problem? By making my own fruit fly traps with jars filled with red wine, plastic wrap over the top with a rubber band to hold it in place, and then poking holes through them. Cost me nothing since I had these objects already on hand. I will never buy this product again.

title: Very small tiny container
review: These traps are so tiny that you cannot grasp them to get the top off. The top is a pop off top but you can’t get it off. Have husband find a thin metal tool and perhaps he can pry it off. The attractant smells like vinegar and you can squirt it thru the top hole; however not sure how you can pry the top off to clean it. Previously I have used the FlyFix Fruit fly trap. It is bigger and the top screws off for cleaning and filling. I have always used apple cider vinegar with excellent results. They are a little more expensive but worth it if you have fruit fly problems. No need to keep buying attractant as apple cider vinegar works well; some people put slices of banana in the trap and claim it works well. I’m going to try it! I just ordered some more FlyFix fruit fly traps.

title: Just use the home remedy for fruit flies and save 10 bucks.
review: I thought this would work better than the home remedy of apple cider vinegar in a dish with plastic wrap on top with a few holes. It does not. In fact, it isn't as good. I would not recommend purchasing.

title: Not worth it
review: Not working for me at all. I’ve put in 3 places and not even one fruit fly killed. Going back to fruit ninja. Highly disappointed. Only thing I liked is the apple decor

title: It does not work
review: What a waste of money! After 2 days of being out, the device managed to catch 3 fruit flies! I caught more than that in my morning coffee cup!

title: You decide
review: I put out all the traps and have noticed after 6 days I have captured ( killed) 4 fruit flys....as I type this review I just tried to kill one flying in front of my face. I wouldn't buy these again even if they were free.

title: Ineffective - Smell made us NAUSEOUS
review: didn't seem very effective. Most of the flies just sat on top or ignored it. We only had the traps out for about 2 hours so we can't say how effective they were long term, but we were forced to dump them and throw them out because having them out made us both severely nauseous at the same time in the same way. We didn't even realize they were the culprit til we went outside to feel better, and as soon as we went back to our offices where the traps were, the nausea returned. So we cannot use them. Nausea is far worse than a few fruit flies. We'll just buy some sticky tape traps at this point.

title: Failllllll
review: Nothing more than apple cider vinegar. One of the tunes of it was open and leaked all in package. Don't waste your $ or time on these

title: Not necessary
review: Don’t get these literally just buy apple cider vinegar and put them in small cups. Works the same

title: Seems to BREED more bugs.
review: It attracted the fruit flies alright--but they just multiplied inside the darn traps and now I have swarms of the little bugs instead of an annoying but manageable issue. Not sure how to get rid of the ones that bred in the traps. This is just awful.

title: Not working
review: It’s a fraud , 3 days and the liquid is evaporated ( it’s inside the house ) and catches nothing

title: Don’t work AT ALL!
review: Bought 4 of these & they don’t work at all! Have escaped flightless fruit flies from feeding dart frogs & small geckos. Two are near where the tanks are that I put the flies in. One within 5’ and the other in the kitchen as they migrated there. None have worked!

title: Its A Scam!
review: Don't buy this! Its a total scam! Its just apple cider vinegar in a silly cup. And oh by the way, even if you don't open it, THEY WON'T TAKE IT BACK!! So avoid this like the plague.

title: Doesn’t work
review: Doesn’t work. Save your money and use apple cider vinegar in a small plate with the same results.

title: Fruit Fly Killer vs. Home Remedy (FTW)
review: I bought the fruit fly traps and set them out... nothing. All four little traps are loaded and sitting there in the disaster zones (garbage disposal, trash can, pantry, plant corner). Not a single trap lured in a single fruit fly. Nor do I see the fruit flies interested in the little traps after several days. They're circling my hanging pans more than the little trap. Maybe the solution was expired? I got online and found some homemade remedies. I put out several plates with apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar and dish soap. Worked like a charm. Two days later, lots of fruit flies in that mixture and problem is down 80%. For pennies on the dollar, a much better solution. I'm going to try the homemade solution inside their cute little traps to see if it works. After 2 weeks: I kept both the traps out and the homemade remedy. Traps caught about 20% of the flies; homemade remedy on plates about 80%. Also, the liquid in the traps dried out quick and were a pain to refill, etc.

title: Doesn’t work
review: Don’t waste your money. This didn’t work at all!

title: These did nothing
review: Useless. After a few days of no change and no gnats in the traps I tried to old vinegar and dish soap and the gnats swarmed to it. So just stick to the old home redies.

title: Terro fruit fly trap
review: Did not work didn't even catch one fly

title: Did not work!
review: I got fruit flies from over-ripen bananas and wanted to get rid of them as soon as possible so I got these TERRO Fruit Fly Traps. I don't see any fruit flies going into the plastic red apple. Whatever the juice that came with it this product doesn't attract the fruit flies.

title: Dont buy this
review: This product is not good. It created a medium for the fruit flies to mass reproduce. Now I have a small infestation. Very upset about this product

title: Made it so much worse- DO NOT BUY
review: This product had so many good reviews so I was really hopeful it would help! There were 3 pesky fruit flies I couldn’t seem to get rid of, I put out two of these “traps” and the next day BOOM it had turned into a full infestation I was horrified. These traps end up attracting more flies into the home, they’re able to get out of the trap because of the many holes, and then they reproduce so quickly. I’m so glad I had a bug killing spray (the STEM brand is amazing) and also the plug-in sticky traps so I was able to get the problem under control but wow I am so disappointed in this product. A complete waste of money, and ended up causing me so much unnecessary stress/anxiety.

title: Quality has gone down
review: I am not sure what has happened to this product. It used to work well. This time it hardly worked at all. Maybe a bad batch?

title: Trash.
review: Quickly evaporates, reeks of apple cider vinegar (I’m convinced that’s all it is), and of the three that I didn’t knock over and spill everywhere, I caught a total of *1* gnat/fruit fly in the two weeks before they were bone dry. Save your money and get one of those UV light traps instead.

title: Did not work.
review: Did not trap more than one fruit fly per container over a span of several weeks.

title: Ineffective
review: Worthless. Didn't catch a single fruit fly in 4 traps in a weeks time. Decided to then purchase a UV/blue light trap that caught over a dozen in under a day.

title: Make Sure You Have Fruit Flies Not Gnats
review: I thought I had fruit flies but I think I had gnats. These did not trap anything and the liquid provided just evaporates. Amazon would not take our return as you have to open the box to see the product. We then ordered the product that you plug into the wall that shines a blue light and captures gnats on a sticky surface. This second product is working beautifully. We have caught over 100 gnats in a few days. So, make sure you have fruit flies not gnats. Fruit flies and gnats look very similar, so don't make the same mistake we did, or you will be wasting your money like we did.

title: NEVER EVER BUY THIS! WASTE OF MONEY!
review: DO NOT BUY LIKE SERIOUSLY ITS SO BAD! I had a fly infestation and the liquid did nothing but evaporate (it was indoor too). I set it up where the flies were spawning from and it caught NOTHING. It's an awful trap. Definitely not worth the money. I wish I could give it zero stars. You can't even return or get refund because of transportation of hazardous materials which is so dumb because how did they send it in the first place. COMPLETE Waste of money. Go buy the light traps instead. I don't know how these other reviews were positive. I ended up having to kill all the flies myself. I killed 26 in one day and these apples sat as dumb decorations.

title: Ineffective
review: I found the product to be ineffective for my use case and is unable to be returned. Would not buy again and I wish I just went with sticky pads as I originally intended

title: Waste of money
review: I bought this because I have a lot of fruit flies recently. When I received this I set it up as noted in instructions and no fruit flies have been attracted to it. Waste of money!!

title: Product Effectiveness
review: There are two traps in each box but only one tube of the liquid. Either the product is short one tube or your supposed to share the tube with both traps - it's not clear. I think there should be two tubes of liquid - one for each trap. Another thing to consider is that the trap does capture some fruit flies - however, most of the fruit flies that enter the trap fly back out of it. A better and more cost-effective way is to get a small jar of some sugar water in it and place something sticky like fly paper sticking out of the jar. This product works but barely. Not worth the cost.

title: Does not work
review: After a month no fruit flies captured, I had this product a year ago and it worked that's why I decided to order it but this time no fruit flies eliminated and the liquid evaporated.

title: This product Doesn't Work
review: Doesn't really work. I have had four traps out for 24 hours and only caught a single fruit fly with them. Just make your own traps with apple cider vinegar, they work better

title: Used for years, but something changed!
review: I’ve been brand-loyal to Terro for years. When I opened the box, I noticed new packaging for the liquid- and now I notice that it no longer traps flies like it used to. With the old bait (clear cylinder, blue screw lid), I would catch ALL of them. This packaging (clear squeeze tube with lid that needed to be cut off) must contain a different formulation because it doesn’t work at all. It also evaporates more quickly.

title: There are better solutions.
review: This did not work well. I had better results with vinegar and dish soap. The apples are cute, but that's about it.

title: Avoid this
review: These are crap. They definitely attract flies but there’s so little liquid that if the flies don’t go all the way in the trap and down the the very bottom, nothing’s going to happen. Them advertising the flies have no way back out is literally just false. The holes they go in through are so large they can just as easily get back out. Going into the little liquid given is the only thing that kills them.

title: Cute, but doesn’t work!
review: This was a super easy to put together and aesthetically pleasing fly catcher, the only problem is that it doesn’t catch any flies. There’s not a single fruit fly in the container and although they seem to be hovering around the area—I’ve kept this catcher out for about half of the week and absolutely nothing. Save yourself some dollars and make a catcher yourself with sugar and apple cider vinegar.

title: It sucks
review: Edit: Knocking off two more stars because the liquid evaporated in 2 days. 180 days? Nope. Noticed improvement within 12 hours, but only after placing two traps, one did not seem to be enough. I will also add that the solution seems to be your standard apple cider vinegar. If the apple trap is what you want specifically over a jar and saran wrap it's definitely worth it but otherwise there's nothing special about the product. Be sure to fill the apples away from any spot you want to save, I filled them at my work desk before moving them where they were needed and that was my mistake. The lingering smell of vinegar attracted them to that spot for hours and it was quite annoying.

title: Bogus product
review: These are simply tiny plastic containers filled with apple vinegar. Absolutely zero accountability or pride in their product. Buying these is identical to buying snake oil. Just but apple cider vinegar and sage your money. -CSL

title: Does not work
review: I did exactly what it said on the box and it did not work at all .

title: Doesn’t work!
review: buy a UV light trap. I had four of these and literally didn’t catch a single fruit fly in all of them and i must have caught 50+ when using a UV light trap. Ridiculous.

title: Did NOT WORK
review: These did not work. Caught 2 gnats over 3 months of trying. Wish Icould return!

title: Not the Terro Quality I Expected
review: Terro Ant baits are my go-to for dealing with ant problems, so I assumed this product would work just as effectively for dealing with fruit flies. WRONG. The flies go in the plastic apple, but are able to fly right out. This product caught zero fruit flies. In contrast, our homemade fruitfly trap that we keep at the other end of our home behind a closed door works like a charm. We took an empty salsa glass jar (the kind that is short with a wider opening and is generally found next to the potato chips at the grocery store), and poked several small holes in the metal lid (I forgot whether we used a nail, or a drill), and filled it halfway with apple cider vinegar. Works like a charm and cost almost nothing to make. I bought the Terro fruitfly traps for the kitchen because I'm too lazy to make another homemade trap, and I thought the plastic apples would look nicer. But it ended up being a waste of money.

title: Ineffective. Buy something else.
review: I can ditto the other 1-star reviews of this product. INEFFECTIVE. Waste of money.

title: They do not work
review: These are ineffective. I have fruit flies all over the house and had them in the worst areas for three weeks. I got one fly. Save your money

title: Wasted money
review: They don't work at all. Total waste of money!

title: Does not work!!!
review: Highly disappointed. Used this brand of ant traps/bait and they worked. I had this out for 2 weeks or more. Not one fruit fly caught, though there were many fruit flies to be had!! Just realized as I sit in parking lot of UPS trying to pull up return code that I can’t return this 4 pack of little red plastic apples - because that’s all this is. Nothing more than a cheap Dollar store item!! They really should have a zero star option. Yes, I’m annoyed!! 🤪

title: Didn't catch anything
review: waste of money. Put two of these out, only caught one fruit fly before the lure dried up. I placed them close to the sink & trash can, where the fruit flies hang out. Left them there for a few weeks and was disappointed with the result. I caught more flies in my morning coffee than in these traps! Side note: I don't like that Terro doesn't list what the active ingredient is in their fly trap chemicals. I'd prefer to know what chemicals are in it before I leave it sitting out on my counters.

title: If you have houseflies this will make it much worse
review: TLDR - if you have homeflies in your area, don't buy this. This was the biggest mistake I've made in years buying this product. If you have a fruit fly problem, buy a plastic cup and fill it with apple cider vinegar; it's the same thing. I live in an area with houseflies, this product made it so much worse. The smell of the apple cider vinegar attracted hundreds of houseflies. They actually started hanging around my door and finding the tiniest cracks to funnel through. They crawled through the screen door via the corners, through cracks in window AC units, etc. I spent hours catching them and had to buy a electric fly swatter. Its one thing to buy a product that doesn't work, its something completely different to create more problems and worsen it. Plus its already a way overpriced for a container and apple cider vinegar.

title: Not very effective
review: Not worth it. Ive left two traps for over 2 days and they’ve catched maybe 4 fruit flies all together. The flies literally stay on top of the plastic and dont fall inside. Not very effective

title: Effectiveness
review: Useless product, in over 3 days of use, it only trapped a single gnat, while a swarm of it is flying around it

title: Cute but doesn't work.
review: These do not work. Today I went back to my old method of apple cider vinegar and dish soap. I had more fruit flies in two hours than in 5 days with this product. Yes, they look cute, but a waste of money. I think it's because the surface area is too small for the flies to get attracted. The jar I'm using is completely open and works great.

title: Pyramid scheme it feels like…
review: THIS DOES NOT WORK! The one thing it’s supposed to do…..AND the bugs are ACTUALLY MOCKING ME. I don’t know who came up with this idea, or what research went in that says this is effective…. The catch ability is NON-EXISTENT!! As seen in the picture, they don’t die or get caught.

title: Fruit Fly Trap
review: There are too many holes, and they are much too large. The fruit flies easily go in and out of the trap. The liquid evaporates too fast to last 30 days. The liquid was gone in just 2 weeks and only caught about 4 bugs in that amount of time. I then used my grandmother's version of a fruit fly trap using a small relish jar with 2 tiny holes drilled in the lid. The solution is apple cider vinegar. In just the 2weeks the Terror trap was in place, the homemade trap caught 2 dozen fruit flies & the liquid hasn't evaporated. In 30 days, the whole surface of the liquid in the glass jar was covered in fruit flies.

title: Not Very Effective
review: Frankly unimpressed. Before getting these, I used a bowl with a TBS of sugar, half a cup of warm water and a few tablespoons of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of Dawn. I also have three Zevo insect traps (basically very sticky plastic inside a plug in that has a warm blue light). The bowl traps were far more effective at getting a dozen of the buggers trapped (fruit fly invasion, and I do mean invasion). The "bait" in these apple traps obviously contains apple cider vinegar. But the flys would crawl around on the outside and only a few would actually end up in the trap. These traps are very small, and supposedly last 45 days which is ridiculous. After only a few days, they stopped working completely. The Zevo traps, on the other hand, had well over a hundred flies trapped. I had to change those traps out twice a week (it's normally like a month or two before they have to be changed, but INVASION of fruit flies). They are much more effective.

title: Not happy with purchase
review: Didn't work as I expected it would. went back to a bowl of apple cider vinegar and a few drops of dish soap, and it seems to work a lot better.

title: Not worth the money
review: For whatever reason these did not work. No fruit fly’s entered the traps and the fluid used to trap the flys dried up in a couple of days. (No extra liquid came in the package.) They knocked over easily and spilled out. Not worth the money.

title: No instructions included
review: No instructions on how to set up or use these was included. There was an insert, but it was just an add for another one of their products.

title: Disappointing Performance: Fruit Fly Trap Fails to Deliver Results
review: I ordered this fruit fly trap with high hopes, especially given its quick shipping and straightforward setup. The product arrived promptly and was easy to assemble – I simply poured the provided liquid into the apple-shaped trap. However, my excitement quickly turned to disappointment as the trap proved ineffective. Despite its appealing design, it failed to catch any fruit flies in my home. The lure liquid seems to be just vinegar, which doesn’t appear to attract the fruit flies as expected. A sweeter scent might have worked better. After giving it a fair try, I cannot recommend this product. It did not deliver the results I needed, and I would suggest looking for a more effective solution for your fruit fly problem.

title: apple shaped traps fall over way too easy
review: These apple shaped traps fall over way too easy spilling the bait on counters or tables attracting MORE flies. Need a more stable base.

title: It didn't work?
review: Maybe it is the type of flies that I had, whatever was infesting a new Boston Fern I just bought. This product did not work on them. Not even one fell for it. The only thing that did were sticky blue light traps. It's likely that this product would work better with your run of the mill fruit flies. The liquid that comes with these do smell like the homemade vinegar traps I have made in the past. If I get a chance to test this product on other flies and if it works, I will update my rating.

title: Does not work, find something else
review: This does not really catch any fruit flies. It’s effective for about a day before it loses whatever causes it to work

title: Waste of money
review: Did absolutely nothing, would not recommend

title: Hard Pass!
review: Not successful with my gnat problem. Used these wax melts yellow sticky spikes. Much better results.

title: Worthless
review: pretty much worthless, even in a small room

title: Cute but Ineffective and smelly!
review: I bought these to combat fruit flies, they are very cute. Poured the apple cider vinegar into the apple and I could smell it pretty distinctly. I was hoping they would work, I brought one to work, 1 upstairs and 1 in the kitchen. Each one caught maybe 1 or 2. I would go with the plugins.

title: Cider vinegar and soap works much better
review: Writing this as two fruit flies buzz furiously around my face. I've had these for a week and the issue is not gone. I've gutted my room and there is nothing that could be harboring these flying monsters. I've used apple cider vinegar and dish soap in the past with success and thought these would work better; they do not.

title: Doesn't last as long as it advertises.
review: I purchased this for my office, which is notorious for getting stupid little fruit flies. I only set up 2 of the 4 apples I received, and filled them using the first set of liquid bottles. In less than 2 weeks, I had to refill the apples again, when the trap fluid is supposed to last for 45 days. Now, a week later, the refill has already dried up again. So what was supposed to be 180 days of lure turned out to be 19 days of supply. I will say, though, that in those 19 days, the product does work. But the liquid just evaporates way too fast to be worth the money out on this.

title: Liquid evaporates
review: The liquid used to lure the fruit flies evaporates within a few weeks, doesn't really work

title: Greenway traps are better than Terro
review: Greenway traps each caught a dozen fruit flies in a couple of days. The only downside is that they don't catch other species of small bugs. (For those pour bleach down the drain.) My Terro traps caught only a few before the liquid evaporated. The Greenway bottle design keeps them from spilling, and also from evaporating. Terro traps have several big holes so they can spill, and that also allows the liquid to evaporate faster. Terro comes with refills but Greenway doesn't need them. The bugs can also get out of the Terro as easily as getting in, but the Greenway traps hold them until the fumes kill them. They can't climb out with the funnel opening for the same reason it doesn't spill.

title: Not efficient long-term
review: Mildly effective, but didn't fully get rid of the fruit flies. Just culled their numbers for a bit until they learned how to walk out.

title: Cute, convenient containers. But it's just vinegar and dishwashing detergent that didn't work alone.
review: Love the cute, convenient containers. But it's literally just vinegar and dishwashing detergent that didn't work alone, and that's what I had tried on my own without much success before buying 4 of these traps for $14. After an entire day of catching NO fruit flies with these, I looked at some YouTube videos and saw a guy who tried BALSAMIC vinegar instead of white vinegar or apple cider vinegar (which is what I had used.) I added the Balsamic vinegar to the Terro solution and left the house to run some errands. When I returned just an hour later, one of the traps already had 10 flies in it. By last night (24 hours later) there were almost 20 in one of them and 10 in another. I'm hoping that by tonight our bizarre infestation will be almost eradicated. But it's the BALSAMIC VINEGAR that I added that made it effective. I don't regret my purchase because these containers were worth the initial investment. My brother said that these used to have a pheromone in them to attract fruit flies but apparently from the reviews, they changed the formula over the past couple of years, and there was nothing in the ingredient list besides the detergent and vinegar.

title: Not very effective
review: Easy to use, but they didn’t do much to reduce the fruit flies in my kitchen. Might work for light issues, but didn’t help my situation much.

title: Haven’t really worked
review: They’re cute and I like how they look around kitchen but honestly they didn’t really work for me. I would maybe find one or two bugs using the liquid they provided. Maybe need to try something else inside.

title: Old coffee works better.
review: Well, I had high hopes for these but the coffee attracted more fruit flies than these did. 8-1

title: Use just perxiode as,the solution vs vinegar
review: Barley worked and the liquid is basically vinegar smell solution. When I put out a small little bowl of peroxide nearby it’s works so much better catching the flys than the Terro traps

title: Not effective
review: Maybe it works for someone, nit for me. 4 traps, 2 liquids. Tried 2 in the kitchen. 1 near hydroponic farm and bananas. 1 on the other side of kitchen, where I eat. Bottle equally distributed. 1st is already liquid free after a week. No catch. Other - 1 catch. And 4-5 fruit flies constantly flying around. (Provably loughing). It seems aroma is just not attractive (or they like bananas more) Turns out Zevo with violet light os more atractive. Catches gnats and flies at astonishing rate. Planning to purchase more. This thing has way to improve. Starting with evaporation rate

title: Not very effective on gnats. Bone dry in 19 days.
review: The traps caught a few gnats for a few days - then nothing. Mine are bone dry after 19 days - nowhere near the 45 days claimed. I guess the attractive containers could be used with a vinegar and dish soap mix, but the plastic tub with a 4" diameter open top I used before getting these caught more gnats. My recommendation would be to spend your money on a large bottle of apple cider vinegar and plan to refresh your bait every week.

title: We were disappointed
review: A home remedy worked better

title: For fruit flys
review: Did not works as well as plugins

title: Not very effective
review: I put these by a sink that always has fruit flies around it. They just fly all around the trap but don’t go in it. In weeks I’ve only gotten 1 fruit fly in a trap. The apple shape is cuter than fly tape though.

title: Less effective than apple cider
review: Easily outdone by a bowl of apple cider and a bit of plastic wrap. Easy to use but not very effective and I not happy about tossing plastic into the trash. I'd rather throw the bugs into the trash and reuse the plastic

title: DIY Version Just As Good
review: I’ve been using a “recipe” I found online for a few years now to get rid of fruit flies every time these darn things start popping up- a mixture of apple cider vinegar, sugar, dish soap, and water. It works AMAZINGLY every time. Seems lately however, I can’t keep up with refilling the dish, changing out the mixture for new stuff (they’re SO BAD right now!!). I was attracted to this stuff by its cute little apple container, and the fact that it claimed to last 45 days. Well, it’s been less than a week and I’ve already gone through all 4. They don’t seem to work as well as the DIY mixture I make, nor do they seem to attract as many fruit flies as when I just put the mixture in a small bowl. Should’ve known it wouldn’t work as well, but with all of the great reviews, I was hopeful! Just Google the “recipe” to make the stuff on your own. It’s a lot cheaper!

title: Don't buy this. Make your own!
review: Well, I got duped by this product. It's mostly my fault. I needed a way to get rid of fruit flies that made their way into my home. I had made my own trap with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but the vinegar was really bad and stunk up the house. I searched for fruit fly traps and came across this. I gleaned over the description and didn't bother with the reviews (two things I usually never do) and ordered it. It arrived the next day (which is why I bought it) and I opened the package. Much to my surprise and disappointment, it was just a small bottle of apple cider vinegar with soap in it. Man, I felt dumb, but I decided to try it. The cap is a joke. It makes the bottle taller when open and easier to knock over so you can spill it everywhere. Also, it leaks if you close it and don't keep it upright. I poured some into a glass pudding bowl, covered it with plastic wrap and sealed it with a rubber band around the bowl. I poked four 3/8" holes in the wrap, set it out near where the flies are and left for a few minutes. When I came back the flies were all over the bowl. Once they make their way in through the holes they're essentially trapped. You will get the same results with apple cider vinegar and dish soap with this setup (because that's all it is) and over time it'll be cheaper. Don't buy this or any other similar brands. Just make your own trap and save the $8 that I stupidly spent.

title: More still flying around than dying
review: I've used Aunt Fanny's ant spray in the past with good results. So I thought, why not try the fruit fly solution for those pesky pests? Well, here's a good reason: it doesn't work very well. Sure, I see some floating in the liquid, but there are at least ten times that are still flying all around my kitchen. Then I decided to try one that sticks to the wall with good reviews. But those fell off the wall and I will return them. So I will buy the ones I should have all along, Terro traps. They worked great and I'm embarrassed that I bothered with anything else. I just wish Terro sold the liquid which how this all began.

title: You can do better
review: I had a THICK CLOUD of fruit flies descend in my kitchen! Researching my options, I found this product & ordered a bottle. While I was desperately awaiting its arrival, however, I fell back on 2 older remedies—beer and apple cider vinegar. Maybe 1/8 of a cup of each of these were poured into separate clean cat food tins with some dish soap for viscosity, then covered with plastic wrap, and punctured with small holes. Once the product arrived, I could easily compare the attraction each liquid possessed. Beer? The winner! Apple cider vinegar? A very close second! Lagging way WAY behind is this product. Granted, it’s got a small number of snagged victims, but nothing like the other two. Save yourself some money. You also get the freebie bonus of finishing off the beer that didn’t get poured into the can!

title: Waste of money
review: Doesn’t work any better than anything else, which isn’t saying much

title: It’s a no
review: This item did not work for me. We followed the instructions and while it did catch some fruit flies, they mostly just hung around the open lid and didn’t actually go into the container. I feel like the design is a bit flawed with that because if the flys go in there is nothing trapping them and they can just fly out. It is easy to use but not very effective. I think if you poured the liquid into something that would actually catch the flys themselves it would work great but again I think the design is a bit flawed.

title: Product arrived leaking
review: Items arrived leaking, with one container's top fully off and the other half off and the plastic wrapping the two torn. The fruit flies were having a field day on my counter!

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Don’t waste your money. Good old apple cider vinegar works better. Pour 1/4c of acv into a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap and poke small holes in the plastic. It actually works better and doesn’t emit any smell like this product.

title: Aunt Fannie's - Needs improvement
review: Gnats (fruit flies) just hang around the liquid but don't attempt to get in. I suggest the company to make these containers very small with a sticky plastic inside so they can get trapped. The idea is great but the designed is terrible. I don't know what to do with it but I am probably just going to have to throw it away unless the company offers a refund.

title: Return required
review: Two of the four bottles had loose lids and leaked. Waste of my time and money. Need to return.

title: Didn't work for me
review: Didn't work well. Strong smell

title: Not safe do not buy
review: Almost impossible to remove the screen covering the liquid and tons and tons of warnings and after saying its safe around kids and pets but also keep away from everything. The smells is also to strong

title: Bad product
review: It stinks really bad and it does not work maybe one or two flies will fall into the water, but the rest of them are smart enough to just sit around the room or run away

title: Does not work, at least for me
review: This item stinks and only attracted two flys in one month of trying to get them to go or drown in this stink pot. My recommendation is that I will not get this product ever again and I suggest you do the same.

title: No me funciona!!
review: El olor es lo de menos,!, pero mis mosquitos pequeños continuaron igual de molestos y hace un mes lo tengo en mis mosquitos pequeños Cosina, soy extremadamente limpia no tengo frutas ni alimentos a la vista y aún hay pensé se desaparecerían pero no!!! Quizás mis mosquitos son especiales?!!

title: Does not work!
review: This did not catch one fly while it was sitting in my bay window for an entire week! All it did was make my whole house smell like vinegar. Does not work save your money!

title: Just buy apple cider vinegar
review: It's literally apple cider vinegar. Just put some in a jar and poke some holes in the lid

title: Don’t wast your time
review: Waste of money had it sitting out for two weeks they would go around it but not inside

title: No luck
review: It doesn't work. I have had it for 3 days and it hasn't attracted any of the bugs. The vinegar smell is horrible and permeates the whole room. It's states the it is safe around kids and pets but it's an open jar of smelly vinegar that if knocked over would spill all over. I am surprised a Raid product is so poorly manufactured.

title: Save your money - Look up DIY & make your own with ACV
review: I am sorry to say, that this is nothing more than Apple Cider Vinegar poured into a small container. It was almost $7.... Has caught maybe 2 fruit flies in about 4 days. They land on the edge, get a drink & fly away. Buy a bottle of ACV & use your own small container, if you want to try this

title: This ain't it, folks
review: I don't know what else to say other than don't waste your money. Get a bulk size of apple cider vinegar and swish some dish soap in it, because that's what this is (and you'll likely avoid an extreme pungent smell of the vinegar by choosing a strong-smelling dish soap, as this product's smell will knock your head back). There's also the matter of the size - it's overpriced for what you get and the shape (deep and narrow) seems off-putting to them. With this, yes it caught a few but I observed mostly them perching on the edges for a few moments then taking off. Just use a white/pale shallow dish/bowl with actual surface area for them to "rest" on.

title: Mid Tier - wasn’t blown away but also not terrible
review: It worked, I suppose? I still have some fruit flies buzzing around, and even in a clean, closed room with three of these, they weren’t completely effective. I really didn’t care for the fact that it was just a wide-open jar. Most products like this have a topper with holes for the flies to go through, but this was just open with nothing on top. Did it catch some of my flies? Yes, it caught a bunch. Did it solve my problem? Not completely. Did it work any better than the little red Apple product? No, and I think the product really suffers from not having a cover on it. Usually, those help to trap whatever flies have scented the bait but haven’t yet drowned. Most of them can’t fly back out once they’ve flown in. This doesn’t have that. It was a bit of a flop for me, but it’s still useful.

title: The Fruit Fly Negotiator
review: This trap has about as much success as a timeshare salesman at a bankruptcy convention. Sure, it gets their attention. Fruit flies definitely show up to the party. They buzz around it like tourists at a gift shop, checking it out, maybe taking a few selfies, but actually committing to the product? That's where things fall apart. The fatal flaw is expecting these tiny anarchists to voluntarily take a swan dive into what's essentially their own demise. Most fruit flies are apparently smarter than we give them credit for. They hover, they consider, they probably write a few Amazon reviews of their own, then buzz off to raid your banana bowl instead. Pro tip: Slap some sticky traps around the perimeter. Think of it as setting up a security perimeter for the world's most underwhelming honey trap. Without backup, this thing is basically expensive fruit fly entertainment. Does it work? Eventually. Is it efficient? About as efficient as using a fork to eat soup. Your mileage may vary, but don't expect any fruit fly apocalypse scenarios

title: Didn’t work as well as expected
review: Apple cider vinegar with dawn worked way better. I bought this hoping the smell wouldn’t be as strong but equally or more effective at getting rid of fruit flies. It was neither.

title: Works ok...
review: Not bad for the price, but didn't attract fruit flies as well as I thought it would.

title: Not very impressed
review: We work are a small retail shop. I forgot how bad apple cider vinegar smells. Also, most of the fruit flies landed on the edge of the cup, and probably 25% got caught in the fluid. However, the price was cheap, so I guess I got what I paid for.

title: Does not attract
review: I mean it was ok. It did catch a few, but only if they happen to land in it. I wouldn’t say it attracts them.

title: Not worth it
review: If you are considering purchasing these to try, I would advice don't. Basically all this is, is a jar of apple cider vinegar that has likely been sweetened. They did work pretty well, but no better than a homemade solutions of ACV with sweetener added to it. At the price of $6 and something a jar, I'll just buy the bottles of ACV and make my own solution.

title: Combo
review: Does a great job of attracting them but a lot of the gnats just don’t land. I put a yellow sticky trap (sold on Amazon in a 54 pack) inside the jar and it greatly increased the catch.

title: Is this working?
review: It does smell strongly of apple cider vinegar. I can see it attracts the fruit flies, but after 3 days I only see about 10 dead inside. The rest are still swarming around. No idea if they die from drinking the mixture or if it attracts them and a few happen to drown.

title: Work ok. Smell is bad.
review: These work but smell rancid

title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
review: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times. Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint. Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page. I bought three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent. It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!! I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper. I actually watched the flies fly from the auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper. After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER. I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear. I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article. The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. The FRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness. I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle. I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses. Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below. First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}. Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant. A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources. Follow these steps : 1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room. REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS. 2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't. 3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate. 4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven, pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates. 5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won... 6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar. It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon. I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Six Traps Set - One Fly Caught. 80 Bucks Wasted
review: What I liked: It's easy to use. What I disliked: It arrived 2 days late. It doesn't work. It's a spill hazard. It's extremely expensive considering it's vinegar, water, fruit juice and soap. I paid $80 to catch one fly. That about sums it up. We get these fruit flies every year but this year is the worst. I've had the drains cleaned and treated professionally and I'm pouring drain cleaner and fly treatment down the drains daily. I was going to buy the decoy traps that look like an apple. I've used them before and they were great. I couldn't find any in stock, except for one that had bad reviews. Then there was Aunt Fannie's. There's no special formula even though Aunt Fannie's has a patent on their formula. It's different because first, it's not a decorative decoy trap that looks like an apple or mini pumpkin. Aunt Fannie's looks like a spice bottle. When I opened the cap, I expected to see some kind of funnel mechanism on top. That's how the other traps work. The flies are attracted by the sweet formula inside. They slide down the funnel right into the solution and can't get out. Aunt Fannie's just has a wide-mouth opening that can very easily spill. I placed 4 in my kitchen, one in the dining room and one in a bathroom - where the flies congregate as the directions tell you. I watched the flies swarm around the traps and sat back waiting for them to dive in and never check out. They landed on the bottles, walked around, climbed down inside, climbed back out, walked around a little more, then swarmed around. One little fly fell in and couldn't swim. So $80, several days of waiting, then placing these open bottles of liquid all over the place, and I caught one, single fly. Just one. I was convinced to buy this product because I saw so many great reviews. It seemed like a no-brainer when I couldn't find the product I actually wanted. I've never had this happen before. I usually buy stuff with 4 stars or better and when I do, I agree with those reviews. In this case, I was completely wrong and I've wasted time and money.

title: Didnt work for my house.
review: I purchased this because I saw the reviews. BUT it did not work for my house not one fruit fly met its death with this stuff. I was thinking maybe its because the opening is the size of the packaging. Most fly traps have tiny openings so they cant get back out. I purchased the apples ones as well. Once those were opened they went right to them. Lots of dead flies in those! So I believe this is a hit or miss for anyone who purchases.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I had this near my bunny cage where i often get fruit flies. I will say I poured a little in one of those tomato looking fruit fly cups and left this open to see if there was a difference because this doesn’t not have holes, just a plain open cap, neither collected flies, even days later. I will not purchase again. Does not work.

title: Aunt Fannie’s my Arse!
review: Aunt Fannie’s Flying Punch is a joke. Three bottles out for one month while fruit flies are doing summersaults around my face taunting me as they exclaim “I’m s that all you got?” Seriously don’t buy this. It doesn’t work. Just donate the money to someone who needs it on the street.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I haven’t caught not one gnat or fly I placed it on my kitchen sink counter around my plants! I have a zevo and sticky traps that work. Every thing catching them except for the punch I even sat it in the pot of one of my plants and still didn’t catch not one gnats

title: Works terribly; less effective than DIY traps and smells terrible.
review: My high rise condo is currently having trash chute issues, so I came home from a weekend trip to a fruit fly problem. I hastily bought this, a blue light/sticky trap, and placed out a few cups with old wine and a drop of dish soap. Left all of these out for 2 full days throughout the kitchen to eliminate my new roommates. The fruit flies are all now gone, but no thanks to this product (or the light trap, while I'm at it). The 2 cups of old wine, however, successfully caught and drowned dozens of fruit flies each. The light trap managed to catch one. This product caught zero. It also reeks of vinegar, strongly enough that I notice it immediately upon entering the apartment. I highly recommending skipping this entirely and putting out old wine or juice with dish soap instead, save your money and your sense of smell.

title: Boooooo Boooooo 👎🏾
review: If I could rate this zero stars or negatives stars I would!!!! This sucks I have a fruit fly infestation I have let this out and the flies are going nowhere near it. It’s literally nothing but apple cider vinegar I coilda bought a bottle cheaper . I WANT MY MONEY BACK

title: Possibly Slipped Past Quality Control???
review: I have never been as disappointed in something from Amazon as I was with this stuff! I had seen them mention it on a TV show. Im thinking maybe GMA...but anyway....so then i checked AZ and it had a ton of positive reviews so I just knew this was going to be the answer to our fruit fly problem. In another few days it will be an entire month that these 2 bottles have sat out in our house where we see these flies the most. Believe it or not....not one single fruit fly is in the liquid of either of these! We've stood and watched them fly to the bottle, and even down in it but pretty soon they fly right back out! Finally yesterday I decided to top each one of them off with a bit more apple cider vinegar..thinking POSSIBLY it hadnt been strong enough originally. NOPE! It's still not working. But yet there are still people saying it worked great for them. So Ive finally started a return today since I feel like Ive given it a decent chance with no success.

title: Product does not deliver advertised results...
review: I am not sure where they came from (or keep coming from), but I have a small swarm of fruit flies in my kitchen that I have been trying to get rid of for several weeks. I take my trash out daily, have cleaned my kitchen from top to bottom including the drains and trash can, no longer leave fruit (or any other kind of food) out on the counter, and have moved my cat's food and water dishes to another room. I also have tried several DIY natural remedies. Yet the fruit flies persist. I do not want to use an insecticide spray in my home because I have multiple chemical sensitivities. I read about Aunt Fannie's online -- the product got good reviews, so I thought it would be worth a try. The Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! arrived and I put it out on the counter above where my kitchen trash can is and waited hopefully for it to work its magic. It has been five days and I am still waiting. In five days, Aunt Fannie's has trapped five fruit flies. In the same time period, I have swatted down 29 fruit flies and a sinkful of soapy water that I soaked a couple of pots in for an hour one day trapped seven fruit flies. I am really disappointed in this product -- it was definitely not worth the money. At this point, I am not sure what will work to rid my kitchen or fruit flies, but I feel fairly certain that it will not be Aunt Fannie's.

title: It is a hit or miss product.
review: This is a hit or miss product. It did not work for me at all. It's a cheap alternative but you risk not having the results you want. Strong vinegar smell. Wouldn't recommend.

title: Just apple cider vinegar in a cup !!
review: This is nothing more than apple cider vinegar in a cup! You can Google home fruit fly remedies, and they all suggest to put apples cider vinegar in a cup with A drop of dish soap so that the flies sink into the liquid. Once I open this product, it was clear that it is just apple Cider vinegar that you can put in a cup for less than a quarter. Yes, this is effective, but you can make yourself at home. Don’t spend six dollars on this.

title: The smell is TERRIBLE
review: I can't tell you if it works or not because the smell is awful. If you like the smell of vinegar airfreshener, then you'll be ok. The next day after opening it, I put the top back on!

title: Poor design, spills easily!
review: I was expecting more for the extra money I spent on this Raid product. Like maybe a liquid product that wouldn't spill stuff all over when I opened it. When I unscrewed the lid, Raid had one of those protective plastic coverings over the opening of the jar that you have to peel back by gripping the extra piece of attached material that's supposed to make it easier to peel, but doesn't actually WORK since it's glued on so firmly. Oh well. OK. So I grabbed a sharp knife and carved away the temporary protective covering, which exposed the jar of apple cider vinegar that is said to kill the fruit flies. For the price, I expected another lid with holes in it to prevent it from spilling when I put it down near my compost pail. But no. It was just a jar of open liquid that had already spilled once when I carved away the protective covering! So I had to place the $8.18 jar of Raid in a sealed plastic sandwich bag with holes in it. I don't know yet how well it works. But here's the issue. If I wanted to create a DIY fruit fly disposal system, I would get my own jar of apple cider vinegar and put it in a sealed sandwich bag with holes in it. AND I would have saved myself $8.18! There are other, better designed fruit fly apple cider products on Amazon that have holes in the lids to prevent spillage. I just expected more from a big brand name like Raid. Silly me.

title: Not effective
review: I bought this with the hopes of catching gnats. It only caught two. I watched the gnats just walk along the rim. I wouldn’t recommend it. I ended up doing baking soda and vinegar in my drain and that worked.

title: Not great.
review: This was not as effective as advertised. It collected a small amount of fruit flies, but it also served as an attractant that they wouldn't touch. I had it open for 2 weeks and the amount of flies only got worse. At the end of the 2 weeks there were maybe 20 in the jar, and still dozens in the air. As soon as I closed the jar, they were gone in about a day. I would not recommend this item. It also smells awful- if using it indoors, prepare for your house to smell like vinegar-soaked work socks.

title: Smell is Strong and Spreads
review: It makes your whole house smell like vinegar with a hint of sweetness. The smell is very strong and spread throughout the entire house overnight. I had to close it up and run a fan to get rid of the smell. It only caught one gnat overnight, even though there was a light trap in the same room plugged into an outlet (Zevo) that had just caught over 50 gnats in the previous 48 hours.

title: Ineffective
review: I have several apple cider vinegar/dish soap traps all around my house already. I bought this to take it up a notch because they aren't working! I had high hopes, until I opened the container. It smells just like apple cider vinegar. Very strong apple cider vinegar. I put it on the counter anyways, hoping there is some specific secret ingredient to attract and catch them. I have massive amounts of these awful annoying little bugs. 48 hours later and there are 2 in the Raid jar. I am so disappointed! Also, the liquid being completely open on my counter doesn't give me the best feeling. I feel like maybe a grid design on top or something to block spillage would be a good idea. I cannot recommend this product.

title: Fruit fly trapper
review: Draws little fruit flies. Had out on counter for a week but flies still around

title: Great start… then … sad face
review: I do not usually write reviews on products but felt compelled due to my disappointment in this. First- I have had this massive amount of fruit flies that have appeared out of nowhere. I ordered this, as I thought the reviews were great. When first opened, as other products said- wow! That is a strong odor that is not terribly welcoming. But I was thinking that I was more than willing to deal with it if it meant that I was fruit fly free. Sadly, those pesky bugs seemed to have outsmarted the trap and only a fraction of them have lost their life to this product. I somehow think (irrational and though it may be) that this product has somehow made them not only stronger but smarter. If you have a small amount of irritants, this may be helpful. But for a larger swarm, I am looking elsewhere.

title: Didn’t work at all…. Perhaps it was the bug not the product?
review: This is a long story. I bought canned cat food from Amazon, as usual I put it in the cupboard and went on with life. Fast forward, a few days later little bugs started flying around my kitchen, I thought they were fruit flies. For two days I put up with them then bought this. Basically this is apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar. You can make the recipe yourself, which I would do instead of buying this. Now, upon a week after the food was put in the cupboard I opened it and was attacked by these little bombers with wings. The gray of cat food was infested, hundreds with eggs. The can of food in the second tray which was covered with the standard cardboard and outer plastic was split which made a great environment for these little jerks. It took me a week to hand kill these things- thankfully they were slow. Perhaps they were not fruit flies and that is why this product didn’t work. This is not why I am giving it two stars. I am giving it 2 starts because of its application. Once the top is flipped open it is easy to tip over, it is not balanced. The top is completely open because the goal is for the flies to go in for a drink and drown. Well, unless you put this inside a mug it is very easy to accidentally tip over. The smell is nauseating, but that is not the fault of the product, sometime the “medicine” is just awful. I also think it is a little overpriced. $8. For ingredients that would cost at most $.75. I know it is the ease of use and when you are being overtaken by bugs you are willing to pay anything. I am giving it 3 stars because I am indifferent of its effectiveness. I am not sure if these were fruit flies- if they were, then this product didn’t work at all, if they weren’t then I am judging the other aspects of the product: ease of use, quality, cost. Etc. Quality: Nice looking label, The high pungent smell of vinegar is enough to make you gag- so, it is the real deal and not watered down. Ease of use: just peel off the thin protective film and flip open the lid- voila. Cost: I think it’s a little pricey for the ingredients which you could easily make yourself. (They give the recipe online) But, isn’t it easy to press the “buy now” button and have the delivery guy drop at your door 48 hrs later?

title: Meh
review: This stuff worked okay. Maybe some batches are better than others. I bought the two-pack and one seemed to attract a lot of gnats while the other caught very few gnats. I tried switching the placement to see if that helped but it didn’t seem to make much difference. It’s very easy to use-just open the package, flip open the lid and it’s ready to go. I’ve made a similar mixture before with comparable results so I probably won’t buy this again.

title: Maybe Not Fruit Flies
review: The product did not work for me, so I originally posted as one-star. Also, it is not eligible for return, so I was stuck with three jars. I am giving three stars now, because of the communication with Aunt Fannie's. I wrote to them hoping they could help with a return. Kelly wrote back promptly and said the return could be done only through Amazon. But, she was very friendly in e-mail and was sorry the product had not worked. She sent some questions and pictures, wondering if what I have is truly fruit flies. As it turned out and upon further research by me, what I seem to have are drain flies. I have eliminated them with baking soda/vinegar and also baking soda/essential oils. I would recommend to anyone that if FlyPunch is not working, consider another fly besides fruit flies. Also, it is worth writing to the company. I found Aunt Fannie's to be very helpful. Update 12/14/17: I have phorid flies, and they are very difficult to get rid of. My baking soda/vinegar/essential oils invention kept them at bay but didn't truly eliminate them. However, I have found a "trap" by happy accident: ruby red grapefruit juice. The little suckers are actually attracted to an open plastic glass filled with juice. It takes a while for them to figure out that they should jump right in, but they are. Does it work? Yes. Do I still have the same type of flies that I had before? Yes, yes I do. Have I tried moving it around where I see flies? Yes, I have. If I had to guess I have 6 flies/gnats, and the bottle has 3 of them. So I gave it a 3/5 rating for getting me 50% of the flies.

review: I only gave this a three because of the aroma. It does work.

title: Didn’t work at all…. Perhaps it was the bug not the product?
review: This is a long story. I bought canned cat food from Amazon, as usual I put it in the cupboard and went on with life. Fast forward, a few days later little bugs started flying around my kitchen, I thought they were fruit flies. For two days I put up with them then bought this. Basically this is apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar. You can make the recipe yourself, which I would do instead of buying this. Now, upon a week after the food was put in the cupboard I opened it and was attacked by these little bombers with wings. The gray of cat food was infested, hundreds with eggs. The can of food in the second tray which was covered with the standard cardboard and outer plastic was split which made a great environment for these little jerks. It took me a week to hand kill these things- thankfully they were slow. Perhaps they were not fruit flies and that is why this product didn’t work. This is not why I am giving it two stars. I am giving it 2 starts because of its application. Once the top is flipped open it is easy to tip over, it is not balanced. The top is completely open because the goal is for the flies to go in for a drink and drown. Well, unless you put this inside a mug it is very easy to accidentally tip over. The smell is nauseating, but that is not the fault of the product, sometime the “medicine” is just awful. I also think it is a little overpriced. $8. For ingredients that would cost at most $.75. I know it is the ease of use and when you are being overtaken by bugs you are willing to pay anything. I am giving it 3 stars because I am indifferent of its effectiveness. I am not sure if these were fruit flies- if they were, then this product didn’t work at all, if they weren’t then I am judging the other aspects of the product: ease of use, quality, cost. Etc. Quality: Nice looking label, The high pungent smell of vinegar is enough to make you gag- so, it is the real deal and not watered down. Ease of use: just peel off the thin protective film and flip open the lid- voila. Cost: I think it’s a little pricey for the ingredients which you could easily make yourself. (They give the recipe online) But, isn’t it easy to press the “buy now” button and have the delivery guy drop at your door 48 hrs later?

I’ve made a similar mixture before with comparable results so I probably won’t buy this again.
