title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
review: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times. Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint. Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page. I bought three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent. It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!! I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper. I actually watched the flies fly from the auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper. After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER. I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear. I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article. The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. The FRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness. I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle. I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses. Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below. First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}. Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant. A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources. Follow these steps : 1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room. REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS. 2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't. 3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate. 4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven, pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates. 5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won... 6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar. It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon. I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Six Traps Set - One Fly Caught. 80 Bucks Wasted
review: What I liked: It's easy to use. What I disliked: It arrived 2 days late. It doesn't work. It's a spill hazard. It's extremely expensive considering it's vinegar, water, fruit juice and soap. I paid $80 to catch one fly. That about sums it up. We get these fruit flies every year but this year is the worst. I've had the drains cleaned and treated professionally and I'm pouring drain cleaner and fly treatment down the drains daily. I was going to buy the decoy traps that look like an apple. I've used them before and they were great. I couldn't find any in stock, except for one that had bad reviews. Then there was Aunt Fannie's. There's no special formula even though Aunt Fannie's has a patent on their formula. It's different because first, it's not a decorative decoy trap that looks like an apple or mini pumpkin. Aunt Fannie's looks like a spice bottle. When I opened the cap, I expected to see some kind of funnel mechanism on top. That's how the other traps work. The flies are attracted by the sweet formula inside. They slide down the funnel right into the solution and can't get out. Aunt Fannie's just has a wide-mouth opening that can very easily spill. I placed 4 in my kitchen, one in the dining room and one in a bathroom - where the flies congregate as the directions tell you. I watched the flies swarm around the traps and sat back waiting for them to dive in and never check out. They landed on the bottles, walked around, climbed down inside, climbed back out, walked around a little more, then swarmed around. One little fly fell in and couldn't swim. So $80, several days of waiting, then placing these open bottles of liquid all over the place, and I caught one, single fly. Just one. I was convinced to buy this product because I saw so many great reviews. It seemed like a no-brainer when I couldn't find the product I actually wanted. I've never had this happen before. I usually buy stuff with 4 stars or better and when I do, I agree with those reviews. In this case, I was completely wrong and I've wasted time and money.

title: Didnt work for my house.
review: I purchased this because I saw the reviews. BUT it did not work for my house not one fruit fly met its death with this stuff. I was thinking maybe its because the opening is the size of the packaging. Most fly traps have tiny openings so they cant get back out. I purchased the apples ones as well. Once those were opened they went right to them. Lots of dead flies in those! So I believe this is a hit or miss for anyone who purchases.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I had this near my bunny cage where i often get fruit flies. I will say I poured a little in one of those tomato looking fruit fly cups and left this open to see if there was a difference because this doesn’t not have holes, just a plain open cap, neither collected flies, even days later. I will not purchase again. Does not work.

title: Aunt Fannie’s my Arse!
review: Aunt Fannie’s Flying Punch is a joke. Three bottles out for one month while fruit flies are doing summersaults around my face taunting me as they exclaim “I’m s that all you got?” Seriously don’t buy this. It doesn’t work. Just donate the money to someone who needs it on the street.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I haven’t caught not one gnat or fly I placed it on my kitchen sink counter around my plants! I have a zevo and sticky traps that work. Every thing catching them except for the punch I even sat it in the pot of one of my plants and still didn’t catch not one gnats

title: Works terribly; less effective than DIY traps and smells terrible.
review: My high rise condo is currently having trash chute issues, so I came home from a weekend trip to a fruit fly problem. I hastily bought this, a blue light/sticky trap, and placed out a few cups with old wine and a drop of dish soap. Left all of these out for 2 full days throughout the kitchen to eliminate my new roommates. The fruit flies are all now gone, but no thanks to this product (or the light trap, while I'm at it). The 2 cups of old wine, however, successfully caught and drowned dozens of fruit flies each. The light trap managed to catch one. This product caught zero. It also reeks of vinegar, strongly enough that I notice it immediately upon entering the apartment. I highly recommending skipping this entirely and putting out old wine or juice with dish soap instead, save your money and your sense of smell.

title: Boooooo Boooooo 👎🏾
review: If I could rate this zero stars or negatives stars I would!!!! This sucks I have a fruit fly infestation I have let this out and the flies are going nowhere near it. It’s literally nothing but apple cider vinegar I coilda bought a bottle cheaper . I WANT MY MONEY BACK

title: Possibly Slipped Past Quality Control???
review: I have never been as disappointed in something from Amazon as I was with this stuff! I had seen them mention it on a TV show. Im thinking maybe GMA...but anyway....so then i checked AZ and it had a ton of positive reviews so I just knew this was going to be the answer to our fruit fly problem. In another few days it will be an entire month that these 2 bottles have sat out in our house where we see these flies the most. Believe it or not....not one single fruit fly is in the liquid of either of these! We've stood and watched them fly to the bottle, and even down in it but pretty soon they fly right back out! Finally yesterday I decided to top each one of them off with a bit more apple cider vinegar..thinking POSSIBLY it hadnt been strong enough originally. NOPE! It's still not working. But yet there are still people saying it worked great for them. So Ive finally started a return today since I feel like Ive given it a decent chance with no success.

title: Product does not deliver advertised results...
review: I am not sure where they came from (or keep coming from), but I have a small swarm of fruit flies in my kitchen that I have been trying to get rid of for several weeks. I take my trash out daily, have cleaned my kitchen from top to bottom including the drains and trash can, no longer leave fruit (or any other kind of food) out on the counter, and have moved my cat's food and water dishes to another room. I also have tried several DIY natural remedies. Yet the fruit flies persist. I do not want to use an insecticide spray in my home because I have multiple chemical sensitivities. I read about Aunt Fannie's online -- the product got good reviews, so I thought it would be worth a try. The Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! arrived and I put it out on the counter above where my kitchen trash can is and waited hopefully for it to work its magic. It has been five days and I am still waiting. In five days, Aunt Fannie's has trapped five fruit flies. In the same time period, I have swatted down 29 fruit flies and a sinkful of soapy water that I soaked a couple of pots in for an hour one day trapped seven fruit flies. I am really disappointed in this product -- it was definitely not worth the money. At this point, I am not sure what will work to rid my kitchen or fruit flies, but I feel fairly certain that it will not be Aunt Fannie's.

title: Don't buy this. Make your own!
review: Well, I got duped by this product. It's mostly my fault. I needed a way to get rid of fruit flies that made their way into my home. I had made my own trap with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but the vinegar was really bad and stunk up the house. I searched for fruit fly traps and came across this. I gleaned over the description and didn't bother with the reviews (two things I usually never do) and ordered it. It arrived the next day (which is why I bought it) and I opened the package. Much to my surprise and disappointment, it was just a small bottle of apple cider vinegar with soap in it. Man, I felt dumb, but I decided to try it. The cap is a joke. It makes the bottle taller when open and easier to knock over so you can spill it everywhere. Also, it leaks if you close it and don't keep it upright. I poured some into a glass pudding bowl, covered it with plastic wrap and sealed it with a rubber band around the bowl. I poked four 3/8" holes in the wrap, set it out near where the flies are and left for a few minutes. When I came back the flies were all over the bowl. Once they make their way in through the holes they're essentially trapped. You will get the same results with apple cider vinegar and dish soap with this setup (because that's all it is) and over time it'll be cheaper. Don't buy this or any other similar brands. Just make your own trap and save the $8 that I stupidly spent.

title: More still flying around than dying
review: I've used Aunt Fanny's ant spray in the past with good results. So I thought, why not try the fruit fly solution for those pesky pests? Well, here's a good reason: it doesn't work very well. Sure, I see some floating in the liquid, but there are at least ten times that are still flying all around my kitchen. Then I decided to try one that sticks to the wall with good reviews. But those fell off the wall and I will return them. So I will buy the ones I should have all along, Terro traps. They worked great and I'm embarrassed that I bothered with anything else. I just wish Terro sold the liquid which how this all began.

title: You can do better
review: I had a THICK CLOUD of fruit flies descend in my kitchen! Researching my options, I found this product & ordered a bottle. While I was desperately awaiting its arrival, however, I fell back on 2 older remedies—beer and apple cider vinegar. Maybe 1/8 of a cup of each of these were poured into separate clean cat food tins with some dish soap for viscosity, then covered with plastic wrap, and punctured with small holes. Once the product arrived, I could easily compare the attraction each liquid possessed. Beer? The winner! Apple cider vinegar? A very close second! Lagging way WAY behind is this product. Granted, it’s got a small number of snagged victims, but nothing like the other two. Save yourself some money. You also get the freebie bonus of finishing off the beer that didn’t get poured into the can!

title: Waste of money

title: It’s a no
review: This item did not work for me. We followed the instructions and while it did catch some fruit flies, they mostly just hung around the open lid and didn’t actually go into the container. I feel like the design is a bit flawed with that because if the flys go in there is nothing trapping them and they can just fly out. It is easy to use but not very effective. I think if you poured the liquid into something that would actually catch the flys themselves it would work great but again I think the design is a bit flawed.

title: Product arrived leaking
review: Items arrived leaking, with one container's top fully off and the other half off and the plastic wrapping the two torn. The fruit flies were having a field day on my counter!

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Don’t waste your money. Good old apple cider vinegar works better. Pour 1/4c of acv into a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap and poke small holes in the plastic. It actually works better and doesn’t emit any smell like this product.

title: Aunt Fannie's - Needs improvement
review: Gnats (fruit flies) just hang around the liquid but don't attempt to get in. I suggest the company to make these containers very small with a sticky plastic inside so they can get trapped. The idea is great but the designed is terrible. I don't know what to do with it but I am probably just going to have to throw it away unless the company offers a refund.

title: Return required
review: Two of the four bottles had loose lids and leaked. Waste of my time and money. Need to return.

title: Didn't work for me
review: Didn't work well. Strong smell

title: Save your money - cheap wine and suds are far better
review: I wanted to like the ease of use and disposability of this product, but it simply did not work and in my experience, was poorly designed. Like most fruit fly-killing concoctions, it had vinegar and dish soap. But judging by the scent, that was about it. No sweetness I could detect (admittedly I don’t know what they are attracted to precisely).Judging by the way they swarmed fruit juice or wine, that seems like a requirement. Also, while the slim container is convenient, a short open glass provided significantly more surface area, which presumably made it easier for them to land. Bottom line, the side by side trial I ran with a glass of red wine, white wine and this product. No comparison. Wines in a landslide of fly carcasses.

title: Paying for packaging
review: This product does work, sort of, for attracting fruit flies. However for the price, you can do just as well to buy the little red plastic apple baits at the grocery. Even better, just use cider vinegar in a trap, because that's basically what this is. I use it as an attractant for a heavy duty fly stick, but red wine or cider vinegar work just as well. I didn't actually catch a whole lot of flies in the little jars.

title: Don't buy
review: Not as powerful as making home remedy

title: Kills, yes...but also attracts.
review: This has been a particularly bad year for fruit flies and gnats down South, and so I needed a little extra help. I love Aunt Fannie's household products, but this one is not one that I will purchase again. The solution inside these containers do kill the pests, but it also attracts them. For every 10 little darlings floating in the bottle, there are 20 more buzzing and crawling around the container, which defeats the purpose. Also, the open container design emits a very strong vinegar odor throughout the house...which I suppose is better than a chemical smell, but it still is unpleasant. The open container design also invites spillage is accidentally knocked over, which is easy to do when participating in food prep.

title: Hoped it eiuldveo
review: I wanted this product to work on my influx of tiny flying insects. Called fruit flies. We found them moving up & reproducing. This product didn't work well for us. Thank you!. I so wanted to be successful . I wanted to it to make iyy outdoor

title: So far, the flies are not going for it.
review: The products was supposed to attract the flies and kill them, right? Well the flies are still buzzing around happily. If however, the product was meant to be Birth control for flies, its efficacy remains to be seen I suppose.

title: What a mess
review: I can’t speak to how well this works but I can tell you almost everyone of the 6 I bought leaked. I could smell vinegar before I opened the box, when I got into it the box was wet as were each of the jars. Every lid was loose and even with an inner seal they had all leaked. What a mess, had to clean them up before even trying to use them. I can’t imagine ordering any more.

title: I'm beginning to think it's attracting more bugs, rather than eliminating them.
review: I bought two, and when I open the lid, I get lots of little fruit flies around the jars -- and most especially on the lid rather than inside the jars. It seems to attract more fruit flies than I saw initially. I tend to wonder if flies from elsewhere (outside?) are finding their way inside to get to these little jars. I have cleaned and cleaned, and I can't seem to find a source of these little bugs. I have no fruit sitting out, or any other exposed food. I'm wondering if they're coming from the kitchen drain, so I bought some stuff to pour down the drain that's supposed to work for killing a variety of flies, but it hasn't arrived yet. So the fight continues... sooner or later, I'll rid myself of these little buggers.

title: We had high hopes this would be the answer
review: Our office goes through periods where we seem to be deviled by very small flying insects, they could be gnats or fruit flies, we don't know for sure but this product has the ingredients that are recommended to work on either. We have never found a dead insect in the bottles and we still had the problem on going. We didn't have that many but they were persistent and annoying. We are in a lull currently and I'd love to say it was this product but neither of the two bottles I bought have shown any dead in them so so far, we'd have to say they didn't work for us.

title: Didn't Work
review: This product didn't work as advertised. I had ordered another similar item and also used a "homemade" solution of apple cider vinegar and a couple of drops of dish soap. The other approaches worked well, trapping several dozen fruit flies/vinegar flies. This only trapped three.

title: I'm Not Sure Why There's a Lid
review: The lid seems to just be there for cosmetic effect. It closes, it seems secure, but you can still smell the vinegar coming through. Turn the bottle upside down, and it leaks out pretty heavily. I discovered this flaw after my cat knocked the bottle over and, closed lid and all, about 1/4th of the fluid leaked out everywhere. I'm sure it works well as a product, but a product you can't secure and will you can smell through the lid isn't great. I don't know if it's jut my lid that's the problem, but the packaging seemed to have quite a few flaws.

title: Changed the formula?
review: The first time I ever used this product it worked great! So I decided to order it again, and now it lo longer works. It hasn’t caught one fly at all! Not at home nor at work. Disappointed. And it evaporates way quicker than the original!

title: Maybe I have mutant fruitflys
review: Although generous amount of liquid and super simple to set up, it just isn't doing the job. These are definitely fruitflies & this product isn't working well. After setting next to kitchen sink there's about 10 dead ff in the container, but at least 50 still flying around. Last year when I had fruit flies I microwaved to warm up a bit of apple juice & set that out & the ff loved it, but wanted something easy so tried this Aunt Fannies. I believe the liquid is basically vinegar with some sort of dish soap in it. I can't recommend this product to others.

title: Above and beyond...
review: ...and around, JUST NOT INSIDE!! Ha! It definitely attracts fruit flies but they just refuse to fly into the stuff. I did better with cider vinegar and soap.

title: Didn't work
review: I hoped that this product would help, but the fruit flies were not even attracted to it. The smell is horrible. It's vinegar. But I wish I could say it worked. But it didn't. I have more luck with the sticky flower pads, they work wonders and catch many fruit flies.

title: Did not work
review: Ok, so I was so hopeful when I saw the reviews for this. We had a fruit fly infestation for a few days, i managed to get it mostly under control (thanks to my dyson and quick reflexes) with just some lingering fruit flies. I would see maybe 3-5 at a time. I put out this solution as directions stated for 5 days… not ONE fly succumbed to this. Very disappointing. Continuing to hunt these things with my dyson, down to about 1-2 a day now. Wish me luck! And don’t waste your money on this

title: Save your money make your own for about 2 CENTS
review: Apple cider vinegar & a few drops of dish soap is cheaper and exactly the same as this. The active ingredients are malic acid and laureth sulfate. I did a direct comparison a few drops of dish soap in apple cider vinegar gently stir about 2 seconds same smell, consistency and performance. It is effective at reducing the number of fruit flies, but will never eliminate them completely without removing garbage and cleaning the area. But do not buy, make your own for about 2 cents and a spare jar or bowl

title: Vinegar in a bottle
review: I didn’t realize when I bought this that it was basically vinegar in a plastic bottle. I had been using the plastic apples with apple cider vinegar in it and it was catching the fruit flies but I was looking for something different, something better. I saw this and thought that I’d try it but it was pretty much the same as what I already had been using. It hasn’t caught any fruit flies and it’s been a few days. I’m afraid that the plastic bottle will topple over and spill vinegar so I put it in the window sill. I hope it works for others, it just hasn’t worked for me.

title: Worthless
review: Does not work. Useless

title: Somewhat worked
review: I'd say there were about 40 or 50 fruit flies trapped in it but that's about it and I had about 100 fruit flies it did somewhat work but but only enough to make a slight impact on my fruit fly infestation.

title: Just apple cider vinegar
review: We had made our own fruit fly traps (apple cider vinegar with a few drops of dish soap) but read about these so decided to try them. When we received, I realized they are…apple cider vinegar with a few drops of dish soap. And, our homemade version has caught more fruit flies, are much cheaper, and these are more precarious and easier to accidentally knock over than if you build your own in a mug. Don’t bother.

title: Does it get worse before it gets better?
review: Could this be a “it gets worse before it gets better” situation? I bought the trap because I noticed only a few flies (maybe 5) around my kitchen I’ve only had the trap out for 24 hours now but I’ve noticed MORE fruit flies than before as if it’s attracting more flies with its smell. There are maybe 10 fruit flies in the trap but at least 10 more flies flying in places around the trap. I’ll try keeping it up a while longer to see if there is improvement but otherwise I might have to throw it away and try something else.

title: Didn't work
review: Basically the same as using a home vinegar mix except this worked less than a home mix. We had an infestation of fruit flies and gnats for a short period of time and even with using 2 of these in different locations of the house, we only caught 3 in a week long period. Caught more using home made mix which was much cheaper and a bug zapper.

title: Doesn't work
review: Its not working and fruit fly still around

title: Kinda worked mostly didnt
review: I did not care for the ACV all the time. Also with the completely open lid it was not very accident friendly or capable of keeping a bug in unless it was fully covered in ACV.

title: Works decently, but homemade remedies are just as good
review: This product is okay. It definitely attracted fruit flies but a homemade container of red wine vinegar and dish soap did the exact same level of job. I still have a fruit fly problem and it seems to have multiplied.

title: Gnats galore!
review: Didn't have any fruit so I guess they came up the drain. Too slow to work and too few dead. I can do the same with just apple cider vinegar

title: Didn't catch anything!
review: Basically, it did nothing but stink up the kitchen. I placed it in the kitchen where flies zooming around. In a week the flies were still airborne and not a single fly in the jar. I think it's design is poor. Just a tall and narrow jar, it is easy to tip over, and unlike similar products the top is nothing but an open jar. Other products to kill fruit flies I have used are lower and wider making them more stable and have several small holes in top so if it does tip it isn't a complete loss.

title: Fruit fly traps
review: I don’t think it was worth the money or even works at all. I have had it out all night and all day today and only see 2 fruit flies in there. Not worth the money

title: After the first week, fruit flies stop getting trapped - maybe the scent wears off?
review: After the first week of using these fruit fly traps, fruit flies stop getting trapped - maybe the scent wears off? I wasn't impressed with these.

title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
review: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times. Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint. Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page. I bought three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent. It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!! I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper. I actually watched the flies fly from the auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper. After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER. I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear. I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article. The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. The FRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness. I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle. I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses. Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below. First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}. Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant. A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources. Follow these steps : 1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room. REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS. 2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't. 3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate. 4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven, pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates. 5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won... 6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar. It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon. I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! As much as I love tasty vine ripened tomatoes and other summer fruit and vegetables, it's just not worth it. I think the high temperatures in July throughout the North East as well as nationaly/globally contributed to the problem experienced by me and almost everyone I know.

title: Six Traps Set - One Fly Caught. 80 Bucks Wasted
review: What I liked: It's easy to use. What I disliked: It arrived 2 days late. It doesn't work. It's a spill hazard. It's extremely expensive considering it's vinegar, water, fruit juice and soap. I paid $80 to catch one fly. That about sums it up. We get these fruit flies every year but this year is the worst. I've had the drains cleaned and treated professionally and I'm pouring drain cleaner and fly treatment down the drains daily. I was going to buy the decoy traps that look like an apple. I've used them before and they were great. I couldn't find any in stock, except for one that had bad reviews. Then there was Aunt Fannie's. There's no special formula even though Aunt Fannie's has a patent on their formula. It's different because first, it's not a decorative decoy trap that looks like an apple or mini pumpkin. Aunt Fannie's looks like a spice bottle. When I opened the cap, I expected to see some kind of funnel mechanism on top. That's how the other traps work. The flies are attracted by the sweet formula inside. They slide down the funnel right into the solution and can't get out. Aunt Fannie's just has a wide-mouth opening that can very easily spill. I placed 4 in my kitchen, one in the dining room and one in a bathroom - where the flies congregate as the directions tell you. I watched the flies swarm around the traps and sat back waiting for them to dive in and never check out. They landed on the bottles, walked around, climbed down inside, climbed back out, walked around a little more, then swarmed around. One little fly fell in and couldn't swim. So $80, several days of waiting, then placing these open bottles of liquid all over the place, and I caught one, single fly. Just one. I was convinced to buy this product because I saw so many great reviews. It seemed like a no-brainer when I couldn't find the product I actually wanted. I've never had this happen before. I usually buy stuff with 4 stars or better and when I do, I agree with those reviews. In this case, I was completely wrong and I've wasted time and money.

title: Didnt work for my house.
review: I purchased this because I saw the reviews. BUT it did not work for my house not one fruit fly met its death with this stuff. I was thinking maybe its because the opening is the size of the packaging. Most fly traps have tiny openings so they cant get back out. I purchased the apples ones as well. Once those were opened they went right to them. Lots of dead flies in those! So I believe this is a hit or miss for anyone who purchases.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I had this near my bunny cage where i often get fruit flies. I will say I poured a little in one of those tomato looking fruit fly cups and left this open to see if there was a difference because this doesn’t not have holes, just a plain open cap, neither collected flies, even days later. I will not purchase again. Does not work.

title: Aunt Fannie’s my Arse!
review: Aunt Fannie’s Flying Punch is a joke. Three bottles out for one month while fruit flies are doing summersaults around my face taunting me as they exclaim “I’m s that all you got?” Seriously don’t buy this. It doesn’t work. Just donate the money to someone who needs it on the street.

title: Didn’t work for me
review: I haven’t caught not one gnat or fly I placed it on my kitchen sink counter around my plants! I have a zevo and sticky traps that work. Every thing catching them except for the punch I even sat it in the pot of one of my plants and still didn’t catch not one gnats

title: Works terribly; less effective than DIY traps and smells terrible.
review: My high rise condo is currently having trash chute issues, so I came home from a weekend trip to a fruit fly problem. I hastily bought this, a blue light/sticky trap, and placed out a few cups with old wine and a drop of dish soap. Left all of these out for 2 full days throughout the kitchen to eliminate my new roommates. The fruit flies are all now gone, but no thanks to this product (or the light trap, while I'm at it). The 2 cups of old wine, however, successfully caught and drowned dozens of fruit flies each. The light trap managed to catch one. This product caught zero. It also reeks of vinegar, strongly enough that I notice it immediately upon entering the apartment. I highly recommending skipping this entirely and putting out old wine or juice with dish soap instead, save your money and your sense of smell.

title: Boooooo Boooooo 👎🏾
review: If I could rate this zero stars or negatives stars I would!!!! This sucks I have a fruit fly infestation I have let this out and the flies are going nowhere near it. It’s literally nothing but apple cider vinegar I coilda bought a bottle cheaper . I WANT MY MONEY BACK

title: Possibly Slipped Past Quality Control???
review: I have never been as disappointed in something from Amazon as I was with this stuff! I had seen them mention it on a TV show. Im thinking maybe GMA...but anyway....so then i checked AZ and it had a ton of positive reviews so I just knew this was going to be the answer to our fruit fly problem. In another few days it will be an entire month that these 2 bottles have sat out in our house where we see these flies the most. Believe it or not....not one single fruit fly is in the liquid of either of these! We've stood and watched them fly to the bottle, and even down in it but pretty soon they fly right back out! Finally yesterday I decided to top each one of them off with a bit more apple cider vinegar..thinking POSSIBLY it hadnt been strong enough originally. NOPE! It's still not working. But yet there are still people saying it worked great for them. So Ive finally started a return today since I feel like Ive given it a decent chance with no success.

title: Product does not deliver advertised results...
review: I am not sure where they came from (or keep coming from), but I have a small swarm of fruit flies in my kitchen that I have been trying to get rid of for several weeks. I take my trash out daily, have cleaned my kitchen from top to bottom including the drains and trash can, no longer leave fruit (or any other kind of food) out on the counter, and have moved my cat's food and water dishes to another room. I also have tried several DIY natural remedies. Yet the fruit flies persist. I do not want to use an insecticide spray in my home because I have multiple chemical sensitivities. I read about Aunt Fannie's online -- the product got good reviews, so I thought it would be worth a try. The Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! arrived and I put it out on the counter above where my kitchen trash can is and waited hopefully for it to work its magic. It has been five days and I am still waiting. In five days, Aunt Fannie's has trapped five fruit flies. In the same time period, I have swatted down 29 fruit flies and a sinkful of soapy water that I soaked a couple of pots in for an hour one day trapped seven fruit flies. I am really disappointed in this product -- it was definitely not worth the money. At this point, I am not sure what will work to rid my kitchen or fruit flies, but I feel fairly certain that it will not be Aunt Fannie's.

title: 2 stars because it *does* (sort of) work
review: Otherwise 1. Guys. This overpriced apple cider vinegar with a drip of dish soap. The DIY way works way better. Get a clear up, put a few drops of dish soap in it. Pour in apple cider vinegar so that there is a light "soap lining" over the top. Then cover the glass with well stretched cling wrap. Use a fork to poke s few small holes (easy to get on, hard for them to get out which is a big thing this product misses). The fruit flies smell it and crawl into the holes, ho toward the food-smell and get stuck from the layer of soap. They can't crawl out because of the plastic wrap. Bingo. $1 worth of supplies

title: Easy, it just did NOT work
review: Fruit flies were not attracted to it. Easy to use, just remove the lid. The scent is fine, not even detectable, it is a great concept but the t e r r o apple shaped fruit fly traps work 100x better. I actually even used both in my home at the same time and this container was knocked over (This is easy to knock over & waste ALL) and hardly had any caught fruit flies in it when the t e r r o apples had caught as many flies as they could catch, so the one minute it takes to squeeze the liquid into the little apples is definitely worth it even though this natural product just requires a person to remove a lid. Would not buy again, and I hate that because this product is reasonably priced and easy to use. It just didn't work.

title: But I've got to say I'm pretty disappointed this time
review: I purchased Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch last summer due to an extreme amount of gnats and flies in our home. I felt the product worked extremely well and I knew I was going to buy it again a year later. A year later came, and i purchased 5 of them, one for each room that the gnats usually show up in. I received the 5 and not a single one of them I can get open due to the cap not coming off. I have to take a small flat head screwdriver and pry the cap off and then I'm able to get it off. When I finally get it off it also rips part of the seal off as well, so it makes a mess getting the liquid inside all over. I'm not sure if this was a production error or it's a problem with the new design of the product. But I've got to say I'm pretty disappointed this time.

title: These absolutely do not work!
review: I bought these because the description on the web site really seemed promising. I put them where we get these damn fruit flys. Bathroom sink, a few areas in the kitchen. The pictures above aren’t good, but there are only 2 out 3 flies in that bottle after over a week. Same with ALL of the bottles I placed. Please- don’t waste your time or money. NOT WORTH IT!!!

title: Lot Of Money for Apple Cider Vinegar
review: Not very effective. Caught some fruit flies but caught way more with homemade traps.

title: Worked after tweak
review: The positive is that I really like the bottle that it comes in. The negative is that it is just, in my opinion, diluted apple cider vinegar. This does not work! I did buy a three pack, and added a few drops of Dawn dishwashing liquid into each bottle and then it worked like crazy! I did have to tweak it in order to get it to work. The first 24 hours, before I added the Don dishwashing liquid, it did nothing

title: Does not work
review: We just recently went on a vacation. Before we left one of our kids left a peach on the counter that rotted. When we got home we were super infested with fruit flys. So I bought this product to help get rid is of them. After 3 days it had caught just 4 fruit flies out of thousands of them.

title: WASTE OF MONEY
review: Purchasing this product was a waste of money. First of all, the package was insecurely packaged. One bottle was empty when l opened the package. The liquid leaked all over the place. Secondly, the product caught very few gnats. I would have been better off just buying fly stickers or using apple cider vinegar and dish lotion.

title: Jar of flies
review: My house has become infested with these stupid little fruit flies/drain flies/gnats whatever you want to call them. I have tried the homemade DIY traps and they catch some but not enough. This started out pretty good. I think my apple cider vinegar and dish soap attracted them more though. After having it out for a few weeks I finally just threw it away. I’m putting a pic of how many it caught. But keep in mind I still have them everywhere. And I stopped buying fresh fruit a couple months ago to try to help the situation(which it did improve but I miss fruit). Overall I would buy it again but there has to be a better way, a permanent way, to get rid of these things!!! Every time I purchase something online, I always check the reviews. I count on others to help me choose the best option. My reviews are always my honest opinion and I try to include photos if possible. If my review has helped you, please click the "helpful" button below, and if you have any questions feel free to ask! Thank you!

title: Didnt work for me, sadly
review: Bad fruit fly problem this summer. Got these amongst other products because I was desperate. Sad to say it didn't work. The flies would hover around it but never actually went in. If anything, I think they took a drink then flew away. Homemade apple cider vinegar traps worked better. It did arrive in a timely manner, however.

title: Don't buy this. Make your own!
review: Well, I got duped by this product. It's mostly my fault. I needed a way to get rid of fruit flies that made their way into my home. I had made my own trap with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but the vinegar was really bad and stunk up the house. I searched for fruit fly traps and came across this. I gleaned over the description and didn't bother with the reviews (two things I usually never do) and ordered it. It arrived the next day (which is why I bought it) and I opened the package. Much to my surprise and disappointment, it was just a small bottle of apple cider vinegar with soap in it. Man, I felt dumb, but I decided to try it. The cap is a joke. It makes the bottle taller when open and easier to knock over so you can spill it everywhere. Also, it leaks if you close it and don't keep it upright. I poured some into a glass pudding bowl, covered it with plastic wrap and sealed it with a rubber band around the bowl. I poked four 3/8" holes in the wrap, set it out near where the flies are and left for a few minutes. When I came back the flies were all over the bowl. Once they make their way in through the holes they're essentially trapped. You will get the same results with apple cider vinegar and dish soap with this setup (because that's all it is) and over time it'll be cheaper. Don't buy this or any other similar brands. Just make your own trap and save the $8 that I stupidly spent.

title: More still flying around than dying
review: I've used Aunt Fanny's ant spray in the past with good results. So I thought, why not try the fruit fly solution for those pesky pests? Well, here's a good reason: it doesn't work very well. Sure, I see some floating in the liquid, but there are at least ten times that are still flying all around my kitchen. Then I decided to try one that sticks to the wall with good reviews. But those fell off the wall and I will return them. So I will buy the ones I should have all along, Terro traps. They worked great and I'm embarrassed that I bothered with anything else. I just wish Terro sold the liquid which how this all began.

title: You can do better
review: I had a THICK CLOUD of fruit flies descend in my kitchen! Researching my options, I found this product & ordered a bottle. While I was desperately awaiting its arrival, however, I fell back on 2 older remedies—beer and apple cider vinegar. Maybe 1/8 of a cup of each of these were poured into separate clean cat food tins with some dish soap for viscosity, then covered with plastic wrap, and punctured with small holes. Once the product arrived, I could easily compare the attraction each liquid possessed. Beer? The winner! Apple cider vinegar? A very close second! Lagging way WAY behind is this product. Granted, it’s got a small number of snagged victims, but nothing like the other two. Save yourself some money. You also get the freebie bonus of finishing off the beer that didn’t get poured into the can!

title: Waste of money
review: Doesn’t work any better than anything else, which isn’t saying much

title: It’s a no
review: This item did not work for me. We followed the instructions and while it did catch some fruit flies, they mostly just hung around the open lid and didn’t actually go into the container. I feel like the design is a bit flawed with that because if the flys go in there is nothing trapping them and they can just fly out. It is easy to use but not very effective. I think if you poured the liquid into something that would actually catch the flys themselves it would work great but again I think the design is a bit flawed.

title: Product arrived leaking
review: Items arrived leaking, with one container's top fully off and the other half off and the plastic wrapping the two torn. The fruit flies were having a field day on my counter!

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Don’t waste your money. Good old apple cider vinegar works better. Pour 1/4c of acv into a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap and poke small holes in the plastic. It actually works better and doesn’t emit any smell like this product.

title: Aunt Fannie's - Needs improvement
review: Gnats (fruit flies) just hang around the liquid but don't attempt to get in. I suggest the company to make these containers very small with a sticky plastic inside so they can get trapped. The idea is great but the designed is terrible. I don't know what to do with it but I am probably just going to have to throw it away unless the company offers a refund.

title: Return required
review: Two of the four bottles had loose lids and leaked. Waste of my time and money. Need to return.

title: Didn't work for me
review: Didn't work well. Strong smell

title: Not worth the $
review: Dried up and didn’t catch any gnats.

title: FRUIT FLY TRAP
review: DIDN'T WORK VERY WELL

title: There's better options out there.
review: I had such a bad gnats problem in the house and I was recommended these. As much as I wanted them to work, they barely did anything. I ended up investing is some Zevo lights and those work wonders. No more gnats or flies for that matter.

title: Not Effective
review: Didn’t work for me. I think I have even more bugs than before! I think the produce inside may work but the opening is narrow. I’m in Texas where these bugs are everywhere so it’s disappointing it didn’t work.

title: Didn't work for me
review: I had gnat-sized fruit flies in the kitchen, then noticed they would trawl around the house- bumbling just above the side tables in the living room, then I'd see them in the windows too. I thought I'd try Aunt Fannie's Flypunch (the vinegar scent smells CLEAN to me); it did attract them, but I watched them- this one-of-many species of fruit fly was smart enough to land on the sides of the jar inside, take a few steps to drink the liquid, then back up and fly out. When the jar was empty, there was a grand total of TWO flies in the bottom. I had high hopes, but no luck... My hubby had better luck with the little butterfly-shaped sticky stakes. He hung one a few inches under the shade on the side table lamp, and cut a slit in the lid of an old plastic margarine dish to slide another one into. Later, his little stakes had 40+ on each one. Of course right now we have no kids or pets around to spread the sticky all over, but the contest is done. 😄

title: Great product but they shorted me a bottle.,
review: This product works. I have ordered it before. But this time, even though the product is sold as a set, they only sent me one bottle.

title: You can easily make this yourself..
review: Vinegar with a squirt of dish soap in a small bowl works just as well. We did a side-by-side test. Use this only if you don’t have any vinegar and dish soap.

title: Sorry, doesn’t work
review: Didn’t really work, was trying to find way to refill Taro containers for fruit flies but all this did was make kitchen smell of vinegar.

title: Overall Not Great
review: The product attracted a few drain flys put didn't reduce their life cycle as advertised. It has the same vinegar smell that attracts the pests and a few will go in. Not worth the money. Won't buy again.

title: Barely works, stick with vinegar and plastic wrap
review: Apple cider vinegar in a small glass, Saran Wrap over the top, rubber band keeping the wrap on the glass. Wrap taut like a drum, poke three holes about 3mm long; long enough for the little so-and-so’s to crawl in. They can’t crawl out, and will eventually pass out and drown. Two or three of these glasses around the kitchen took care of everything. This product, by comparison, smelled worse and grabbed maybe 1/10th the amount of each wrapped glass.

title: Productive evaluation
review: I looked at all the DIY suggestions on how to get rid of my fruit flies that seem to be multiplying exponentially. None of them really worked well and so I bought this product. Frankly, for me it didn't work any better than what I had tried and the formula seems to be relatively the same as the DIY

title: Works, mildly
review: I have had much better success using apple cider vinegar and dish soap. Pour about a half inch of apple cider vinegar into a coffee cup and add a drizzle of dish soap. No need to mix, just leave it wherever you've seen the fruit flies. This product costs $8 and the only thing it was good for is the plastic container in my case. I have seen others having a lot of success with this and had hi hopes. I have also seen that others have said that they may not have fruits flies, but I'm pretty sure the little buggars are just that. No worries though, just trying different options.

title: Still have gnats/ drain flies
review: For the price point I really expected it to do a way better job. It helped a little but definetly not the fix for tge problem .

title: Doesn’t work
review: Unfortunately, this didn’t work for me. I live in an apartment of less than 600 sq feet and the fruit flies did not take. I kept it lying around to keep re-trying it but instead it eventually ended up spilling and making my apartment smell like vinegar. Don’t recommend you wasting your $ for a fancily-packaged vinegar.

title: Changed Formula?
review: Bought these a few times now and they’ve always worked great! Recently tho they have not been catching anything at all!

title: Not What I expected
review: this pretty much smells like apple cider vinegar. not sure if it has other things in it. Did not work as i hoped. have had it for about 3 weeks. there are a few flies in it but co side ring how many i have it is about 5% the others just swarm around the top. Will not be buying again

title: Homemade trap works better
review: This is just a very expensive vinegar trap. I placed it next to a homemade trap with red wine, and another with vermouth. The vermouth trapped 90% of the flies. Not worth the cost

title: Effective item leaking.
review: Saved my product defective with leaking. Returned.

title: Did not work at all - it caught nothing! lol
review: I've had it open for a week and caught no fruit flies. The homemade "traps" that i made (apple cider vinegar with a drop of dish soap covered with plastic with a few holes in the top with a toothpick) placed not too far away caught 5 fruit flies within 2 days.

title: Didn't work for me
review: This product (Annie's Fruit Fly) somewhat worked for my niece but it didn't work well for me.

title: Caught a few, but have many, many more that are still flying around.
review: Fall brings these little fruit fly, gnat things around my area. They are really problematic. This product was suggested to me and was said to be a miracle that would solve my problem. NOT!! While a few of these annoying little critters were attracted to the open bottle, the majority were not and kept annoying the household. Wouldn't waste my money again, would try the home remedy I was told about with apple vinegar and dish soap. Don't think it would catch any fewer. Good luck, buyer beware!

title: You catch more flies with vinegar...
review: After reading reviews and press for this product, I had high hopes. Unfortunately, the product didn’t quite deliver on my expectations. When the fruit flies first became an issue in my apartment, I tried out a DIY concoction of apple cider vinegar, water, sugar and dish soap. It caught a lot of flies, but not all of them. I ordered this product and put it out in the same room as the DIY solution. Unfortunately, it only caught one fly while my mixture caught 15-20 flies in the same time span. I have continued to leave Fanny’s out, but although the other mix continues to drown flies, this one still only has that one corpse in it. Save your money.

title: Catches some, but not all
review: I’ve cleaned. My drains closed off. My drains done everything that I can to mitigate the problem, but I just cannot get rid of the fruit flies. This catches some of them, but from time to time you’ll see fruit flies, flying around it, or landing on the mirror above it, but never going into the bottle. It does catch some. It’s just not luring all of them. Ive had it for several weeks. has strong smell initially.

However, this being cheap little bottle of plastic, having it open on your counters is not advised. I tipped this over several times causing the terrible vinegar smell to linger longer than desired! This tipped due to a gust of wind from my kitchen window or my maneuvering thru the kitchen just trying to make dinner.

review: For the cost, this is really ineffective. It works slightly better than trying to get apple cider vinegar and dish soap mixed properly but not by much. Smells about the same. I tried leaving it cracked open, and fully opened as well. One night I accidentally left a ramekin of uncooked egg on the counter ( I was making pie or something) and the next morning I noticed the ramekin had about 20 flies over just one night and the traps still had zero. It clearly works for some people, but for me it didnt. If it didnt work for you, try the egg trick.

It’s as if you dumped the bait into a mug. The flies mostly sit on the rim then fly off. Perhaps if one could use the bait in a more effective trap, it’d be better, but one generally doesn’t expect to have to buy separate traps at this price. At least it doesn’t smell horrible or like a chem lab; just the homey tang of apple cider vinegar.

title: Didn’t work at all…. Perhaps it was the bug not the product?
review: This is a long story. I bought canned cat food from Amazon, as usual I put it in the cupboard and went on with life. Fast forward, a few days later little bugs started flying around my kitchen, I thought they were fruit flies. For two days I put up with them then bought this. Basically this is apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar. You can make the recipe yourself, which I would do instead of buying this. Now, upon a week after the food was put in the cupboard I opened it and was attacked by these little bombers with wings. The gray of cat food was infested, hundreds with eggs. The can of food in the second tray which was covered with the standard cardboard and outer plastic was split which made a great environment for these little jerks. It took me a week to hand kill these things- thankfully they were slow. Perhaps they were not fruit flies and that is why this product didn’t work. This is not why I am giving it two stars. I am giving it 2 starts because of its application. Once the top is flipped open it is easy to tip over, it is not balanced. The top is completely open because the goal is for the flies to go in for a drink and drown. Well, unless you put this inside a mug it is very easy to accidentally tip over. The smell is nauseating, but that is not the fault of the product, sometime the “medicine” is just awful. I also think it is a little overpriced. $8. For ingredients that would cost at most $.75. I know it is the ease of use and when you are being overtaken by bugs you are willing to pay anything. I am giving it 3 stars because I am indifferent of its effectiveness. I am not sure if these were fruit flies- if they were, then this product didn’t work at all, if they weren’t then I am judging the other aspects of the product: ease of use, quality, cost. Etc. Quality: Nice looking label, The high pungent smell of vinegar is enough to make you gag- so, it is the real deal and not watered down. Ease of use: just peel off the thin protective film and flip open the lid- voila. Cost: I think it’s a little pricey for the ingredients which you could easily make yourself. (They give the recipe online) But, isn’t it easy to press the “buy now” button and have the delivery guy drop at your door 48 hrs later?

title: Meh
review: This stuff worked okay. Maybe some batches are better than others. I bought the two-pack and one seemed to attract a lot of gnats while the other caught very few gnats. I tried switching the placement to see if that helped but it didn’t seem to make much difference. It’s very easy to use-just open the package, flip open the lid and it’s ready to go. I’ve made a similar mixture before with comparable results so I probably won’t buy this again.

title: Maybe Not Fruit Flies
review: The product did not work for me, so I originally posted as one-star. Also, it is not eligible for return, so I was stuck with three jars. I am giving three stars now, because of the communication with Aunt Fannie's. I wrote to them hoping they could help with a return. Kelly wrote back promptly and said the return could be done only through Amazon. But, she was very friendly in e-mail and was sorry the product had not worked. She sent some questions and pictures, wondering if what I have is truly fruit flies. As it turned out and upon further research by me, what I seem to have are drain flies. I have eliminated them with baking soda/vinegar and also baking soda/essential oils. I would recommend to anyone that if FlyPunch is not working, consider another fly besides fruit flies. Also, it is worth writing to the company. I found Aunt Fannie's to be very helpful. Update 12/14/17: I have phorid flies, and they are very difficult to get rid of. My baking soda/vinegar/essential oils invention kept them at bay but didn't truly eliminate them. However, I have found a "trap" by happy accident: ruby red grapefruit juice. The little suckers are actually attracted to an open plastic glass filled with juice. It takes a while for them to figure out that they should jump right in, but they are. I am joyfully seeing dead bodies float. This, after going through frustration trying to kill them. I tried adding a drop or two of dishwashing liquid but am finding they are more attracted to just the juice alone. No ACV, orange juice, beer, or red wine for my visitors. Ruby red grapefruit juice. Who knew.

title: So-so
review: I really like this product when it works but it seems inconsistent. Some bottles I have purchased catch a zillion fruit flies and other bottles seem to be totally ineffective. Not sure what's happening there. Appreciate that there is no awful smell and the design doesn't both me sitting out in my kitchen.

Maybe it intoxicates them & they fall in & drown. Eventually some bugs do wind up dead at the bottom of in the solution. I did notice a significant decrease in the number of small flying insects in 7-10 days; just not an immediate impact. Cats do not like the vinegar smell & leave it alone wherever you put it (off the floor).

Does it work? Yes. Do I still have the same type of flies that I had before? Yes, yes I do. Have I tried moving it around where I see flies? Yes, I have. If I had to guess I have 6 flies/gnats, and the bottle has 3 of them. So I gave it a 3/5 rating for getting me 50% of the flies.

My cup is right on the sink, so I'd think there would be something. We'll see how this goes, but so far, I have to be careful not to spill it, it's just ACV, and I haven't caught any fruit flies, so it's not working. I'll update if something changes.

title: Horrible Packaging
review: Yeah, never buying this again. Who looks at a jar of gnat killer and thinks "yeah, let's put a pull-to-open seal on this"? Yes, the kind that come on jugs of tea. The kind that almost always explode open even when you slowly pry them off. So now you've got this sticky, disgusting smelling fluid all over yourself and whatever you opened it over. Your whole house smells like gnat killer now, and the stupid thing doesn't even have a cap! So you just set this open jar of fluid out and hope you don't gave kids or pets cuz they can just take it like a shot glass. And it's ugly to boot. Not worth a penny, just buy those little fruit shaped ones you can get for a buck at walmart.

title: DO NOT BUY! Does not work !
review: This is just vinegar. It does not work at all. I see zero dead fruit flies.

title: Very strong odor that fills the room
review: This product has a very strong vinegar odor. I opened it and used it for two days until I could not stand the smell any longer. There is a very strong vinegar smell. I discarded it and will not use this again. At the same time, I was killing tiny flies That were within 2 to 3 feet of the opened jar of this product as recommended and it did not work. It did not attract the flies at all.

title: Do not buy. A pointless pot of stink
review: I thought I was getting a trap like those little apple ones, where a scent trap is deep inside a container that attracts the flies and keeps them from flying back out. Nope. This is just a jar of really stinky foul liquid that you leave open to the air (there's no cover or anything aside from the lid, which you have to take off to make the thing work so it's an open full pot of a bo smelling sludge that sits there making your kitchen stink and getting bumped by the cat etc. It also didn't work very well. It killed like 2 bugs and then stopped smelling. Now I have to put the lid back on and throw it away I guess. Terrible purchase.

title: A waste of money‼️
review: ABSOLUTELY NO STARS, I KEPT ONE OF THE TWO I ORDERED. THIS CRAP WAS A WASTE OF MONEY....AND IT TOOK DAMN NEAR A MONTH FOR THEM TO REFUND YHE UNOPENED UNUSED PRODUCT‼️‼️‼️😡

title: Stinky, didn't catch a single fly
review: I didn't catch any fruit flys after leaving this out for a month and a half. Fruit flys would land on the rim, and taunt me, but never plunged to their death in the nasty apple cider vinegar goo. Oh yeah, it stinks of apple cider vinegar, so unless you love smelling vinegar and don't want to catch fruit flys, don't waste your money.

title: Trash
review: Does not work I’ve been using it for about a week now I use a strainer because I don’t see any less fruit flies and there is literally nothing that was in it

title: Does not work at all
review: Does not repell any inspects at all, just offers a slight odor.

title: Don’t bother.
review: It did not work at all don’t waste your time and it smells horrible.

title: Worthless as a fruit fly trap
review: This so-called fruit-fly trap was just a container of liquid that smelled like vinegar. It did attract the fruit flies, but, because there was no perforated cover over the liquid, the fruit flies crawled down the sides of the container, sipped the liquid, crawled back up, and then flew away. It is more of a fruit fly feeding station. It did provide inspiration for a trap I made myself. I used an old spice bottle with a perforated top. I filled it half-way with a mixture of cider vinegar and dishwashing liquid. The fruit flies crawled into the bottle and were unable to get back out.

title: Fruit Flies didn't altogether go away
review: I had fruit flys and while this worked o.k.... the night lights were better!~

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Attracts but not traps. The fruit flies will be attracted to the area you placed it but after 4 hours of use I’ve only trapped 1 fruit fly. It’s just apple cider vinegar and other additives in a cup. Stinks up the entire apartment and hasn’t helped with eliminating the problem.

title: Doesn’t kill the Gnats
review: Do not buy these. The liquid attracts the gnats but they do not go into the liquid. It doesn’t kill them. So you just have a ton more gnats flying around.

title: Not that great
review: Attracted flies but did not eliminate them. Flies would only land in rim but never the liquid. Was not worth it did not feel like it was useful. Had a bad scent. Think home remedies would have worked better.

title: Barely works.
review: I’ve used other fly traps in the past in the same room where I set this one up at. They normally catch about 15-20 for a month, whereas this one only successfully caught 1 foolish gnat. Stinks up the room worse than others and also looks ugly and out of place. It’s easy to use, just unscrew the lid however. Just didn’t work and stunk badly. Just use apple cider vinegar and dish soap next time.

title: Make your own, this is crap
review: This is a over prices cup of apple cider Vinager with a drop of detergent. SC Johnson is selling a folk remedy, but they're doing it wrong, there's no perforated top to keep bugs from crawling out. Get some jam jars and make you own, reminding me of that technique is the best thing about this product. It's an insult to consumers to mark up 5¢ of ingredients, pretend it's new, and sell it at a huge mark up.

title: Doesn’t work
review: This product doesn’t work well. If anything, I just draws the fruit flies in to sit on the rim and then they fly away. It doesn’t attract them and eliminate the situation.

title: Don’t do it
review: Promised to start working immediately I have been using this for over a week and it hasn’t worked one bit to get rid of my fruit fly issue. Honestly get a jar and fill it with apple cider vinegar and dish soap will work better than this has.

title: You have better luck pouring vinegar in a dish
review: Waste of money! Doesn’t work as advertised!

title: Doesn't work
review: This did nothing to help the issue. I followed the directions and placed it by the kitchen sink where the little nats gathered, nothing was attracted to it. It killed nothing. Just took up space and was in the way. Very disappointed.

title: It will make your house smell.
review: It stinks. Don’t know if it kills bugs or not. Couldn’t stand to use it.

title: Does not work- smells and nasty!
review: I had high hopes for this product, but all it did was mold on the top layer. I dumped some out and it molded again. Did not see 1 fruit fly caught or knat. And more for the poor review, the product smells, very bad! Will not buy ever again or recommend! Had much much more success with the blue light traps you plug in

review: Bought this after trying many other traps (sticky UV lit traps, DIY apple cider vinegar) for fruit flies near my basement sink. It's been open for almost a week now and not a single fly has been trapped. I've had this trap paired with a USB powered UV lit fan trap and the USB trap has outperformed this Raid trap by a long shot. Maybe this trap works better for certain species of flies or warmer climates (I'm in the northeast US) but it has done little except stink up my basement laundry room.

title: Waste of money.
review: Doesn’t clean easy - leaves stain. Leakage from container. Just plain does not work. Don’t buy it. Waste of your time using it also. If I could put no stars, I would’ve done that.

review: Does not work

I could have made this myself at home for nothing as I already had the ingredients. I bought it because I hate the smell of vinegar and it mentioned essential oils so I bought it. Never again!!! The company who makes it should be ashamed of themselves for selling this. Oh and the package/ product is very small like 2in x 2” !!! What a ripoff!!!

It’s not unpleasant but it is also not pleasant - pungent and unexpected.

review: Have many fruit flies. Only one was drawn to this solution. Also, one of two bottles leaked all over the packaging. Returned after let it sit there on my counter tempting none of the fruit flies.

title: Don’t buy if you love your life!
review: Do not buy this! I repeat! Do not buy this! Within 10 minutes your house will be full of something that you cannot put your finger on other than grasping for fresh air and trying not to meet your maker. Someone decided that putting some sort of mix of ether, apple cider vinegar and some concoction of liquid from the pits of hell together and put it in a bottle said to be safe for home use and thought that was a good idea. 10/10 do not recommend! Just let the fruit flies dance!

title: Total waste of money in my case
review: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
review: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

title: Ineffective and malodorous
review: I did not expect to open the bottle and find that it was a wide-open design and thus easily spillable. I have pets (including a very inquisitive and ungraceful cat), so I can't put it in certain places. I did try to put one in the kitchen but a tiny spider on the windowsill nearby is catching more fruit flies than this trap. The smell of vinegar is quite strong and not pleasant, and so far the fly trap hasn't caught a single obnoxious flying anything.

title: Do not recommend
review: This has been put on my counter for over a day. There is not a single fruit fly in it. Definitely would not recommend. Terro traps are much more effective.

title: Very disappointed
review: I finally received this item after a lengthy shipping period. Both bottles had the caps on wrong and all of the liquid was gone, the packaging is wet and smells like the product. Probably left a trail of fruit fly fluid the whole way.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
review: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

title: Caught three flies only. Put your investment elsewhere.
review: I paid almost $8 to catch three flies. My cat would have done a better job. Basically useless did absolutely nothing to solve my problem. I would be investing in something else.

They were all just hanging out on the popped top diving in for a slurp of vinegar and then resting back on the top. I had more success with a small jar of vinegar with cling wrap poked with a toothpick! China is dumping their junk and Amazon is selling it to us!

The design is clumsy at best and is a spill waiting to happen, It’s just a wide open bottle. I have left one out for over a week now where I have an abundance of fruit flies. Not a single fly in it, they’re not even interested in these. Save your money and find a working product.

title: Save Your $ & Make A Trap From A Old Water Bottle & Vinegar!
review: A homemade trap from an old water bottle & vinegar with a few drops of soap works better than this any day! This simply doesn't work. The reviewers that say it does must have some bad infestations or something as I've had this in various locations for several weeks and not ONE fruit fly was captured! I even added some foil over the top and poked a few holes as some suggested and it still is a miserable failure!
