Actually unreal that i just paid $8 for this, should have read the ingredients. Was specifically trying to not use apple cider vinegar because it stinks. DO NOT BUY! It doesn’t work very well.

title: Probably useless!
review: I tried this product Because i was desperate to get rid of fruit flies. It’s my nderstanding that the that the flies would be attracted to it, enter the bottle and die. If I’m correct, the product was useless,as it did not draw a single fly into it, despite my having left it open on my kitchen counter for 4 days. It just so happens that the infestation had significantly improved by the time I received and set the bottle out, and the flies were actually almost gone by the end of the 4 days, so IF the product works just by sitting open and on the counter, it MAY be that the product did work. At this time I’m just trying to be fair and offer the seller the benefit of the doubt; however, I cannot, now give the product more than one star. I invite the seller to clarify the situation, especially if the product does not need to draw the flies into it for it to work. Also, however, the odor emitted from the jar is so strong and pervasive that it made me nauseous and I doubt I could have tolerated it much longer.

review: I had an area where some fruits and vegetables had gone bad. I saw them land in the bottle but not a single one went into the liquid and died. I've had better luck using plain white vinegar.

title: An absolute waste of money.

title: It does not work !

I let it sit there in disturbed until September 3, 2025, absolutely nothing happened to the flying fruit flies. The fruit flies ignored the bottle all together! Do not waste your money !

title: No longer effective, change in formula?
review: UPDATED REVIEW: Two years ago my apartment has very annoying fruit flies - I lived in a house of four girls, with all of our bananas and avocados and tomatoes, etc, that made it impossible to live produce free for long enough to make the bugs go away. I bought this product, and within days there were over 15 fruit flies that it had gotten rid of. I bought more, and our fruit fly problem went away and stayed away. This year, with the summer heat and plethora of summer fruit, the fruit flies are back. And this time, after buying 5 of these liquid traps, none of them are working. I even see fruit flies flying immediately next to the traps, but after 4 weeks of hoping they would start working again they are not, and I am thoroughly disappointed. The company must have changed their formula for this drastic of a decline in its effectiveness.

title: Eh
review: While I do like these and they work okay… They don’t stop the source of the problem which is likely the garbage disposal or a drain. They kill off a fair amount but they keep coming.

title: OK
review: This works okay, but not as good as store products or homemade recipes unless you change it every 3 days.

title: Doesn’t work much
review: The first package was poorly wrapped and arrived with one broken bottle of liquid all over everything. Amazon replaced this with no issue. But, it now sits next to my old jar with homemade stuff in it (red wine, and a bit of dish detergent) and the flies have not used this stuff any more than the homemade. They keep flocking to my homemade stuff. So save your money and look up a nice recipe.

title: Open bottle - prone to spills
review: It caught a couple of fruit flies so that’s good. I was surprised to see a completely open top. If it gets knocked over, it will be a huge headache to clean up never mind disgusting. I’ll probably use it to refill the little apple/strawberry-shaped containers that are less likely to leak if tipped over.

title: Ineffective trap design
review: The trap smelled like other vinegar based traps which I've used before. This is essentially a spice container filled with vinegar/soap solution. There is no inverted bit to keep insects from flying back out. Unfortunately they fly in but don't get caught in the trap unlike others I've used. This didn't work at all. I ended up pouring the solution into a glass with a plastic bag over the top, cut a smaller hole, and it worked better than what I was provided.

title: Not really worth the cost.

review: I had purchased this product a year or two ago and I was very impressed with how well it worked as it seemed to alleviate all of the fruit flies in our kitchen within ~24 hours after putting it out. When I went to reorder a few weeks ago, I noticed that it had different packaging but didn’t think much of it. However, after having it out for several days now, there are still fruit flies flying around. Not sure if it is a different formula than what was used in the past but it doesn’t seem to be working as well this time. A bit disappointed.

title: Wasn’t great; smells like vinegar
review: This stuff smells just like vinegar. The label says there are other ingredients, but I feel like I just paid way too much for a little bottle of something I already had in my cupboard. More importantly, it didn’t really work that well. As you can see in the picture, there is a fruit fly perched on the outside of the bottle at the top of the label. I managed to catch a few of them, but it wasn’t enough to make a difference.

title: Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch! Fruit Fly Trap ...
review: I have been battling fruit flies for 2 weeks! Between the produce I buy and my fruit flavored vape juice they have been relentless. I just received one of these today along with a 2 pack of Terro brand "Peaches". I set all three out in my house. One Terro and this product in kitchen and one Terro in my den. The Aunt Fannie's product has eliminated more flies than the two Terro peaches combined so far (less than 24 hours). Update: You can lead a fly to a lure, but you can't make the fly jump in. I ended up finding a chemical product called PT Alpine that eliminated all the flies in my home in 48 hours.

title: Fruit Fly Trap
review: We all of a sudden had a huge amount of fruit flys in our kitchen and bathroom areas. Tried all the home made remedies we could think of and nothing seemed to work. I bought Aunt Fannies Fruit Fly Killer from Amazon and was hoping to get rid of them all. Much to our disappointment, it did not work as well as we had hoped. It did trap a few flies, but not any better than the home made remedies we tried. We are still battling with them. We even bough a spray by RAID it does kill them but not all of them. Don't know where they are coming from or how to get rid of them

title: So it did work….
review: But only for about a week. Honestly this is just apple cider vinegar in a spice container. You could make it yourself if you just buy vinegar and dawn soap.

title: There are better products on the market.
review: Okay so I managed to get some fruit flies the first few days, but not all. Obviously the more you have, the better chance you will get at getting rid of fruit flies. I would consider it mildly effective at best though. And because the lid opens up wide without any sort of barrier, I have unfortunately knocked it over several times and had to clean up a stinky mix of smelly vinegar and dead bugs. After the initial effectiveness wore off, no more flies are taking the bait--I still have tons of flies everywhere. I think you're better off investing in a better product.

title: Works as well as vinegar and dish soap.
review: Works as well as dish soap and apple cidar vinegar or regular white vinegar. More expensive than the mentioned method. The container is cool but you could buy one for cheap. Good option is you do not wish to out the ingredients together yourself and pour into a container. I caught two fruit flies with it, my vinegar and dish soap caught three over a 24 hour period. Could be location of containers. I ended up swatting about 10 of them myself. So get a gooe fly swatter. The flies will land in areas and you can see them and crush their souls.

title: Didn’t Work as fast as I thought it would
review: I liked how easy it was to use, but it took awhile for the flies to get attracted to it, and the smell was a very strong vinegar smell.

title: Works great but wasn’t packaged well
review: These have historically worked great for me, but this is my first time ordering them from Amazon. Both had burst open and leaked all throughout the packaging causing a sticky mess.

title: kinda works?
review: Bought this for some fruit flies we had, had it opened in my room for about 4 days and in that time it caught 2 flies. It's nice because it requires very zero effort but in the same amount of time, I manually squashed maybe 2 or 3 by myself. I don't think the flies were especially attracted to it, but perhaps the unlucky ones who happen to stumble across will get caught. I ended up closing the jar and putting it away because the smell was bothering me more than it was attracting/catching the flies.

title: Only for fruit flies
review: My office has a problem with drain gnats. I thought I would give this a try even though the description says it's specifically designed only for fruit flies. Well they weren't lying. Not a single gnat went in this bottle. They circle it and land right next to it but do not go in. Also, this thing just contains apple cider vinegar and a little soap. You could use an empty spice container and make the same thing at home.

title: Impressed by the Reviews but Disappointed by the Results
review: I have been needing a fruit fly trap desperately and had seen this was one of the top rated products. I had been hoping it’s simple design would be all there was so I left it adjacent to our sink and garbage can (a hotspot) and let it be. Two weeks later, there are only 3 measly flies down at the bottom compared to other pictures I’ve seen where there are dozens gathered down there. I’ve noticed the flies don’t actually go down in the bottle and mostly walk around the outer rim before flying off. Maybe mine are just too smart...

title: Worked ok
review: It’s an ok product caught some fruit flys not all of them and it just smells like vinegar and could be made at home

title: Stinky product
review: Omg, this stuff smells so bad! I mean maybe that’s the point to attract the bugs, but I couldn’t stand to be in the same room as an open container of this. For the most part I left it open at night and then lit a candle to get rid of the smell the next morning. To make matters worse, I ended up accidentally knocking over mine.. dead bug juice everywhere. It does work, but not enough for me to want to buy this product again.

title: Worked decent after awhile
review: Like a lot of reviews have mentioned, I opened this thing up with a decent number of fruit flies around and was having seemingly no success. I went ahead and left it in position near my trash can and after a few days it finally started to catch them. Not sure if they needed time to warm up to it or what, but it works decent these days for a relatively cheap product that doesn't stink up the place TOO bad.

title: Doesn’t seem to attract fruit flies
review: Love ease of use, but out of all the different types of traps we set out, these were the only ones that barely attracted a single fruit fly. The ones that work the best are the ones shaped like little red apples with lots of holes in the top. Those are now full of dead fruit flies, but the Aunt fannies fly punch traps have only one fruit fly trapped out of all four of the traps that we set out.

title: Not effective
review: It as effective as I would have liked!

title: Gnats
review: The product works okay but not as good as I expected.

title: Moderately effective
review: Liked the dead fruit flies! Prefer not having another open liquid container on my kitchen sink, but workable if careful. Has time-limited effectiveness. DOES attract the little buggers but dont expect immediate results. Not the wayvm it's intended to work.

title: Im not sure...
review: So I will say the product works because it did capture a lot of flies after a while. I guess my main concern was that It had to sit on the counter for a long time before anything really started to happen. Im kind of on the fence about ordering again because of that fact. other than that, the product was great, didn't have a unpleasant smell and arrived very quickly.

title: Worked better when there were A LOT of fruit flies
review: Originally this product worked as well as if I'd just put a cup of water on the counter. In over a couple of days since opening it, it was put to use near the source of the problem, and it lured/killed 2 fruit flies while the rest continued to fly around freely in the kitchen. Disappointed 😕 but once I put it around a higher concentration of flies, it lured more. It didn't work well when there were only 5-10 flies.

title: Not The Best Product For Catching Fruit Flies
review: Having a Bearded Dragon and Guinea Pigs as well as breeding my own meal worms and super worms for my Bearded Dragon and to sell we tend to get a lot of fruit flies. I bought a 6-pack but unfortunately they have not really been successful in catching the fruit flies. There have been an average of about five in each bottle. It is easy and convenient but not doing the job as we had hoped.

title: Not effective. the "apple" fruit fly traps work better
review: thought they were expensive apple cider vinegar..

title: Not worth it
review: So so. It smells like vinegar mostly and there’s no way to prevent a spill if it’s open. The flies land on the side a lot. The second one I ordered didn’t work at all. Like they got immune to it or something. Orange juice did the trick in a fraction of the time so save your money.

title: Doesn’t kill them, only attracts them.
review: This doesn't work, it attracts more fruit flies but does not kill them. I used it for more then 2 months and hasn't killed one… I have a lot more flies then before actually.

title: Save your money.
review: Ineffective -- we recently had an issue with fruit flies and this product didn't do its job. Better luck with homemade solution of water, vinegar, and dish soap. Also found sticky traps worked.

title: Fruit Flies Roundly Ignored this substance.
review: Have many fruit flies. Only one was drawn to this solution. Also, one of two bottles leaked all over the packaging. Returned after let it sit there on my counter tempting none of the fruit flies.

title: Don’t buy if you love your life!
review: Do not buy this! I repeat! Do not buy this! Within 10 minutes your house will be full of something that you cannot put your finger on other than grasping for fresh air and trying not to meet your maker. Someone decided that putting some sort of mix of ether, apple cider vinegar and some concoction of liquid from the pits of hell together and put it in a bottle said to be safe for home use and thought that was a good idea. 10/10 do not recommend! Just let the fruit flies dance!

title: Total waste of money in my case
review: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
review: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

title: Ineffective and malodorous
review: I did not expect to open the bottle and find that it was a wide-open design and thus easily spillable. I have pets (including a very inquisitive and ungraceful cat), so I can't put it in certain places. I did try to put one in the kitchen but a tiny spider on the windowsill nearby is catching more fruit flies than this trap. The smell of vinegar is quite strong and not pleasant, and so far the fly trap hasn't caught a single obnoxious flying anything.

title: Do not recommend
review: This has been put on my counter for over a day. There is not a single fruit fly in it. Definitely would not recommend. Terro traps are much more effective.

title: Very disappointed
review: I finally received this item after a lengthy shipping period. Both bottles had the caps on wrong and all of the liquid was gone, the packaging is wet and smells like the product. Probably left a trail of fruit fly fluid the whole way.

title: Well it didn’t work, also leaked out before I got it…
review: When I say this was the biggest disappointment I have come across in along time, I mean it. Now this worked for my friend and was recommended to me so I thought, trusted review from a trusted person so why not. Yeah no, smell is much stronger than regular soap and apple cider vinegar but I was willing to smell( it in a completely different room mind you) as long as it worked. Received the product and both bottles were leaking all over the Amazon package… oh well moving on. Left it out for a couple of days and didn’t catch one bug, not a gnat, not a fruit fly, only attention it caught was mine cause that smell was STRONG. You would have better luck just making a concoction yourself or buying a big light for gnats and fruit flies- that’s what I did when I returned this. Would not recommend to anyone but my enemy.

title: Not worth it for the price
review: I just don’t like it

title: Good concept but not great results
review: Still waiting. One fruit fly caught. My resolution - take caution using - pouring hot water from the tea kettle down all drains - it eradicates living fruit flies and the eggs if they have laid any in your drains. Haven't seen a bug since! To be sure, I have treated every night before bedtime for 4 days. Total success!

title: Sadness and despair
review: One can came empty. Amazon won’t respond I can’t get the seller to respond. So I pours half the liquid from one into the other and set them out. It’s been two days not a single fruit fly. :( I had high hopes but it really doesn’t work for me.

title: Stinks
review: Stinks and leaking. I don’t know why I expected it to have a way too keep the bugs in, like you do when you set up a home made one. But there’s no way to trap them in.

title: Works BUT see the photos attached and you decide
review: The FlyPunch works, BUT,... I had much better luck with a simple household product that didn’t cost me but a few pennies. Both traps were set at the same time 48-52 hours ago. FlyPunch and a bowl of apple cider Venegar with 2-3 drops of dish soap stirred in. Traps were set 3-4 inches apart on the kitchen window. Pictures attached that shows a massive difference between the 2 traps. I was able to count 8 fruit flies in the FlyPunch and far too many to count in the apple cider vinegar mix Can’t say if the FlyPunch would have worked better with the cling wrap, often saw fruit flies sitting on the rim but not too many died. I simply followed the directions on the bottle and did the same with the apple cider trap I googled. 🤷🏽♂️ Left for Thanksgiving and forgot to throw out the bananas, and Shazam,... lots of fruit flies when we returned. 48-52 hours later 99% are gone. You decide which trap worked better.

title: Didn’t work!!
review: Had high hopes this product would work… But… Not one fruit fly took the bate.. very disappointed!

title: Didn't work for me
review: I bought this product because I began to have fruit flies in my apartment. I wanted something easy, something that didn't require much work, so I thought this would be perfect. Just open and forget it. Well after almost two weeks it only caught two fruit flies, just TWO. I was pretty disappointed. I ended up just buying one of those electrical fan things that have a light that are made to trap fruit flies via the fan down onto a glue board. I ran this for two weeks and caught almost 60! So this fan thing worked way better than this liquid. And to top it off, no refunds are allowed. Very shady in my opinion. If my fan trap caught 60 and this liquid caught 2, then it obviously if faulty and I should have the option to get my money back. Do not waste your money on this product.

title: Toxic. Misleading Amazon description.
review: Sorry I ordered this and it will be going down the drain. The description says it’s “plant-based” and “safe around food”. But the label on the product contains several warnings, including to wear rubber gloves when handling and what to do if it gets on your skin. When it’s set up for use it’s an open bottle, just waiting to tip over. It contains Ethyl Lactate: “Ethyl lactate can be harmful if inhaled or absorbed through the skin. Prolonged contact can irritate the skin and eyes, and breathing it in can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, and passing out. Ethyl lactate is flammable and can cause serious or permanent injury”

title: A 100% useless product
review: Completely useless against gnats (fruit flies)...or any other fly infestation. A total BS product. Don't be fooled!

title: Bad product
review: Does not work. The flies aren’t attracted to the trap.

title: Terrible!
review: I bought two of these and left them out for three weeks. Neither caught a single fruit fly/gnat. I cannot believe I wasted $16 on these. I do not understand how anyone gave these good reviews! If I could give 5 negative stars, I would.

title: So disappointing
review: I have been struggling with fruit flies for a few weeks now and I have been trying every trick in the book. I did some research and heard about these and thought oh finally something easy to help with these annoying things. I have had them out for two days now and nothing….it attracts the fruit flys but they don’t go inside and if they do they come right back out. I thought I would try dumping some of it into a shallow plate but that did not work, I tried putting it in a bowl and that does not work either. I had got these little apple looking things prior and they worked pretty well so I just ordered a bunch of those alone with a drain killer to pour down my kitchen drain and hopefully soon I won’t have an issue anymore. But all in all I would not recommend these.

title: Not worth it
review: Purchased this product, and was very excited to use it since I have a pesky fruit fly problem. The bottles came broken. Some of the contents spilled into the packaging. Contacted customer support from the dealer and they do not do refunds since I bought through Amazon. Decided to use the product anyway, from what I had. I’ve had it open for 3 days now. It has caught one fly. All the other flies just fly around it. Product did not work for me. Don’t waste your money.

title: It hasn't caught a single fly...
review: When we open the back door, we've discovered flies congregating by the door, and invariably, at least a couple of flies fly in the door. (We have to go in and out a lot to walk dogs). I got one of those battery-operated fly eliminators that look like a tennis racket, thinking I could get them right at the door, but I'm not fast enough. We tried sticky fly paper, which works quite well, but it isn't attractive. I thought we'd give this a try. In four days, it hasn't attracted a single fly. There is nothing in containers. I got six. I put two out. I'm very disappointed because these containers sure look better than fly paper. I will update if there's any change but so far, not one fly...

title: Not worth buying
review: This product doesn’t do much if you’re looking at drastically improving a gnat infestation. Get a drain cleaner instead. This is too gentle and doesn’t do much. Save your money. I wish I could return this lol

title: Does not work at all!
review: We had a lot of fruit flies upon returning from vacation. We tried these traps and caught only two flies with them in two weeks! The jars do not have any way to trap the flies, the lid is wide open, and this is a flaw of design. If the lid had smaller holes in it, the flies would get trapped in there. The flies fly into these traps and do not stay there--whatever is in it does not attract or kill them. We got rid of our fruit flies using yellow sticky glue traps and other liquid fruit fly traps that have a better attractant and design to keep the flies trapped. And also good old-fashioned home-made vinegar, water, dish soap traps helped--with a dash of apple-cider vinegar as attractant or small piece of fruit in it.

title: Don't bother
review: Strong vinegar smell, but tolerable. After 2 months, only 6 fruit flies. My leftover glass of wine works much better. Leave a small bowl of wine or juice overnight. Much more effective.

title: Useless
review: Literally did nothing. Left it out for 5 days and 0 flies went in. Waste of money

title: It didn't work this time, formula change?
review: Unlike the same product we purchased previously that worked really well, these two bottles were completely ineffective. Not a single fruit fly was caught, while my used wine glasses attracted many. I am not sure if there was any formula changes, but these simply didn’t work at all.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
review: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

title: Caught three flies only. Put your investment elsewhere.
review: I paid almost $8 to catch three flies. My cat would have done a better job. Basically useless did absolutely nothing to solve my problem. I would be investing in something else.

title: Total failure
review: sadly they do not work - don't know why but I was hoping this took care of my problem but not happening - going back to my local hardware store to get the ones that have worked in the past and these are going back to Amazon

title: Junk
review: Don’t waste your money! Not only is this nothing more than vinegar, it is a poor design. The top is just wide open. You have to have small holes so the fruit flies can get in but not out! They were all just hanging out on the popped top diving in for a slurp of vinegar and then resting back on the top. I had more success with a small jar of vinegar with cling wrap poked with a toothpick! China is dumping their junk and Amazon is selling it to us!

title: Doesn’t work.
review: Initially I had high hope for this based on what others were saying. Unfortunately these were a huge let down for me. The design is clumsy at best and is a spill waiting to happen, It’s just a wide open bottle. I have left one out for over a week now where I have an abundance of fruit flies. Not a single fly in it, they’re not even interested in these. Save your money and find a working product.

title: Save Your $ & Make A Trap From A Old Water Bottle & Vinegar!
review: A homemade trap from an old water bottle & vinegar with a few drops of soap works better than this any day! This simply doesn't work. The reviewers that say it does must have some bad infestations or something as I've had this in various locations for several weeks and not ONE fruit fly was captured! I even added some foil over the top and poked a few holes as some suggested and it still is a miserable failure!

title: Odd bottle
review: The bottle is odd designed, unprofessional, unpractical.

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Ineffective, and will not get the job done. You could probably make something better on your own.

title: Ridiculous
review: Do not waste your time nor your money. Zero effectiveness. Nothing else needs to be stated. Have a nice day.

title: Just ACV! Biggest waste of money
review: Biggest rip off ever. This item is literally a plastic spice jar of apple cider vinegar, you could make this for 50 cents in less time it would take to order this with items in your kitchen. Actually unreal that i just paid $8 for this, should have read the ingredients. Was specifically trying to not use apple cider vinegar because it stinks. DO NOT BUY! It doesn’t work very well.

title: Didn't work- not a single fly
review: We've been having a massive Fruit Fly issue and been trying everything we could to get it under control. I had high hopes for these but we've had two of them open for a week now and not a single Fruit fly has gone for these. We've moved them around to different areas of our pantry and kitchen and nothing. We've had better luck with homemade traps using dish soap w/ red wine or cider vinegar. They still aren't managing the situation but at least SOME dead flies have resulted from those.

title: Didn’t work at all
review: I bought a two pack of these….they both collectively caught three gnats. Mind you, I’m having an infestation right now. My own home made ACV and sugar water with dawn dish soap worked way better.

title: Charging for 12 bottles and sending just 1 bottle
review: Ordered the 12 pack for $80 and received just one bottle. Requested a replacement and received one bottle instead of 12 again despite a charge for a 12 pack

title: Don’t waste your time or money!!
review: This was an absolute freaking waste of money. I am so irritated because it was one of those products that really stood out to me, like no way thousands of people are being dishonest and rating it highly consistently. Boy was I wrong. So, I have a summer time issue with fruit flies (due to fruit). Could not get rid of them for anything. I used the katchy, stem spray, and this product. I had my home PROFESSIONALLY cleaned, opened one of these jars, and left for a 2-week vacation. I just knew I would be coming back to a fruit fly free home thanks to this product working it’s magic. No such luck. I’ll stop there, but just take it from me. It is a waste of money, so don’t get your hopes up.

title: Don’t waist your money!!!
review: If I can give zero stars, I would, but it makes me pick at least one. Total waste of money. I’ve worked in the bar industry for years, I’ve seen barflies congregate around the alcohol for years. I bought this product because it said it was specifically formulated for barflies. At the three days only two barflies were caught in the syrup. I decided to buy another product and filled the bottom cup portion with Jim Bean. Within an hour, there was over a dozen flies caught in the trap. Don’t waste your money. This product does not work.

title: sent an open product
review: we were sent a product that was open, spilled all over the bag and one of the containers was missing half the liquid

title: Disappointed
review: I was having an awful problem with fruit flies in the kitchen and dining room. I read about using apple cider vinegar and water or, even better, Flypunch. I had apple cider vinegar on hand so I tried it first and ordered Flypunch on the same day. After two days of using the apple cider vinegar 95% of the fruit flies were gone. The Flypunch arrived and I figured it would clear up the remaining 5%. That was not the case. After three days of using only the Flypunch, two bottles, the fruit flies were back. I pulled out the apple cider vinegar and the next morning the flies were gone. If you want to get rid of fruit flies first try the apple cider vinegar.

title: Aunt Fannies No Catch Punch
review: This product did not work for me! I have had it out for about a week. There were only two fruit flies captured. I purchased another product which seems to have caught the ones that Aunt Fannies fly punch didn't catch. I absolutely wasted my money.

title: More wasted money
review: I purchased Aunt Fannie's fly punch fruit fly trap based on all of the encouraging reviews. More wasted money! It smelled just like vinegar when I opened it and left it out for quite a few days with quite a few fruit flies .They were not interested! I have a picture of the open container of the fly punch next to a tuna fish can filled with regular apple cider vinegar and a few pieces of old fruit. Regular apple cider vinegar caught more fruit flies compared to the fly punch which caught none.

title: Boo..
review: Hasn't caught anything!! It ended up getting knocked over... what a mess!! It smells like vinegar. My son found a DIY recipe online and it's only caught a few but it was free!! I did a thorough cleaning with bleach on counters, floors, and cabinets and it's adequate a noticeable difference for today anyway!! Save your money... or throw it away but don't give it to these people!!

title: Ease of use
review: When I got my product one bottle the lid was loose and had leaked all out in package . So didn’t even get to use it. We shall see if it really works as of now not sure. Don’t like the lid has to be completely open should have some kind of guard where the liquids won’t leak out if tipped over

title: seems my used wine glasses that sit on the counter overnite get more attention from the fruit flys
review: not what i expected . takes quite a while to attract the fruit flys

title: It works better for me than home-made.
review: A lot of people are upset that this is basically just the home remedy of apple cider vinegar and soap. And yeah, it is, but I’m catching way more of the flies with this than the home brew, so Aunt Fannie’s doing something right. I wish it was a little more enclosed though, because the open mouth with the unwieldy flip top is begging for it to get tipped over and spill.

title: Would try again
review: I love aunt fannies products, this one just did not work for the little flies in my house. I’ve done everything and they won’t go away, so it may not be this products fault.

title: Kill nets
review: Did not kill the fruit flys

title: Worked
review: Although it worked,it didn’t perform as I hoped

title: Not great
review: The flies don't go in. Doesn't work.

title: It's trying to work
review: It attracts the flies, but the lip is perfect for them to have a little snack and not fall in. I watched one fly in yesterday so I know it works. I've removed the lid to see if that is the problem. You could probably make one of these yourself if you wanted to save like 4 bucks considering what you need to make this included.

title: Not sure what it supposed to do 🤔
review: So to be honest. I'm really not sure what it is supposed to do. According to the description it should trap the fruit fly but it didn't trap even one but it repelled them where I don't have any in my house anymore which the goal. So I'm happy with it. It did deliver what I paid for even though it is the opposite outcome🤪🤪

title: cider vinegar works just as well and is cheaper
review: We went on vacation and forgot to take out the trash so when we returned home the house was full of fruit flies. I set out little dishes of cider vinegar with a drop of dish soap to get rid of them but they were not disappearing fast enough so I purchased this to see if it would work quicker. It looks and smells just like the cider vinegar and only worked about as well. There were no more bugs in this than in the other home remedies I used so it was really a waste of money to buy it when it didn't work any better.

title: Nice packaging, but doesn’t work.
review: I’m sorry, I thought this cute little bottle with the peculiar odor would be the end of my fruit fly problem. Nope. A few of the little buggers have flown in, but not enough to make a difference. I’m also afraid I’m going to knock it over. Uggh. No re-buy for this product.

title: Catching fruit flys
review: Did not work right away, over a few days noticed flys in liquid, but did not work quickly

title: Fruit Flies do like it
review: Tt worked instantly, fruit flies hovering over it and dove into the liquid... but it slowed down considerably. It could be that I got a fair amount of them, not sure. I still see one or two/three, etc buzzing around. I've only had this for a week....so I'll try to update this review. Smells like apple cider vinegar, so if that's what is in this, you could make a home remedy

title: Attracts flies.
review: It does attract flies. The cost per volume seems high.

title: It works but not for a large infestation
review: This product is okay but I would highly recommend one of the products you pour into the sink and let sit overnight.

title: These bugs are literally mocking me
review: I have little knats in my house and I thought maybe I'd leave the formulating of these traps up to the pros. They have been out now for almost 24 hours, not 1 big captured. Update. I think I have a combined 18 dead. So... I take it back... It does work.

title: Make Your Own For a Lower Price
review: It's essentially apple cider vinegar with soap- you could make something like the product by yourself and for way less money. As another reviewer pointed out, the bait liquid itself will probably drown some fruit flies but to really maximize the number of fruit flies it kills, you need to stick some doubled sided sticky fly traps into the bottle. If you do this, you'll be amazed and disgusted by how much fruit flies have been lurking around your home.

title: Package leaks
review: Package leaks and the fluid was all over the inside of it and it smells pretty bad so that's my review

title: Not Worth It
review: I didn't look closely at the photos and assumed the lid had small holes in it, but it's just a wide open lid. You're better off pouring some cheap apple cider vinegar and dish soap in an old cup of your own. I've noticed that this method of catching fruit flies works best when you use a paper funnel or poke holes in plastic wrap, to trap them once they're lured in. I caught more doing that than I did with this wide open on my counter.

title: Use apple cider vinegar instead
review: Save yourself a few bucks and use apple cider vinegar, the cheap stuff, because that's basically all this product is, with a couple of other things thrown in that you don't really need. I've been using the same container and have just been adding some vinegar to it as needed, but you can use any container you have available. I haven't noticed any difference in their product vs. the apple cider vinegar. It still attracts them into the bottle and there they stay, in the liquid, until you dump it out and refresh it.

title: Probably useless!
review: I tried this product Because i was desperate to get rid of fruit flies. It’s my nderstanding that the that the flies would be attracted to it, enter the bottle and die. If I’m correct, the product was useless,as it did not draw a single fly into it, despite my having left it open on my kitchen counter for 4 days. It just so happens that the infestation had significantly improved by the time I received and set the bottle out, and the flies were actually almost gone by the end of the 4 days, so IF the product works just by sitting open and on the counter, it MAY be that the product did work. At this time I’m just trying to be fair and offer the seller the benefit of the doubt; however, I cannot, now give the product more than one star. I invite the seller to clarify the situation, especially if the product does not need to draw the flies into it for it to work. Also, however, the odor emitted from the jar is so strong and pervasive that it made me nauseous and I doubt I could have tolerated it much longer.

title: Useless Product - Did Nothing
review: Left out for about a month and caught 0 flies in my kitchen. Just dried up. Waste of money…Avoid.

title: Apple cider vinger
review: Not worth the money. This does nothing. Its vinger and that's what I've been using.

title: Waste of money.
review: High priced vinegar. Didn't work for me. Very dissapointed. I usually never take the time to write a review, but this product was so bad. A week went by and just one fruit fly. Another week and still nothing. They don't even seem to go near it. Not worth the risk of accidently spilling the contents, due to open container. Unbelievable how some people love it.

title: I put out 2 traps & watched cloud's of fruit flies surrounding it
review: I had an area where some fruits and vegetables had gone bad. I sat both of the items with their tops opened ( sure smelled like Apple Cider Vinegar to me) and for 3 days watched cloud's of fruit flies flying in clouds around it. I saw them land in the bottle but not a single one went into the liquid and died. I've had better luck using plain white vinegar.

title: An absolute waste of money.
review: You can achieve the same results BETTER by simply putting some apple cider vinegar in a small dish. This is overpriced for a container that isn’t special. And a solution that is nothing special. Ol Aunt Fannie scammed us all. Aunt Fannie… more like Aunt Farty. Don’t waste your money.

title: Doesn't work, save your $$
review: This product arrived half-empty and the little that remained did not attract any fruit flies. Zero. Don't waste your money.

title: Does not work at all
review: This didn’t work at all. I left it out for several weeks and it didn’t do anything. There isn’t really a trap, it’s just a bottle of vinegar, with a fully open flip top lid, that the gnats can fly in and out of. I feel like this was a complete waste of money and time. It needs a better design as there isn’t a way to actually trap the bugs.

title: It does not work !
review: I bought this brought June 2025. I opened the lid and placed it on the kitchen counter next to the fruit bowl. I let it sit there in disturbed until September 3, 2025, absolutely nothing happened to the flying fruit flies. The fruit flies ignored the bottle all together! Do not waste your money !

title: No longer effective, change in formula?
review: UPDATED REVIEW: Two years ago my apartment has very annoying fruit flies - I lived in a house of four girls, with all of our bananas and avocados and tomatoes, etc, that made it impossible to live produce free for long enough to make the bugs go away. I bought this product, and within days there were over 15 fruit flies that it had gotten rid of. I bought more, and our fruit fly problem went away and stayed away. This year, with the summer heat and plethora of summer fruit, the fruit flies are back. And this time, after buying 5 of these liquid traps, none of them are working. I even see fruit flies flying immediately next to the traps, but after 4 weeks of hoping they would start working again they are not, and I am thoroughly disappointed. The company must have changed their formula for this drastic of a decline in its effectiveness.

title: Didn’t do much
review: Based on what was advertised, it did none of that. And I didn’t read reviews where I saw some say nope and I still purchased it anyway. I was desperate. I had so many fruit flies in my house it was crazy. Placed both of them in designated areas and over 12 hours went by and it had only captured maybe 2 or 3. 24 hours maybe 6.

title: Do not buy
review: Bought this and the red terro traps and this. Placed them side by side for 2 weeks. Terro traps continually trapped fruit flies. This? Not even one. Complete waste of money.

title: not worth $0
review: DOES NOT WORK AT ALL! Did NOT capture 1 fly and there are plenty.

title: The Worst
review: The container has no little holes for the fruit flies, its just open on top when you set it up. They don't list the ingredients but it's basically vinegar and some dish soap. You could make this yourself with an empty spice container. To add insult to injury it ABSOLUTELY DOES NOT WORK. Can fruit flies laugh? Because I'm pretty sure they're laughing as they swarm around our kitchen and completely ignore this "trap". Literally not even ONE fruit fly is stupid enough to fall for it. I however was dumb enough to purchase without checking all the reviews so Fruit Flies 1, stupid human 0.

title: Not effective
review: Didn’t catch a single fruit fly.

title: Don't waste your money.
review: I only gave this a one star because I couldn't give it a zero. When I read reviews I try to take all of them and try or not try based on what others say that is important. Please Don't waste your money on this product to me it doesn't smell like other say it does since I use apple cider vinegar at my house on a regular. But it doesn't help with the fruit gnats either. I placed a bottle right beside one of my plants and not one gnats went into the bottle. Even after two weeks when the smell was not strong it didn't have any gnats inside the bottle.

title: Doesn’t work
review: Product has been left out in kitchen counter for over a week, and just 1 little fly or gnat has been trapped in there. Definitely will not purchase again. I love AF products but not this one! Better stuff out there for sure

title: Does not work
review: I was hopeful this would work based on the reviews. However, after two days, it has done nothing. I'm going to give it two more days. I will update my review if anything changes.

title: Not worth it
review: I purchased this item due to a recommendation by several websites. I had a MUCH better experience catching fruit flies with a home remedy than this product. I tried it in different areas of the kitchen and only caught one. The home remedy caught the large majority of the flies we were struggling with. The home remedy was apple cider vinegar and a drop of dish soap. I learned through trial-and-error that a shot glass works best instead of a bowl. I assume the steeper sides of the glass helped catch them.

title: Doesn’t kill them, only attracts them.
review: This doesn't work, it attracts more fruit flies but does not kill them. I used it for more then 2 months and hasn't killed one… I have a lot more flies then before actually.

title: Save your money.
review: Ineffective -- we recently had an issue with fruit flies and this product didn't do its job. Better luck with homemade solution of water, vinegar, and dish soap. Also found sticky traps worked.

title: Fruit Flies Roundly Ignored this substance.
review: Have many fruit flies. Only one was drawn to this solution. Also, one of two bottles leaked all over the packaging. Returned after let it sit there on my counter tempting none of the fruit flies.

title: Don’t buy if you love your life!
review: Do not buy this! I repeat! Do not buy this! Within 10 minutes your house will be full of something that you cannot put your finger on other than grasping for fresh air and trying not to meet your maker. Someone decided that putting some sort of mix of ether, apple cider vinegar and some concoction of liquid from the pits of hell together and put it in a bottle said to be safe for home use and thought that was a good idea. 10/10 do not recommend! Just let the fruit flies dance!

title: Total waste of money in my case
review: I have been battling fruit flies in my kitchen for a while. I've tried several methods including fly strips as well as multiple homemade traps using differing methods (mason jar with apple cider vinegar & dish soap, wine bottles with a bit of wine left, mason jars with apple cider vinegar *and* rotting fruit with saran wrap & holes poked, jars with paper funnel, etc.) I've even heated the apple cider vinegar before setting out the traps to produce an aroma of the fermenting vinegar/fruit. I had high hopes for this product but it literally only caught 1 or 2 fruit flies. I caught many more with just regular fly strips that catch them by chance. I left this product in two separate places in my kitchen for over a week and the fruit flies ignored it completely. Total waste of money in my case. I got rid of my fruit flies by actively spraying them with a spray bottle filled with dish soap & water, fly strips, and pouring boiling water down the drain every day (and being diligent about not leaving food crumbs out). Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch did not help at all and was a waste of money in my case. The fruit flies I had completely ignored this product (which smells like it is simply apple cider vinegar anyway).

title: An expensive version of a cheap home remedy that doesn't work
review: I probably should have researched the product a bit more before buying it. After opening it it became very obvious from the smell and look what it was. It's literally just a bottle of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of soap. It even says so in the ingredient list "vinegar, water, ethyl lactate(aka soap)". To be fair it does kind of say that in the description so that's on me. Does it work? - About as well as apple cider vin and soap does (because that's what this product is). I've heard of this working for others so that's what I tried before buying this. For me I caught about 5 flies with my home made stuff and 3 with this product. My other home made trap was a bottle with a small amount of fruit juice and sealed with some plastic wrap with a few small holes. That has caught around 50. Still have an infestation. This, along with the home made stuff, will make the whole area smell of vinegar. If you really want to try this method then just make it yourself for half the cost. Most people have acv and soap laying around anyways. And if it doesn't work then at least you'll have left over soap you can use to clean and acv you can cook with.

title: Ineffective and malodorous
review: I did not expect to open the bottle and find that it was a wide-open design and thus easily spillable. I have pets (including a very inquisitive and ungraceful cat), so I can't put it in certain places. I did try to put one in the kitchen but a tiny spider on the windowsill nearby is catching more fruit flies than this trap. The smell of vinegar is quite strong and not pleasant, and so far the fly trap hasn't caught a single obnoxious flying anything.

title: Do not recommend
review: This has been put on my counter for over a day. There is not a single fruit fly in it. Definitely would not recommend. Terro traps are much more effective.

title: Very disappointed
review: I finally received this item after a lengthy shipping period. Both bottles had the caps on wrong and all of the liquid was gone, the packaging is wet and smells like the product. Probably left a trail of fruit fly fluid the whole way.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
review: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

title: Caught three flies only. Put your investment elsewhere.
review: I paid almost $8 to catch three flies. My cat would have done a better job. Basically useless did absolutely nothing to solve my problem. I would be investing in something else.

title: Total failure
review: sadly they do not work - don't know why but I was hoping this took care of my problem but not happening - going back to my local hardware store to get the ones that have worked in the past and these are going back to Amazon

title: Junk
review: Don’t waste your money! Not only is this nothing more than vinegar, it is a poor design. The top is just wide open. You have to have small holes so the fruit flies can get in but not out! They were all just hanging out on the popped top diving in for a slurp of vinegar and then resting back on the top. I had more success with a small jar of vinegar with cling wrap poked with a toothpick! China is dumping their junk and Amazon is selling it to us!

title: Doesn’t work.
review: Initially I had high hope for this based on what others were saying. Unfortunately these were a huge let down for me. The design is clumsy at best and is a spill waiting to happen, It’s just a wide open bottle. I have left one out for over a week now where I have an abundance of fruit flies. Not a single fly in it, they’re not even interested in these. Save your money and find a working product.

title: Save Your $ & Make A Trap From A Old Water Bottle & Vinegar!
review: A homemade trap from an old water bottle & vinegar with a few drops of soap works better than this any day! This simply doesn't work. The reviewers that say it does must have some bad infestations or something as I've had this in various locations for several weeks and not ONE fruit fly was captured! I even added some foil over the top and poked a few holes as some suggested and it still is a miserable failure!

title: Odd bottle
review: The bottle is odd designed, unprofessional, unpractical.

title: Don’t waste your money
review: Ineffective, and will not get the job done. You could probably make something better on your own.

title: Ridiculous
review: Do not waste your time nor your money. Zero effectiveness. Nothing else needs to be stated. Have a nice day.

title: Just ACV! Biggest waste of money
review: Biggest rip off ever. This item is literally a plastic spice jar of apple cider vinegar, you could make this for 50 cents in less time it would take to order this with items in your kitchen. Actually unreal that i just paid $8 for this, should have read the ingredients. Was specifically trying to not use apple cider vinegar because it stinks. DO NOT BUY! It doesn’t work very well.

title: Didn't work- not a single fly
review: We've been having a massive Fruit Fly issue and been trying everything we could to get it under control. I had high hopes for these but we've had two of them open for a week now and not a single Fruit fly has gone for these. We've moved them around to different areas of our pantry and kitchen and nothing. We've had better luck with homemade traps using dish soap w/ red wine or cider vinegar. They still aren't managing the situation but at least SOME dead flies have resulted from those.

title: Didn’t work at all
review: I bought a two pack of these….they both collectively caught three gnats. Mind you, I’m having an infestation right now. My own home made ACV and sugar water with dawn dish soap worked way better.

title: Charging for 12 bottles and sending just 1 bottle
review: Ordered the 12 pack for $80 and received just one bottle. Requested a replacement and received one bottle instead of 12 again despite a charge for a 12 pack

title: Don’t waste your time or money!!
review: This was an absolute freaking waste of money. I am so irritated because it was one of those products that really stood out to me, like no way thousands of people are being dishonest and rating it highly consistently. Boy was I wrong. So, I have a summer time issue with fruit flies (due to fruit). Could not get rid of them for anything. I used the katchy, stem spray, and this product. I had my home PROFESSIONALLY cleaned, opened one of these jars, and left for a 2-week vacation. I just knew I would be coming back to a fruit fly free home thanks to this product working it’s magic. No such luck. I’ll stop there, but just take it from me. It is a waste of money, so don’t get your hopes up.

title: Don’t waist your money!!!
review: If I can give zero stars, I would, but it makes me pick at least one. Total waste of money. I’ve worked in the bar industry for years, I’ve seen barflies congregate around the alcohol for years. I bought this product because it said it was specifically formulated for barflies. At the three days only two barflies were caught in the syrup. I decided to buy another product and filled the bottom cup portion with Jim Bean. Within an hour, there was over a dozen flies caught in the trap. Don’t waste your money. This product does not work.

title: sent an open product
review: we were sent a product that was open, spilled all over the bag and one of the containers was missing half the liquid

title: Disappointed
review: I was having an awful problem with fruit flies in the kitchen and dining room. I read about using apple cider vinegar and water or, even better, Flypunch. I had apple cider vinegar on hand so I tried it first and ordered Flypunch on the same day. After two days of using the apple cider vinegar 95% of the fruit flies were gone. The Flypunch arrived and I figured it would clear up the remaining 5%. That was not the case. After three days of using only the Flypunch, two bottles, the fruit flies were back. I pulled out the apple cider vinegar and the next morning the flies were gone. If you want to get rid of fruit flies first try the apple cider vinegar.

title: Aunt Fannies No Catch Punch
review: This product did not work for me! I have had it out for about a week. There were only two fruit flies captured. I purchased another product which seems to have caught the ones that Aunt Fannies fly punch didn't catch. I absolutely wasted my money.

title: More wasted money
review: I purchased Aunt Fannie's fly punch fruit fly trap based on all of the encouraging reviews. More wasted money! It smelled just like vinegar when I opened it and left it out for quite a few days with quite a few fruit flies .They were not interested! I have a picture of the open container of the fly punch next to a tuna fish can filled with regular apple cider vinegar and a few pieces of old fruit. Regular apple cider vinegar caught more fruit flies compared to the fly punch which caught none.

title: Boo..
review: Hasn't caught anything!! It ended up getting knocked over... what a mess!! It smells like vinegar. My son found a DIY recipe online and it's only caught a few but it was free!! I did a thorough cleaning with bleach on counters, floors, and cabinets and it's adequate a noticeable difference for today anyway!! Save your money... or throw it away but don't give it to these people!!

title: Well it didn’t work, also leaked out before I got it…
review: When I say this was the biggest disappointment I have come across in along time, I mean it. Now this worked for my friend and was recommended to me so I thought, trusted review from a trusted person so why not. Yeah no, smell is much stronger than regular soap and apple cider vinegar but I was willing to smell( it in a completely different room mind you) as long as it worked. Received the product and both bottles were leaking all over the Amazon package… oh well moving on. Left it out for a couple of days and didn’t catch one bug, not a gnat, not a fruit fly, only attention it caught was mine cause that smell was STRONG. You would have better luck just making a concoction yourself or buying a big light for gnats and fruit flies- that’s what I did when I returned this. Would not recommend to anyone but my enemy.

title: Not worth it for the price
review: I just don’t like it

title: Good concept but not great results
review: Still waiting. One fruit fly caught. My resolution - take caution using - pouring hot water from the tea kettle down all drains - it eradicates living fruit flies and the eggs if they have laid any in your drains. Haven't seen a bug since! To be sure, I have treated every night before bedtime for 4 days. Total success!

title: Sadness and despair
review: One can came empty. Amazon won’t respond I can’t get the seller to respond. So I pours half the liquid from one into the other and set them out. It’s been two days not a single fruit fly. :( I had high hopes but it really doesn’t work for me.

title: Stinks
review: Stinks and leaking. I don’t know why I expected it to have a way too keep the bugs in, like you do when you set up a home made one. But there’s no way to trap them in.

title: Works BUT see the photos attached and you decide
review: The FlyPunch works, BUT,... I had much better luck with a simple household product that didn’t cost me but a few pennies. Both traps were set at the same time 48-52 hours ago. FlyPunch and a bowl of apple cider Venegar with 2-3 drops of dish soap stirred in. Traps were set 3-4 inches apart on the kitchen window. Pictures attached that shows a massive difference between the 2 traps. I was able to count 8 fruit flies in the FlyPunch and far too many to count in the apple cider vinegar mix Can’t say if the FlyPunch would have worked better with the cling wrap, often saw fruit flies sitting on the rim but not too many died. I simply followed the directions on the bottle and did the same with the apple cider trap I googled. 🤷🏽♂️ Left for Thanksgiving and forgot to throw out the bananas, and Shazam,... lots of fruit flies when we returned. 48-52 hours later 99% are gone. You decide which trap worked better.

title: Didn’t work!!
review: Had high hopes this product would work… But… Not one fruit fly took the bate.. very disappointed!

title: Didn't work for me
review: I bought this product because I began to have fruit flies in my apartment. I wanted something easy, something that didn't require much work, so I thought this would be perfect. Just open and forget it. Well after almost two weeks it only caught two fruit flies, just TWO. I was pretty disappointed. I ended up just buying one of those electrical fan things that have a light that are made to trap fruit flies via the fan down onto a glue board. I ran this for two weeks and caught almost 60! So this fan thing worked way better than this liquid. And to top it off, no refunds are allowed. Very shady in my opinion. If my fan trap caught 60 and this liquid caught 2, then it obviously if faulty and I should have the option to get my money back. Do not waste your money on this product.

title: Toxic. Misleading Amazon description.
review: Sorry I ordered this and it will be going down the drain. The description says it’s “plant-based” and “safe around food”. But the label on the product contains several warnings, including to wear rubber gloves when handling and what to do if it gets on your skin. When it’s set up for use it’s an open bottle, just waiting to tip over. It contains Ethyl Lactate: “Ethyl lactate can be harmful if inhaled or absorbed through the skin. Prolonged contact can irritate the skin and eyes, and breathing it in can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, and passing out. Ethyl lactate is flammable and can cause serious or permanent injury”

title: A 100% useless product
review: Completely useless against gnats (fruit flies)...or any other fly infestation. A total BS product. Don't be fooled!

title: 2 stars because it *does* (sort of) work
review: Otherwise 1. Guys. This overpriced apple cider vinegar with a drip of dish soap. The DIY way works way better. Get a clear up, put a few drops of dish soap in it. Pour in apple cider vinegar so that there is a light "soap lining" over the top. Then cover the glass with well stretched cling wrap. Use a fork to poke s few small holes (easy to get on, hard for them to get out which is a big thing this product misses). The fruit flies smell it and crawl into the holes, ho toward the food-smell and get stuck from the layer of soap. They can't crawl out because of the plastic wrap. Bingo. $1 worth of supplies

title: Easy, it just did NOT work
review: Fruit flies were not attracted to it. Easy to use, just remove the lid. The scent is fine, not even detectable, it is a great concept but the t e r r o apple shaped fruit fly traps work 100x better. I actually even used both in my home at the same time and this container was knocked over (This is easy to knock over & waste ALL) and hardly had any caught fruit flies in it when the t e r r o apples had caught as many flies as they could catch, so the one minute it takes to squeeze the liquid into the little apples is definitely worth it even though this natural product just requires a person to remove a lid. Would not buy again, and I hate that because this product is reasonably priced and easy to use. It just didn't work.

review: I purchased Aunt Fannie's FlyPunch last summer due to an extreme amount of gnats and flies in our home. I felt the product worked extremely well and I knew I was going to buy it again a year later. A year later came, and i purchased 5 of them, one for each room that the gnats usually show up in. I received the 5 and not a single one of them I can get open due to the cap not coming off. I have to take a small flat head screwdriver and pry the cap off and then I'm able to get it off. When I finally get it off it also rips part of the seal off as well, so it makes a mess getting the liquid inside all over. I'm not sure if this was a production error or it's a problem with the new design of the product. But I've got to say I'm pretty disappointed this time.

review: I bought these because the description on the web site really seemed promising. I put them where we get these damn fruit flys. Bathroom sink, a few areas in the kitchen. review: My house has become infested with these stupid little fruit flies/drain flies/gnats whatever you want to call them. I have tried the homemade DIY traps and they catch some but not enough. I’m putting a pic of how many it caught. But keep in mind I still have them everywhere. And I stopped buying fresh fruit a couple months ago to try to help the situation(which it did improve but I miss fruit). Overall I would buy it again but there has to be a better way, a permanent way, to get rid of these things!!! Every time I purchase something online, I always check the reviews. I count on others to help me choose the best option. My reviews are always my honest opinion and I try to include photos if possible. review: I received the fly punch September 8, 2022. I have a bad fruit fly problem and opened it up and stuck it on counter along with a homemade fruit fly trap I made from cutting a plastic cup in half and placing a loose lid on top. I used Braggs organic apple cider vinegar and Palmolive dish soap but do not mix. You can use any dish soap. The pictures I shared are all 6 days. The Fly Punch has a couple of fruit flies and the homemade one has tons. I feel I wasted my money on this and the description made the fly punch sound appealing as to why I bought it. Thinking it would work better then homemade. Homemade is the way to go.

review: We have had really bad fruit flies in our area and I made this trap with a mason jar and within a few hours, all these flies were caught. title: Does not attract fruit flies more than other liquids
review: I'm offended that I paid money for this. First, it's no better than laying out some apple cider vinegar out. Second, it will only work if you're super diligent about removing all other standing water sources: dry sink area, no plants retaining water in soil, no cups/pots with standing liquids, etc. I kept one by my kitchen sink and only caught 1 fruit fly over 5 weeks. Another was in an isolated grow room with visible fruit flies -- it only caught 2. I killed more with my bare hands by snatching them out of the area each time I was near these so called "trap". Honestly, this product is overpriced vinegar evaporating on my window sill. I won't be purchasing again.

title: Live and learn
review: I’ve waisted my money on a few things in life And this is definitely one of them it would not attract a fruit fly much less catch one !

title: No flies were trapped
review: Had high hopes but flies either never went in or just didn’t get trapped. They seemed to fly around it but didn’t go in. We have had it on our counter for a couple of weeks now. Agree with other reviews that perhaps the bottle design isn’t the best for trapping. It does smell like it is just strong vinegar. The smell was strong at first but weaker now. I will continue my search for fruit fly traps. Maybe the flies have now evolved to outsmart the vinegar traps.

title: Waste of money
review: First of all I only received two of the three bottles that were supposed to come in the package. I had a terrible fruit fly infestation when I bought these, so I used what came out of desperation and didn't return them. These were a waste of money. There were literally hundreds of bugs in my kitchen and maybe 10 flew into these, and I put them where I saw the highest concentration of them. Standing in my kitchen with the vacuum hose/wand in my hand for half an hour at a time (several sessions of this) was the only way to get rid of the infestation.

I usually use the Terro apples, but I wanted to try a more economical solution but this didn't work at all. My homemade trap has caught bunch, I just don't know if I got a bad batch or what?

review: I had high hopes for Aunt Fannies flypunch… but it didn’t get rid of the fruit flies. We had what seemed to be 5-10 fruit flies this summer… driving us insane. I was so hopeful that this flypunch would do the trick to get rid of them. Nope they would land on the lid, but that was it. I never saw one fruit fly that had gone for a swim in the punch. Smells just like apple cider vinegar. It’s in a bottle that spices would come in, so size is ok but the flies were not convinced and neither was I. I would probably not order this one again.

title: Waste of my money...
review: Purchased this for fruit flies, it seems to attract them only....they walk along the rim of the opened container but nothing happens! Except for the fact that they get bigger!!! Waste of my money.🤬

I don’t know if the viscosity of the vinegar is also a problem but in the current design it only appears to be working because they breed in it. Within two days the number of flies had doubled, today at one week I’m throwing them all out because I’m getting pelted by flies flying into me randomly all day.

I got one of those battery-operated fly eliminators that look like a tennis racket, thinking I could get them right at the door, but I'm not fast enough. We tried sticky fly paper, which works quite well, but it isn't attractive. I thought we'd give this a try. In four days, it hasn't attracted a single fly. There is nothing in containers. I got six. I put two out. I'm very disappointed because these containers sure look better than fly paper. I will update if there's any change but so far, not one fly...

review: We had a lot of fruit flies upon returning from vacation. We tried these traps and caught only two flies with them in two weeks! The jars do not have any way to trap the flies, the lid is wide open, and this is a flaw of design. If the lid had smaller holes in it, the flies would get trapped in there. The flies fly into these traps and do not stay there--whatever is in it does not attract or kill them. We got rid of our fruit flies using yellow sticky glue traps and other liquid fruit fly traps that have a better attractant and design to keep the flies trapped. And also good old-fashioned home-made vinegar, water, dish soap traps helped--with a dash of apple-cider vinegar as attractant or small piece of fruit in it.

title: Trap Doesn't Attract Flies, Spills, Improvement required - Trap Parts Potentially Useful for DIY
review: Trap Doesn't Catch Flies & Spills Unavoidably! Have been using for over a month - haven't caught a single fly (but have other traps that catch smaller flies just fine). This Trap is really no different from small vinegar based fly traps, but is intended to catch larger flies. The flies are supposed to enter the top grid (should be attracted to the weak detergent mixture inside as it smells like weak vinegar which they like), and are supposed to fall into the dilute detergent mixture in the packet sitting inside, which would kill them. But not only did flies seem to be completely not attracted, unfortunately, but the packets are shaped such that you can't attach or remove the grid/lid, without one side of the detergent packet snaps on the legs of the lid, and spills as you open it. So you end up with much less liquid in the trap, which will dry out quickly. I will be trying out my own apple cider vinegar solutions to try to improve the attraction rate, and possibly will add a small amount of detergent, though that may not be required (will require testing), as there seems to be a real gap in the market for a small non-toxic liquid based trap like this, for larger flies (there are plenty of effective vinegar traps for the small flies already). These traps will be worthwhile if I can at lease reuse the casings ... but not sure I can even get that to work yet.

title: Waste of money
review: Absolutely useless. The little tubs that hold the liquid are made of the thinnest of plastic, and every single tub was warped, causing it to sit lopsided in the hard case. I spilled some liquid on my hands, and honestly, it just smells like pure vinegar. I mean, maybe there’s some sort of pheromone or chemical in there but it’s not effective. Every summer, the flies are so bad in my area. I’ve had these tubs sitting on my windowsills for three days now. I placed them there because that’s where a lot of the flies gravitate to, but it hasn’t caught a single one. Save your money, and invest in a good flyswatter. I suggest a metal one. Oh, and stay away from those little zapping paddles because I tried that too. All it did was knock the fly out for literally five seconds. Hardly enough time to finish the job before they regain their senses and fly away.

review: I bought these traps to put in my kitchen and bathrooms. In our kitchen, we tend to get fruit flies around our coffee machine. In the bathroom, we get them around the sinks, as they come out of the overflow drains and like to hang around my potted plants. These come in a 6-pack, which includes 6 small plastic cases and 6 single-use solution tubs. To setup, you take on plastic case, and one solution tub. Peel the sealed cover off of the solution tub, drop it into the case, and put the lid on the case. From there, you just place it in the area where you notice flying insects. The solution looks unremarkable, visually, but smells slightly of vinegar. After these had dried up, it looked somewhat goopy, but still smelled of vinegar. Putting a bit of water into the solution tub quickly reconstitutes the solution. Given this, I believe the solution is nothing more than vinegar, water, and soap, which is the recipe for a DIY fruit fly trap, but in a MUCH smaller scale. The first night I put these out, I caught a single fruit fly in the bathroom, which made me very hopeful that these were to solution to my problem. Unfortunately, these seem to be absolutely ineffective, as that first fruit fly I caught has been THE ONLY fruit fly I’ve caught, even though you can see them flying around these things. I’m not sure if the solution is too weak, too small amount, or just not an effective solution in the first place. Given that I’ve had these in place for months at this point, and have only caught one single fly, which I believe was a complete fluke, I have to come to the conclusion that these are a complete sham that do absolutely nothing, which the company probably knows, but still decides to cash in on people needing a real solution. Overall, these are a major disappointment, and I would not recommend these to anyone.

If i relied upon the Hot-Shot traps alone I wouldn't have a full undestanding of my overall gnat problem.

The trap contains a liquid that easily spills, so you have to be careful to place it where it isn't at risk of being knocked over (away from kids and kitties, for example). I placed on of these traps on our kitchen countertop behind the sink and next to prime gnat real estate over ten days ago, but so far, it hasn't caught a single critter. This morning I saw a gnat hovering close to it and thought, "ok, today is the day the fly trap will do its thing." But I checked a few hours later, and still--not a single captured critter. This trap only has a couple more days to perform (the directions say to replace them every two weeks), but I am not too optimistic that I will suddenly see a different outcome from what I've experienced to date.
