title: Day Spa for Fruit Flies
review: First, the product is not that easy to use. The instructions say to shake well before opening, but it creates a layer of foamy bubbles that take about 15 minutes to dissolve. While the bubbles are present, the fruit flies don't go anywhere close to it. Then the whole product is a jar of some vinegar liquid that is just supposed to be left open on the counter 24 hours a day until all the flies are trapped. It's really easy to tip/spill every where and at 5.4 fl oz, it makes a mess. Second, the scent is awful. It smells like a jar of vinegar (which I could have poured without spending money on this product) and it permeates a 5' radius of where it's located. We kept trying to figure out what was leaking before we realized it was the fruit fly trap. Third, the fruit flies think it's a day spa! They land on the rim and dip down to the top of the liquid, but don't actually fly in the trap. They just chill out around it like we've created a resort for them instead of exterminating. We have other Stem products and love them, but this one was an epic fail!

Little bugs are still flying around, so far doesn't look like a single bug has gone into this stuff and it stinks to high heaven. The only thing it's done is change color from the clear look when opened to a honey color (as mention in the directions). Bear in mind I have very few little bugs (usually only "maybe" 1 or 2 in the house but they are still annoying. Since I have this stuff, as long as the stink doesn't drive me totally bonkers I'll leave it and see what happens but I'm not optimistic at this point. I would have expected at least 1 little flying bug to have at least landed on the rim of this container instead of trying to land on my breakfast. Some people say it takes a couple of days to work so I guess we'll see.

title: I was extremely dissappointed in this product
review: I read the directions twice and it is very simple. Shake real good before opening then unscrew the lid off and peel off the protective foil. Then just leave it sitting out on a counter or whatever, near where the fruit flies or gnats seem to be the worse. I would watch the fruit flies crawl all over this product kinda checking it out but it seemed they would always lose interest and go away instead of going for the liquid to get trapped. Now to be fair, I may have caught close to 50 after a couple weeks but when I saw it wasn't working to well, I broke out some fly ribbon paper I had leftover in an old box and the fly ribbon was absolutely covered with them so I won't be wasting any more money on traps like this when I can get 10pc of fly ribbon paper for real cheap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. If you don't like using fly paper then do one of the DIY tricks from youtube with a plastic cup, apple cider, and a bit of saran wrap.

title: Mostly effective, and for German roach nymphs
review: These have been somewhat effective. While I have seen less of these pests when I've got this active, I've also seen them literally just hangout on top of the apple. It's like it can see its dead incestuous disgusting family in the goo and it actually takes it as a warning to not proceed. Perhaps I should stop reusing the same trap...Once this stuff runs out, the pests start right back up again. Not as dense as before, but it is noticeable. I'd rather have this than nothing, that's for sure.I wish this came with way more of the liquid. I feel like I have too many apples and not enough liquid. This seller doesn't appear to sell the liquid in bulk, you just have to buy more traps, which is annoying.I also prefer filling it way more than it suggests because if I fill it less, then I have to replace it more frequently. Ergo, providing more of the liquid would be far more useful.This does emit a faint smell, but I've found that it only smells when I'm directly above it.Make sure to tell your guests or family that this thing can spill if you pick it up wrong.I'd ideally rate this maybe 3.5 stars. It works well enough to keep the pests down, but it's not a permanent solution and they don't always fall for the trap.Update: I've changed my mind. Solid 4 stars. I noticed German roach nymphs wading dead in the liquid. I've been keeping these near my sink because that's where the fruit flies hang out. It appears as though the roaches, while trying to get a drink in the sink, find the fruit fly trap and want in. I have a small infestation of roaches in my place, so if they don't fall for one trap, I'm glad they'll fall for another. I don't like having roach traps on my counter due to the chemicals used, so this much-less-poisonous-to-humans trap is a great alternative.

title: So disappointed! No longer recommend. Seller never responded.
review: FRUIT FLY SEASON IS RAPIDLY APPROACHING AND I'M DETERMINED TO PREVENT LAST SUMMER'S INFESTATION. Update : I contacted the company multiple ways and multiple times.Amazon and the company totally ignored my legitimate complaint.  Obviously they don't care about their customers dissatisfaction. It's not about the money - it's about blatant misrepresentation and unethical behavior displayed by both companies. I couldn't even get Amazon to include the "frequently returned" box on the item's page.I bought  three bottles of auntie's product on Amazon 6 days ago to replace my DIY liquid attractant of appl cider vinegar +brown sugar +dish detergent.It's been 5 days and can confirm the other negative reviews that the product CAN'T contain the same liquid attractant - the fruit flies feed on the liquid and are not trapped - they can fly away!!!I unintentionally performed a side by side experiment using this WORTHLESS product against my attractant. Both liquids were placed next to separate hanging cylinders of bright yellow sticky fly paper.I actually watched the flies fly from the  auntie's product into my liquid. Unlike the auntie product, any flies that were not trapped in my DIY liquid were trapped in the fly paper.After 5 days I had to replace the fly paper adjacent to DIY liquid. in contrast, the 3 bottles of Auntie containing who knows what had A TOTAL OF LESS THAN 20 IN THE BOTTLES AND ABOUT 10 TO 20 TRAPPED BY THE FLY PAPER.I am so angry about wasting money on products from Amazon with good reviews. This product has overall rating of 3.8. But that rating is CUMULATIVE - The much older reviews are generally positive compared to more current negative reviews. I conclude this is due to a change in formulation that neither amazon or the seller made clear.I was so pleased that Good Housekeeping had recommended the best way to eliminates fruit fly infestations in a recent article.  The GH panel incorrectly included this product as the only commercially effective liquid attractant since it contained malic acid as part of the formulation. TheFRUIT FLY SEASON article made me remember that I had used Aunties successfully a few summers ago and loved their esthetics and effectiveness.I already emailed a request for them to provide evidence of its effectiveness using a recent bottle.I am requesting a refund from this seller based on my results and will update the status with both responses.Meanwhile if you are battling with fruit flies, infestations made worse by the higher temperature (I live in Connecticut) in the Northeast, read below.First understand that you must use the following steps throughout the fruit fly lifecycle (over several weeks so that the original fruit flies are trapped as well as the their progeny hatched from the hundreds of larvae deposited on whatever they fed on. {I am a biochemist and patent attorney so I needed to know what was going on}.Keep in mind for DIY solutions or other traps that you must attract and rid them from escaping. Otherwise you'll have dead flies near and flying around the attractant.A single fruit fly will deposit hundreds of larvae on fruit and vegetables and existing food sources.Follow these steps :1. Clean all surfaces daily with your typical all purpose cleaner (I use Fantastic with bleach) wherever you find these annoying bugs. For us this is primarily the kitchen in addition to the bathroom and TV room.REMEMBER THEY ARE ATTRACTED TO LIGHT AND 1 FLY WILL DEPOSIT EGGS THAT MATURE IN about 5 to7 DAYS.2. Unfortunately surface cleaning every 1-2 days is necessary to eliminate flying flies you see and larva that will hatch that you can't.3. Immediately thoroughly wash all fruit and vegetables (existing or new) and refrigerate.4. Eliminate All food debris from kitchen counters, microwave, garbage cans, toaster oven,  pet water and food bowls, etc. and keep everything covered or washed like used knives, glassware and plates.5. If you think this is drastic like I did, then you will see an infestation that feels as if those little things won...6. in the article, Good housekeeping recommended this product as using malic acid which is found in apple cider vinegar.  It was part of discussion on using a DIY solution see ingredients above. Any solution must also contain a detergent which causes the flies eating on the attractant  liguid to sink in the solution. They can't fly away and begin a new cycle of depositing eggs. At the beginning of the infestation I used the ingredients above along with standing/hanging yellow sticky fly paper I also bought from Amazon.I am very frustrated that I didn't do the research and work upfront instead of wasting money trying to find the non-existent magic bullet all summer!! title: Works but shouldn't be your only method
review: I had a bad infestation of fruit flies, worse then I have ever experienced this year. Fruit flies can come into your house on produce or they can develop in your drains. The product does work but if you have an infestation of fruit flies you must use several methods to exterminate them which takes time and patience.1. Throw ALL food you keep on your counters. This not only includes fruit but any other food you keep out. Fruit flies are attracted to fermenting foods. I had a mesh bag full of onions in my lazy Susan that I had to throw out because I found the flies in the bag.2. Deep clean your entire kitchen. The fuit flies continue the reproduce because they are laying their eggs on surfaces that are dirty. They can lay up to 500 eggs a day so if the adults keep having places to land aka fruit and sticky surfaces they will continue to reproduce. This means taking out everything on your counter and spraying with a cleaner solution.3. Last but not least, you need to find the source! Fruit flies can breed in your kitchen drain. This means using a solution to pour down the drain to kill the flies and eggs. There is solutions sold on Amazon that can be used. This needs several treatments and ensure your sink is always clean.In conclusion, you can get ride of fruit flies but it takes time. For me it took about 2 weeks. If you only use this trap, its just catching the flies but they will still reproduce if you don't give them a place to breed. Along with these traps, I made my own with apple cider vinegar. I deep cleaned my kitchen and bought the solution used to treat the sink for flies. One you kill the breeding ground, you just continue to set traps until the last adults are gone.Good Luck!

title: Only thing that worked!!
review: For some reason, this summer was bad for fruit flies at our home. We also had an invasion of these strange flies that looked like mini house flies whose wings folded completely over their bodies... no idea what they were.Anyhoo, the long and short of it is that I watched a $÷!+ ton of TikTok videos and tried what seemed like a gazillion "fruitless" methods of ridding my home of the Amityville Horror invasion of flies. None of them worked.  I purchased fly strips that were allegedly scented to attract flies, apparently they dont smell appealing to these flies. I purchased sticky fly boards, I think I caught approximately 12 fruit flies as I frustratedly swung the board through the cloud of flies on my way to deposit it in the trash we had moved outside in a bid to mitigate the buggers.I remembered seeing this advertised late last winter when I purchased some Aunt Fannie's carpet fresh and I searched Amazon until I found it. My mom lives next door and she was under attack as well so I purchased a 2 pack!Fast forward to the arrival and within an hour of me putting this fly ninja stuff out I had trapped and drowned more flies than I had in the entire month of TikTok tries and strips/boards combined!It's a jar of vinegar and perhaps soap? I put it on the window sill above my sink and they dip in for a looky loo and never come out!Well worth the price to find that apple cider vinegar really does lure those flying germ spreaders in!Hands down the best at riding my house of both types of flies and I will purchase again! They worked equally well for my mom and she says she is purchasing the next 2 pack we need ;)

title: Has an effect over time, just not immediately
review: Smells like an open jar of red vinegar.  No film to trap flying insects in the solution,  They basically sit on top of the open jar & nothing precludes the insect from flying away. title: Highly Effective Way to Deal with Fruit Flies
review: This is by far the most effective solution for fruit flies that I have found, and I have tried several. The flies are attracted by the odor of the liquid and fall into it, and they're done! It's easy to use -- just pop open the cap and leave it in the problem area.

title: Better than homemade
review: Texans know that summer means fruit-fly season, and these twerps are difficult to get rid of! I’ve made my own apple-cider and vinegar traps, but these bottles work way more effectively! title: NO MORE FLIES
review: This product works without any mess. Simply open jar, flies are attracted and fall into liquid . Simply close jar and discard.  No more flies !

title: Amazingly effective!
review: We've been having a serious fruit fly/gnat infestation for years, and I'm almost positive they're breeding somewhere in our walls, floors or ceilings -- we've had leaks in the past, and I think we still do. So while it may take more than a trap to eradicate the gnat population here, this trap has brought us substantial relief, in just the span of 2-3 days.We can't call in the professionals at this point, for reasons I can't go into, but since the weather got warmer this spring, life in our small apartment was becoming unbearable. They were flying into our faces, landing on us, and landing in or on our food, even as we prepared it or ate it.I don't think it's been more than 48 hours, and there are A LOT of dead flies in the trap.We've caught substantial numbers with both homemade vinegar traps and the electronic Katchees, but this trap seems to summon the gnats, even from other rooms of the apartment (the trap is in the bedroom, but we also have a combination kitchen/LR, a bathroom and a foyer).Be warned, the trap does have a strict vinegar smell that wafts around, but the smell is NOTHING in comparison to the nuisance of the gnats.They do hang around the rim of the trap for a while, but then they definitely fly into it and die. We put it in an awkward place, and I don't want to take the chance of spilling it, so I can't get anything close to a count, but not only can I glimpse a large quantity of dead gnats, but I haven't seen ANY flying or landing anywhere else in our place, in many hours. This is truly amazing.I don't expect that it will eradicate them completely, because we don't know the breeding source, but one can always hope that all breeding adults will eventually fly around and find this thing. Until then, we may have to keep replacing the traps and finding ways to stretch out the liquid. Maybe we'll post an update, at some point.Meanwhile, I THANK GOD for the blessing of having this trap to control the terrible nuisance that was making our lives so unpleasant and difficult.Posting this update about 2-3 weeks later -- unfortunately in the warm weather (and we don't have air conditioning), these gnats are multiplying faster than the trap can catch them. Without it, we'd probably be swamped in gnats, fruit flies and whatever all these pests are. We'll have to put more traps around.

title: Day Spa for Fruit Flies
review: First, the product is not that easy to use. The instructions say to shake well before opening, but it creates a layer of foamy bubbles that take about 15 minutes to dissolve. It's really easy to tip/spill every where and at 5.4 fl oz, it makes a mess.Second, the scent is awful. It smells like a jar of vinegar (which I could have poured without spending money on this product) and it permeates a 5' radius of where it's located. We kept trying to figure out what was leaking before we realized it was the fruit fly trap.Third, the fruit flies think it's a day spa! They land on the rim and dip down to the top of the liquid, but don't actually fly in the trap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. title: Super Ninja Fruit Fly Traps: bait useless for my fruit flies while Terro brand bait has worked well.
review: I tried 3 different brands of liquid fruit fly attractant: in this home for 25 yrs but had never had a fruit fly problem in my life, they must have come in w/fruit which we don't buy a lot of: found out one female lays 500 eggs...This product, Super Ninja Fruit fly traps- I put several of these pre-filled bottles out for days but SUPER NINJA FRUIT FLY TRAPS DID NOT CATCH A SINGLE FRUIT FLY, compared to Terro brand used in the red plastic tomatoes, which worked well. I even tried the Super Ninja bait in the red Terro plastic tomatoe containers as some ads claimed the color + shape of the vessel played a role in attracting bugs but still no luck. The excellent Terro brand even worked well in a clear glass baby food jar.Terro works well, I see several of the fruit flies in the liquid. However, the tomatoe shaped plastic holders can tip easy, its a sticky, stinky liquid for which the company in South America would not tell me if it has a percent of poison in it- many of their products do, + they only give the number of poison control, + insist that the formula is 'proprietary information'. But after trying 3 brands, will stick w/Terro even though it does not sell a large container of liquid (I do not need more plastic tomatoe holders  plus glass baby food jars worked just as well)Have put the Terro liquid bait-filled plastic tomatoes in clear plastic cups (clear so insects could see the red fruit shape), as the tomatoes have many preferations, which is good, but they are light-weight, tip + spill easily.However, the flat rectangular shape of the bottles of the Super Ninja Fruit fly Traps, though the liquid they came with is useless, the bottles w/their flat walls can be attached to any flat surface or wall w/a sticky strip; That had been my intent when I ordered them so I did not have to worry about containers spilling or space to put them down in or my cat getting to one... As the Ninja contents have proved useless, I will empty + rinse them out so I can fill them w/Terro attractant. will report if the insects will use these glass containers.While I had planned to take advantage of the flat walls of the Ninja glass containers + a photo in the Ad may have suggested they could be stuck to a wall, I was surprised that they came w/a pre-attached silicone sticky strip pre-attached for that purpose (one should use a spatula to remove the sticky strip and bottle intact from the wall (they are silicone w/adhesive + residue can be easily removed).There was one other brand of 25 vials which also did not catch a single fruit fly- even when used in Terro's tomatoe shape, which I also do not recommend, 'Qualirey 20 Pack Fruit Fly Trap Refill Liquid'...Do not recommend the Super Ninja Fly Traps because the bait does not work, at least for my fruit flies in Connecticut; but I still need to substitute Terro liquid bait in their their rectangular glass containers a+ see if the insects will then use them before I formally recommend the containers themselves- they have a yellow funnel on top. However, $39.99 plus tax is a high price to pay for the 12 glass containers which I will need to empty out to use with Terro brand liquid- if the bugs will use that container w/Terro bait.

title: Completely Ineffective
review: I bought these traps to put in my kitchen and bathrooms.  In our kitchen, we tend to get fruit flies around our coffee machine.  In the bathroom, we get them around the sinks, as they come out of the overflow drains and like to hang around my potted plants.These come in a 6-pack, which includes 6 small plastic cases and 6 single-use solution tubs.To setup, you take on plastic case, and one solution tub.  Peel the sealed cover off of the solution tub, drop it into the case, and put the lid on the case.  From there, you just place it in the area where you notice flying insects.The solution looks unremarkable, visually, but smells slightly of vinegar.  After these had dried up, it looked somewhat goopy, but still smelled of vinegar.  Putting a bit of water into the solution tub quickly reconstitutes the solution.  Given this, I believe the solution is nothing more than vinegar, water, and soap, which is the recipe for a DIY fruit fly trap, but in a MUCH smaller scale.The first night I put these out, I caught a single fruit fly in the bathroom, which made me very hopeful that these were to solution to my problem.  Unfortunately, these seem to be absolutely ineffective, as that first fruit fly I caught has been THE ONLY fruit fly I’ve caught, even though you can see them flying around these things.  I’m not sure if the solution is too weak, too small amount, or just not an effective solution in the first place.Given that I’ve had these in place for months at this point, and have only caught one single fly, which I believe was a complete fluke, I have to come to the conclusion that these are a complete sham that do absolutely nothing, which the company probably knows, but still decides to cash in on people needing a real solution.Overall, these are a major disappointment, and I would not recommend these to anyone.

So you end up with much less liquid in the trap, which will dry out quickly.I will be trying out my own apple cider vinegar solutions to try to improve the attraction rate, and possibly will add a small amount of detergent, though that may not be required (will require testing), as there seems to be a real gap in the market for a small non-toxic liquid based trap like this, for larger flies (there are plenty of effective vinegar traps for the small flies already). The 1st day I noticed that this didn’t work, then I tried putting apple cider vinegar next to the traps and I feel that helped the gnats accidentally fly in to the trap. Next I tossed the light and stuck the sticky sheets directly on the apple cider vinegar cup side and that worked well.

review: Not a single fruit fly so far, and we have a lot in our house right now. Would not buy this. UPDATE: I originally gave this 1 star. For whatever reason, this did not work in our kitchen where we have the most fruit flies. But it works great in our bathroom. I think it may work better on a white wall because it shines brighter. But I also taped a white piece of paper on the backsplash shown in the attached picture (that’s before I taped the paper) and it still didn’t work great in our kitchen. I think it’s worth the price to try this device, as we also purchased a Zevo and have been disappointed so far.

Basically just a light with a very small piece of sticky paper directly behind the light. It sounds good in theory. I'll continue to leave it plugged in and see what happens. I noticed flies in front of my door leading into the house. I don't see anything in the vicinity that would be attracting them. If one makes it into the house I'll see what happens with this product.

title: Not so easy to use and doesn't attract many bugs
review: I found this product not to be as good as others and I won't be using it again. It is difficult to get the sticky paper into the slot and the blue light doesn't seem to attract as many bugs as other brands do that I have used. Live and learn.

title: Alright insect trap
review: It has been working well to catch all the small flying insects, and I’ve even managed to catch a few flies with it.

title: Sticky to use but works okay
review: That’s are sticky to use and easy to get stuck on your fingers. Doesn’t really attract little fruit bugs or flies well unless they just happen to land on them. Probably would not purchase again unless I had a major flying insect issue.

title: The sticky cards work great
review: These plug ins weren't attracting the flies so I took another reviewer's advice and put a little sweet wine in a pint glass and laid the sticky cards across the rim of the glass and that worked great! The fruit fly issue was under control within 24 hrs. and eliminated by 72. If I could, I would buy a box of the sticky cards, as the UV plugs were useless for me. I tried using packing tape with the wine/glass trick with no luck. Not sticky enough. Plus, the sticky cards have something that attracts pests.

title: Did not work for me
review: They do light up. They are sticky. But my fruit flies will not land on them. I don't know why. Returned these and bought another brand, which is working a bit better.

title: Doesn’t do much on it’s own, has a good aesthetic
review: I’m appreciative of the fact that I have something ready to catch the fruit flies around my home, though I’ve noticed it only catches the super tiny ones and not the larger fruit flies. Most of the time I unplug it from the wall and wave it over the fly to catch it in its stick pad and that’s how I’ve caught 75% of the insects pictured. Outside of the light, theres nothing really special that draws the flies to the trap so I would think about pairing it with an apple cider vinegar trap to lure them in and hope they get stuck in the trap. The video included is how I catch them manually. It seems seem for animals and children and does not emit any smell. As far as quality, I rate it 1-2 stars as a standalone device, 3 stars is because with my fly catching idea, at least it is catching something. It almost makes me want to buy just the refills and have them on standby to catch on my own. I did expect more out of the quality coming from the Zevo brand. It does not kill the bugs, it just makes them stuck until they die. I’ve had this for about 2 - 3 weeks and this is all it’s caught (small bugs on it’s own, larger flies with my assistance).

title: Works, Careless Packaging, A Bit Overpriced
review: I’ve ordered this item twice because it does the job and is much more pleasant than fly tape. 3 stars out of 5 because you’re paying for the light bulb and overall aesthetic. My 2nd delivery arrived in a large plain paper envelope; the product box was somewhat crushed and the device was cracked. The plug was rendered loose but since the bulb was not broken and the overall device still worked I didn’t want to hassle with exchanging it. So it’s an OK solution but is spendy to continually replace, plus depending on packaging, it may or may not arrive damaged.

title: Not 100% effective- probably 50-60% for fruitflies.

title: Zevo Flying Insect Traps & 2 Refill Cartridges (first and second version)
review: My two‑star rating reflects an average between the first and second versions of the Zevo trap, because the two products performed very differently. First Version – No Longer Available, and Misleading The original version is no longer listed, so I can’t leave a review specifically for it. If I could, it wouldn’t get more than one star. The main reason I bought it was the claim that it also worked for mosquitoes. After using it for a year and a half, I can confirm that this was completely false. It catches plenty of other flying insects, but never mosquitoes, which made the original purchase pointless for my needs. Second Version – Accurate Description, Works Properly The updated version no longer claims to trap mosquitoes—likely removed after customer complaints. And this time, the product performs exactly as described. For the insects it lists, it works reliably, and I would normally rate this version five stars on its own. Final Rating Logic Because I can’t leave a separate review for the discontinued first version, and because the original misleading claims were the reason I bought the product in the first place, I’m forced to average the experience. I can’t give 2.5 stars, so I’m leaving 2 stars to reflect the accurate performance of the new version and the misleading marketing of the old one.

title: Gnat Busters
review: I gave Zevo these two out of five stars because this trap only catches 2 out of 5 Gnats. I placed two devices where Gnats love to gather. One in the Kitchen, One near the bathroom. I check every day, as I also kill Gnats by hand every day. I have a very clean home; I use a garbage disposal and do not store food that can rot in the kitchen bin. I store all fruit and vegetables in the refrigerator. Yet every time that I leave a door or window open for fresh air, these little critters gather. (Even with screens). I have tried everything. But this was the most expensive and least successful. I will return to flying insect sprays. I do not know what so called "Genius" thought that insects like "blue light." But I do know, he/she is not very intelligent. I also have 2 blue light/ light bulbs, that are also zappers... also no results. My recommendations, keep a clean house, wash and dry all fruit and vegetables and store them appropriately, (never store fruit or any food in open air). And my latest discovery... If you use a citrus dish cleaning liquid, keep the bottle clean and the top tight. It is weird, but I have recently discovered that Gnats are attracted to the artificial scent.

title: It just didn't attract the flying insects as much as was advertised, especially for the price.
review: It's basically expensive fly paper. The blue light is supposed to attract flying bugs and it does - but only mildly. The height of fruit fly season runs from August to October. There were so many fruit flies in my house, it was hard to have a conversation without waiving the little buggers away. Enter Zevo - which I have seen being advertised aggressively on TV as being the greatest flying insect eradicator ever. So I shelled out the money for 2 blue lit insect traps and 2 refill cartridges, assembled, plugged in and sat back waiting for the fruit fly fog to clear. It never did. I broke down and added 2 bowls filled with Apple Cider Vinegar, topped with tightly covered saran wrap, poked some tiny holes in the wrap and watched to see what worked better. Scot 1 for the Apple Cider Vinegar. I collected 100x more fruit flies in 2 days than I did the entire time I had the cartridges plugged in. The blue lights are pretty - I'll give it that. But it's passively effective, not aggressively effective, so I'll continue to use my tried and true, albeit kinda gross, method.

title: More bug nightclub than bug graveyard.
review: It’s gnat season, and after yet another round of vinegar pots, I decided to go high tech with these Zevo plug-in traps. I put one upstairs, one downstairs, and waited for the carnage. In practice? Not much carnage. After a month (and a house so thick with gnats you could smack them out of the air just walking by), I’ve caught… maybe 15. I watch the bugs chilling in the blue light like it’s happy hour, but they refuse to land on the sticky trap. Maybe my gnats are too smart, maybe my walls are extra tasty, or maybe I’m just more attractive than UV. Whatever it is, these things aren’t worth the money or the hassle of a bright blue beacon glowing 24/7 on both floors of my house. To be fair: The design is pretty cool. The sticky refills are easy to replace, and you don’t have to touch the goo. But I could easily catch more bugs with my bare hands in three minutes than these have snagged in three weeks. If the point is to catch bugs, this thing missed the mark. Unless you’re looking to start your own insect sanctuary, I’d keep looking.

review: Check the review pictures. It catches a bunch of fruit flies, some midges, a couple of mosquitoes, and in my case, one enterprising moth. But despite having a bunch of houseflies in my house and this plug being very visible for almost two weeks, NO HOUSEFLIES CAUGHT. I had a friend that raved about this catching all their flies. And despite what I considered a high price tag for a disposable-cartridge type product I went for it. Because we have a ton of flies (it's fall and I live in a rural area.) About a week after this has been in my kitchen, I also put up a traditional strip of flypaper which now has a dozen flies on it. Still no houseflies in the zevo. I'm on the verge of saying one star, but I'll give it two because it does catch a bunch of fruit flies that I didn't know we're so bad.

title: After using since late last summer till now, Save your money and buy a bug/animal glue pad catcher
review: Purchased this over 6 months ago and have tried them in different rooms, areas, and heights, and I don't see them doing anything great. I had them in a spot for over a month and maybe one or two little noes see em bugs land on one by the door. Flies don't go on them I have watched them land or scurry right around it like it had no interest at all to them. Also, the way it is curved like a quarter moon is so close to the wall when you plug it in I don't think any bugs will go behind the cover then jump onto the pad. Most of the time there is never anything on them after a month even. It reminds me of those ways you catch a mouse glue pad type that is put in with a light. I am going to buy the mouse catch pads and put a night light by it. I think I will have better luck with that or a fly bug strip. And they don't last that long before you have to replace the pad and the price for the couple of replacements is way over priced.

title: Not worth the cost unless you've got a huge flying insect problem
review: My daughter suggested I get this device because she has had very good results at her beach house. These were placed in clear view right behind our fruit basket where we had a ton of the flies, unobstructed. Disappointed for the price.

Might work better in a completely dark space or with a smaller infestation, but for me, it just didn’t do the job. Disappointed overall.

review: So I've officially had these plugged in for 17 days. (A little over 2 weeks) One in the kitchen and one on the wall between the living room and dining room. My apartment is small. The one in the kitchen caught 4 flies so far and the other one caught only 2. While it does it's job, It seems like it's not catching all the flies because there's always some fruit flies lingering in my house. I feel like it's because there are other light sources around. For example when I am working from home I'll see them fly past me while im sitting at my desk or land on my computer screen. If I go in the bathroom and turn on the light, it will fly in my bathroom. My apartment gets natural sunlight, specifically from the living room window which brightens up my apartment so I feel like the flies will naturally just be where the natural sunlight is, not where the blue light is. So I feel like it may only work at night when the blue light is the only light that is on in my apartment and all the lights are turned off. That's just my theory. Anyway, they haven't caught any new flies in the last week, it's still the same flies from the first week on it so idk how to feel about it. I just use my fly swatter whenever I see them since the traps aren't really catching them.

title: It works, but not as well as I would have liked
review: We have/had a gnat problem in our house. First in the kitchen, and then in the bathroom. I bought a bug zapper for the kitchen, which worked well, but scares the heck out of you every time a bug gets zapped. Sam's also had a rotating bug trap that works pretty well. When the gnats moved to the bathroom, there wasn't enough space away from the sink, toilet, or bathtub to put the zapper. I went ahead and bought these traps to plug in there, as well as the spray that Zevo sells. I figured, given the small footprint of the bathroom, the plug-in trap would be perfect. The first night, it caught two gnats, and I thought, "Great, it works!" However, a week later, the same two gnats were in there, and no additional gnats. Another week, same two gnats. For whatever reason, the "night light" lure just didn't bring in any more gnats. I ended up killing the rest of the gnats either with the spray or with a swatter of some type (mostly my hand). Does it work? Sure, yes. Does it work well? Not really, at least not in my case. I did notice that both Sam's and Costco sell these as well, so I'm guessing they have to be popular enough, right?

review: The good: - Refillable sticky cartridges make it modular. - It "can" catch flying insects. The bad: - Game is called luck. You might get lucky to catch a bunch. Or you are unlucky and catch nothing. - Doesn't do much to attract flying insects. That light isn't like the light beam from Wreck-it-Ralph. The what? - It actually works better as a fly swatter catch. Whenever we see a flying insect, we pick this thing up and swipe at it. Works better than just leaving it plugged in 😅 - If that's the case, you are better off wrapping sticky tape and with some of the sticky side up, around a fly swatter at that point.

title: Not worth the price paid
review: Although, it does attract bugs, they are few and far between. Definitely does not attract gnats as we plugged it in right by our sink where the gnat problem is and in the bathroom and made sure to turn all lights off, and still barely caught any. I am very disappointed. These traps were definitely not cheap.

title: Doesn’t seem to be very effective
review: I’m having an issue with fruit flies and I think it’s because I’ve been doing a lot of food prep lately and I have two dogs and leave my patio door open for them to go in and out so I’m trying to figure out where they are coming from because I do my dishes right away The extra star is because it does look very sleek and I like the little light that it has and it looks so much nicer than anything else on the market, but I have shifted it around to four different outlets and I have caught two fruit flies in the past couple weeks… and then I took a piece of tape and looped it around on a popsicle stick and place it in a little glass filled with maple syrup and I caught like 10 more over the past 24 hours so I’m bummed that it didn’t work

title: Add Apple Cider Vinegar to Card
review: Item does work but it is advised that you swab the bait with apple cider vinegar to increase the attractant. Also, unit is plug in and thus might not be movable closer to where bugs might appear. While the light should attract bugs, neither the existing bait card nor the light seems to attract many bugs. Although some bugs do get caught an overwhelming majority fly closer to the garbage unit containing fruit levels and refuse.

title: LFSYS 2pcs. Fruit Fly Traps For Indoors.
review: I ordered this on November 26th & received it on November 29th 2025. One fruit fly trap works the other does not. I haven’t noticed any fruit flies or flying insects collected yet. I’ll have to return because the blue light does not work. I tried different outlets.

title: Could be better
review: I really wanted this to work, but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to the expectations. I set up both devices in my kitchen and bathroom where I’ve been having issues with fruit flies, but after several days, there was barely any sign of flies getting trapped. The UV light seems weak, and the sticky pads didn’t catch much of anything. I followed all the instructions and even moved the devices around to different spots, but the results were still minimal. The design is nice and it’s quiet, which I appreciate, but that doesn’t help much when the fruit flies are still buzzing around. Might work better in a completely dark space or with a smaller infestation, but for me, it just didn’t do the job. Disappointed overall.

title: Does not work for fruit flies
review: The blue light does not attract fruit flies. This product is a waste of money. I placed the sticky pad next to open bottle of apple cider vinegar and caught a few fruit flies as they tried to get to the vinegar. Caught more flies in the open bottle of apple cider vinegar than on the sticky pad.

title: Not for flies
review: I have had a lot of flies in the house this season so I thought this would be a good option. I've had 2 plugged in for over a week and have not caught a single fly. There are a few gnats on the sticky tape but that's it. They are also very expensive for a glorified nightlight. Would not recommend if you are trying to get rid of flies.

title: Don’t attract flies well
review: Does not attract them that well, they don’t seem attracted to the light. Caught 2 flies in a week.

title: Sticky Situation
review: Have an issues with fruit flies in my kitchen and was hoping these would work well. Have 2 outlets in my kitchen. The 1st picture caught very few and had it plugged in for 3 days. I pulled the other 1 out of the outlet and set it on some peppers. Had way better luck doing that! Just get some sticky paper and save yourself some $

title: It's just a white nightlight.
review: It is a white light. Not the traditional blue, as shown, for attracting insects. Also the images are deceptive. READ THE SIZE. The pots and pans would have to be doll house size to be an accurate representation. XD Also this is just an outlet nightlight with sticky film. You could make your own with a cheap night light, some double stick tape, and a clear sheet protector.

title: Buy an electric zapper light instead…
review: They didn’t work..literally popped them in above my trash can (where the problem area was) and I got like 3 in a month… The other got 1 and a mosquito.

title: Garbage for sink flies
review: I had high hopes for this since the reviews were promising. I plugged it in and have had it for 5 days now and it’s not attracted a single insect! And there’s plenty of sink flies roaming around, they today ignore this junk. Save your money on this one

title: Anser the question, Do they work.
review: Received on December 3 and installed, today is December 12th and they have yet to trap or catch a single fruit fly. After day 3 I got out my bowl and filled it 1/2 way with apple cider vinegar, made a cover of aluminum foil punched some small holes in the foil. Since then it has captured 17 fruit flies and the traps still have caught none. If you purchase I hope you have better luck with them than I had.

title: Not effective except as nightlight
review: installed three days ago , and if I were to box it up right now , it would pass for new . the transparent protective pieces were removed and units plugged into outlets, all other lights off at night . NOTHING trapped! going back

title: ….. at least the light is pretty??
review: They make great night lights for children, but that wasn’t what I bought them for 🫠 Not a single fly was caught, these did not work for me at all.

title: Overhyped waste of time
review: Not sure where all these positive reviews are coming from, this product is not good at all. After 2 days, the fruit flies do not fly in this thing, even after putting them next to the sources of infestation and leaving it on all night. 4 of them are strategically placed in the household, and the old Apple cider vinegar trick works 100 times better. Don't fall for the hype; this product, in my opinion, is junk. Just a few here and there landed on the sticky film.

title: Sadly not trapping
review: The fruit fly trap has not capture any in 3 days. They fly near the trap but continue to avoid. I had high hopes for it working

title: Never caught a single one
review: These things suck. For some weird reason I have knats in my kitchen. Kitchen is very clean so I have no idea where they keep coming from. I tried these and haven't caught a single one. It's been a week. I have to use a spray then reclean everything. No food sitting out. All I can think of is they are coming from sink. Even poured bleach in all drains. Guess I'll stick with the kid/pet safe spray.

title: DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY!!!!
review: I bought a pair of these thinking that they would be good and attract gnats instead didn’t attract anything total waste of money

title: It does not work. It does the opposite
review: So I bought this because I have fruit flies in the house. This is a joke. They fly by it I even lured them to the bananas it doesn’t work. I waited a whole day 24 hours. Nothing even at night when that is the only light they see. I wasted my money. I’m researching to see another product that works. There isn’t any smell (I can’t smell anything) and they certainly are not attract it to it. They avoid it because they would normally go to the bananas and if I put them close to the thingy they don’t get near it lol. They should sell it as a repellent not a trap

title: Terrible product.
review: Have had these for a little while now and it doesn't work at all have gnats still not a single one has gone to this trap!!!

title: You can catch more fruit flies with vinegar than you can with ZEVO traps.
review: My garden has been overflowing with tomatoes and summer squash and my counters were accumulating bowls of produce faster than I could can or freeze them. Suddenly I had an infestation of fruit flies. Prior to using ZEVO, I was using an old home remedy for trapping fruit flies. I placed a piece of banana in a jar, covered the opening with plastic wrap, and punched a couple of slits in the plastic wrap. In a second jar I placed pieces of tomato. The fruit flies can get into the jar through the slits but can’t get out. My ZEVO order arrived two days after I set out the jars and I eagerly put the ZEVO traps to work. The next morning I checked the traps. The ZEVO traps had only 5 or 6 fruit flies attached to the sticky trap. The jars which had been sitting out for 2 days, had a dozen or so fruit fries and my counters were still full of flies. The next morning, the ZEVO traps had a few more flies but the jars were full of flies. Now, four days later, the ZEVO traps continue to underperform. I replaced the banana with a little vinegar and it’s like a fruit fly magnet.

title: Did not work for fruit flies- waste of our money
review: So far I am not at all impressed. Not sure how we got them but all of a sudden we had a ton of fruit flies. (Despite no fruit out and rotting. Nothing we could find. Unless they were in the drain….i have no clue where they came from) We did a kitchen and fridge deep clean. We did drain cleaning. Garbage can bleaching. Etc. Bought these. Plugged one in in out kitchen. A few days later…nothing. Not one single fruit fly was caught. Opened and plugged in the second one as well. Two days later….still nothing. I killed more with my hands than these caught. I gave up and called my mom and ended up doing the old wives take ACV and dish soap with plastic wrap and holes in it over it. I have 10 over night that way. Two days later they are all dead in my ACV trap. Too bad these $35 traps couldn’t have caught and killed a single one. Maybe they work better with different bugs than fruit flies but….they absolutely did nothing for us.

title: Zevo fly trap did not work for me
review: Many reviewers praise this fly trap and have had success with it, but my experience has been that the fly trap is very ineffective. I have numerous house flies in my condo, but they ignore the Zevo fly trap and do not seem attracted to the UV light. I have tried placing the fly trap right where the flies are, tried dimming the lights and darkening the room to make the UV light more visible, and have tried moving the trap around to several different locations. None of these approaches work. At the moment, there are approximately 10 flies in my small condo. They fly around and near the trap, but ignore it and do not seem attracted to it at all. For me, this was a fairly expensive investment to help control the flies. I was optimistic it would help based on all the positive reviews, but it did not work for me. I'm already calling it a loss and looking for another alternative.

title: What are you really paying for/ getting?
review: It’s not exactly what it represents is in the box, at least the one I got. Now my box had been torn open, so I may be wrong. Yes there was 2 traps, but no pads were in them, so the 2 “refill pads” actually should be a part of the traps, so no refill pads are part of the package!

title: Don’t waste your money!
review: I’d give it 0 Stars if possible. I’ve had one plugged in one foot from a bowl I keep onions, avocados and other various vegetables from time to time and not one single fruit fly or any other flying insect has found its way too. My roommate and I have each killed a handful during this time. We have another in my bathroom where I am constantly finding a tiny flying insect and it has also not attacked a single one in 10 days!! It is a complete waste of money!!!

title: Old fashioned remedy wins the day and smokes the Flying Insect Traps.
review: Over the course of three days using these in hopes of dealing with an infestation of gnats, the one in the bathroom caught a gnat and a mosquito. Then, someone suggested I simply put some apple cider vinegar in a glass, with a drop of Dawn dish soap, rubber band a cover of plastic wrap and punch some holes in it. I did this in both the bathroom and the kitchen. In two days in the bathroom, I caught six gnats. In the same period in the kitchen, I caught more than I could count - probably 50 or more. The flying insect traps are still plugged in but haven't caught any additional gnats (not too many around since I put out the apple cider vinegar.

title: Glorified Light Light
review: We have lots of gnats flying around in our house. Though this would be better than a bug bomb. We bought the two pack. 2 days and not a single catch. The device does absolutely nothing to attract bugs. I suspect the blue light is just a standard blue LED light. Our old fashioned TAT fly strips are out performing these things at this point. I’m sure one of them will eventually catch a bug, when it happens to fly between the shield and the wall. Until then it looks cool in the dark. * Update * I moved them around the house. I have two Zevos. I’ve had them for just over a month. It total we have captured 4 bugs. In the same amount of time. I’ve killed two with a fly swatter, two with toilet paper and one by clapping my hands. Not super impressed with them. I still think the light is just for show.

title: Manufacture defect
review: Do not get it from this seller it arrived broken. I had inspected the Zevo on arrival and plugged it in and it doesn’t light up because who ever put it together didn’t seat the white outer shell to the gray housing cover. There is an opening between them and I bought a two pack so it’s obvious one light up and the other one doesn’t. It’s so irritating I have to go out of my way and ship it back to them. I wish they had inspected it but it probably was a return and they didn’t even check it when they put it back for sale.

title: Hasn't trapped a single fruit fly. Worthless bright light
review: Bought to combat fruit flies that are constant with having a parrot. Not a single fruit fly has been trapped in either trap. One set in kitchen and the other next to my birds cage. Very disappointed

title: NO TO ZEVO!
review: This product is useless. I returned it and had to take it to staples. They processed the return and I went on my way...my account was charged back because the return wasn't received??? What did staples do with it??? Now I am out 40 dollars and I'm out the worthless product. UPS is the only way to return. Don't buy zevo

title: Did not help with my fly problem
review: I bought this hoping to solve a problem with houseflies. Our place is full of them and I don't know where they are coming from. I have searched and could not find a place where they might be breeding. I didn't rely on just Amazon reviews to buy this. It has reviews all over the net saying that it worked well for the kind of problem I have. When I received this I read the instructions and put it up in an area that is full of flies. It has been up for a couple of weeks and has only caught maybe half a dozen flies. There are still tons of flies zooming around in here doing what flies do. They buzz my face, attack my eyes and mouth, land on my ears and sit there buzzing. I'm still trying to find the source where they are coming from but this product isn't helping. It said it would help me combat houseflies but the flies aren't interested in it. The blue light was supposed to attract them. I don't think it does. I don't know if it works for other flying insects but it does not help with houseflies. I saw reviews that made it seem like a near miracle worker. It is not. Do your research and look beyond review sites before you buy this product.

title: A nice night light.
review: Situation: Fruit flies had gotten out of hand in the kitchen and other parts of the house. Tried other home remedies with mixed results Got the Zevo and well…i’s a nice night light. That’s it. Over the course of around three weeks, sitting in my kitchen, it caught and killed 4-5 fruit flies. It was easy to assemble and set up, but it just didn’t work as expected and especially in regards to price point. Save your money. I was using one of those Terro Apples and a Raid Yellow fly stick (with apple cider vinegar poured in the bottom of it) and this is the order of effectiveness: 1) Raid yellow stick is the best for fruit flies. 2) Terro Apple is effective over the long haul but if you need to kill quickly, it’s Raid. 3) Zevo is shiny and neat looking and it’s a decent night light but it only killed around 3-4 fruit flies and did that mostly at night.

title: Disappointed - did not perform as advertised
review: Had a fruit flie issue. These did not work on them. Had it up for 2 1/2 weeks right by where they were. Didn’t trap a single one. Just pulled out and put in the draw. Made a home remedy that I found on the internet-!: that work way better.

title: Maybe I'm using it wrong, but...
review: I plugged this into my bathroom to take care of a small gnat problem. The next day, I got a letter of complaint from the gnats, saying that the blue light kept them up all night, and could they please get some fresh water? Lovely. And these weren't weird gnats, either. Just garden variety flying insects, the kind it says it will trap.

title: Not a very good /fast solution for trapping fruit flies
review: This product did not work as expected . I was very disappointed the first few day no one Nat was in that tape and it was plugged into the outlet right above my problem area .. I thought the light was meant to attract them and it didn’t I have had it plugged in for a week and I caught maybe a handful .. I bagged all my stuff in ziplock and made an apple cider vinegar with some dish soap and picked holes in plastic wrap over the top and caught twice as many in just two days.. In all the years at my home I had never had fruit flys .. I won’t again now that I know how to contain and prevent it in the summer .. I wouldn’t waist the money on this item ..

title: Did very little for problem
review: Disappointed….only 2 gnats in several weeks…used along with 2 Terro fruit fly traps and which caught 1 gnat in each apple trap. Also tried apple cider vinegar with dish soap in a bowl and that caught 1…seems a waste of $25 total…believe insects came in on houseplant brought in for the winter and have lessened a lot but not in traps. Tried traps because spray was not safe for my cat.

title: It’s ok I guess.
review: Has a nice blue light that probably attracts some bugs and the quality seems good, I got it for a fruit/drain fly issue. It is very sticky but wasn’t effective for the fly issues I had. It may be effective for other pests.

title: Minimally Effective. Not Worth The Price.
review: Overpriced fly paper. I had an outbreak of fruit fries. I bought this in hopes they would be eradicated. Aside from few little soil mites from my plants, not one fruit fly got caught. Vinegar and dish soap concoction was much more effective. Packing tape would probably be as effective at a fraction of the price. Will not purchase again.

title: Waste of money
review: We have a total infestation of fruit flies and in the couple weeks we’ve had it it’s only collected a small amount. We put out homemade vinegar traps, and in one night got three times as much in each vinegar trap. And that was much cheaper. Don’t waste your money. The only reason I’m giving two stars is because it wasn’t completely empty, but they could’ve just ended up on there by chance. The first week or so it only had like 5 on there. Pics show what it looks like after weeks of use. The second photo I will show you how many we got in our vinegar trap in a night and it’s hard to tell how many there actually is in there from the photo.

title: Waste of money
review: I was so excited to get this due to the positive reviews and I was being invaded by small flying insects that bite. After following the included directions and placing the device in the outlet at the end of the kitchen island directly across from the kitchen sink with the trash enclosed underneath. The device has trapped maybe 6 insects at most while I sit on the couch about 6 feet away being swarmed by theses little insects that ARE NOT mosquitoes.

title: It’s alright…
review: It does its job but it might take a while to accumulate flies. I bought this in the summer when I had lots of fruit flies at home. After installation over the 3-4 days it only accumulated few flies so I had to buy apple traps and those are way more effective, killed a bunch in first 24hr. This thing helped too eventually , but if we split efficiency I would say Apple traps vs this is like 80/20 so get it if you buy it together with those, not just as a sole solution

title: Aw gnats
review: I really had high hopes for this and saw the positive reviews but I guess my gnats are smarter. The 1st day I noticed that this didn’t work, then I tried putting apple cider vinegar next to the traps and I feel that helped the gnats accidentally fly in to the trap. Next I tossed the light and stuck the sticky sheets directly on the apple cider vinegar cup side and that worked well.

title: Works depending on location
review: Not a single fruit fly so far, and we have a lot in our house right now. Would not buy this. UPDATE: I originally gave this 1 star. For whatever reason, this did not work in our kitchen where we have the most fruit flies. But it works great in our bathroom. I think it may work better on a white wall because it shines brighter. But I also taped a white piece of paper on the backsplash shown in the attached picture (that’s before I taped the paper) and it still didn’t work great in our kitchen. I think it’s worth the price to try this device, as we also purchased a Zevo and have been disappointed so far.

title: Good in theory?
review: It hasn't caught anything. However, I haven't seen any flies since I put it up, so I really can't say if it is effective or not. I can tell what the product is. Basically just a light with a very small piece of sticky paper directly behind the light. It sounds good in theory. I'll continue to leave it plugged in and see what happens. I noticed flies in front of my door leading into the house. I don't see anything in the vicinity that would be attracting them. If one makes it into the house I'll see what happens with this product.

title: Not so easy to use and doesn't attract many bugs
review: I found this product not to be as good as others and I won't be using it again. It is difficult to get the sticky paper into the slot and the blue light doesn't seem to attract as many bugs as other brands do that I have used. Live and learn.

title: Wish it was better
review: ending Sumer/fall with lots of gnats still. I wish I could say this was 5 stars. I have moved it around kitchen which is only 7x11 feet and still have gnats The trap has caught many gnats but no enough to like this product

title: Alright insect trap
review: It has been working well to catch all the small flying insects, and I’ve even managed to catch a few flies with it.

title: Sticky to use but works okay
review: That’s are sticky to use and easy to get stuck on your fingers. Doesn’t really attract little fruit bugs or flies well unless they just happen to land on them. Probably would not purchase again unless I had a major flying insect issue.

title: The sticky cards work great
review: These plug ins weren't attracting the flies so I took another reviewer's advice and put a little sweet wine in a pint glass and laid the sticky cards across the rim of the glass and that worked great! The fruit fly issue was under control within 24 hrs. and eliminated by 72. If I could, I would buy a box of the sticky cards, as the UV plugs were useless for me. I tried using packing tape with the wine/glass trick with no luck. Not sticky enough. Plus, the sticky cards have something that attracts pests.

title: Did not work for me
review: They do light up. They are sticky. But my fruit flies will not land on them. I don't know why. Returned these and bought another brand, which is working a bit better.

title: Not very effective for fruit flies
review: I recently went out of town for a week and left the wife on her own. We already had a couple fruit flies when I left (maybe 3-5 that I noticed), but this isn't unusual since we always buy fruit as it comes into season and this brings fruit fly eggs into the house. Before I left I just reminded her that the trap needed to be setup and she said it wouldn't be a problem. By trap, I mean the apple shaped trap you can get at just about any store where you put a little vinegar and dish soap in and it just "makes the problem go away." I have used those traps for years and they work great, I just put one on the table near the fruit bowl and one near the kitchen sink. Well, I get home and it seems the wife stopped doing dishes and taking out the trash for a week and and fruit flies had gone ham in the sink. Absolute infestation. Swarms plume from the sink when you approach it. The little apples couldn't keep up. So I figured I would try something new. The new UV trap has been setup for 4 days/3 nights. The trap is plugged in right next to the kitchen sink and all the lights are off at night so this trap has had the best chance of succeeding. It has caught, a disappointing number of flies. Maybe 15-20 in that number of days when the number in the house is multiple hundred. I actually just before writing this unplugged it and waved it around over the sink and caught 4 time more in 30 seconds waving this thing around than I have in 4 days. This is probably fine as a very minor preventative, but it costs way more than the little apples, is far more noticeable and not any more effective. I do not recommend.

title: Doesn't work or is too slow.
review: Look, the idea of trying to get rid of those annoying fruit flies makes my skin crawl and my blood boil at the same time. I hate them. Most insect such as those I despise. But nothing I hate more than fruit flies. This product took AGES to catch even a couple of them, let alone the thousands that are made per day sometimes. If any of you reading this have had them, you know what I mean. They are obnoxious. Here is the thing: the quicker you kill them off, the better. This will not do it, not even close. Left them on for a month and when I went to just toss them in the garbage, I could literally count the fruit flies and other things that somehow found there way behind this to get stuck. Here is how you get rid of fruit flies MUCH QUICKER and for WAY LESS MONEY: Apple cider vinegar + ramekin or other small/medium container + clear plastic wrap + toothpick. Fill half of the ramekin with the vinegar, stretch film over the top. Poke little holes in the saran wrap. Place near infected area. After a day or two, you will be unable to count how many of those little ******* are dead in there. Rinse and repeat when it starts to get too full. I have probably killed millions with this little death pit. These are a gimmick, stay away. Especially for fruit flies. Not sure how well they work for mosquitos.

title: Apple cider vinegar works better than this!
review: This doesn’t even deserve 1 star. It’s officially been 24hrs since it was delivered and plugged in. It has been in my kitchen, directly next to the fruit that sits on the counter. I currently have an INSANE amount of fruit flies due to “someone” leaving an opened applesauce in the pantry…. I did a test. I put a small medicine cap filled with apple cider vinegar and Dawn dish soap in a separate portion of my house, where I have seen the least activity of fruit flies. The kitchen area is over run with fruit flies. The photos speak for themselves. For fun, I even took a piece of cardboard and did a layer of Elmer school glue right after I plugged in the blue light. Again, the photos speak for themselves. You see how many fruit flies were trapped by the Elmers glue makeshift trap, in the short time it took to dry, compared to this $20 piece of junk. I truly don’t understand how this has so many great reviews. Photo 1 is the small cap filled with ACV and Dawn (the cloudiness are drowned fruit flies). Photo 2 is the school glue, photo 3 is this product 🙄🤨 I will be returning this!

title: It didn't work as expected.
review: I recently purchased the ZEVO Fly Trap after reading numerous glowing reviews that touted its effectiveness in catching flies. With summer in full swing and the usual influx of pesky insects, I was eager to try out this product. Unfortunately, my experience has been far from the exceptional results I had hoped for. Performance: Over the course of a week, I placed the ZEVO Fly Trap in a strategic location where I typically see a lot of fly activity. To my disappointment, it only caught one fly during that entire time. I had expected a much higher catch rate based on the reviews I had read, which made me question the reliability of those testimonials. Expectations vs. Reality: Given the rave reviews, I anticipated a significant reduction in the fly population in my home. Instead, I found myself swatting flies as usual, with the trap seemingly doing little to help. It’s puzzling how others have had such positive experiences while mine was lackluster at best. Conclusion: While the ZEVO Fly Trap may work for some, my experience has been disappointing. I had high hopes based on the exceptional reviews, but the results did not match the hype. If you’re considering this product, I recommend tempering your expectations and perhaps exploring other options if you’re dealing with a significant fly problem. For me, it’s back to the drawing board in the search for an effective fly control solution.

title: In FIVE days it only caught THREE FLIES - Sending it back
review: I am underwhelmed. In FIVE days it only caught THREE flies. The old fashioned ugly-ass fly strips that are coated with the sticky attractant are just a few dollars for a pack of ten that will last several months and they work better than this useless contraption. Very disappointed. All those 5 stars Amazon reviews must be AI generated? Right now I am sitting on my couch in my living room and there are 8 flies buzzing around me driving me CRAZY. Flies are strongly attracted to carbon dioxide that humans breathe out. They will land on us and eat the dead skin cells and sebum on our skin. No matter how much you swat them away they keep coming back. This gadget looked impressive - the blue light is supposed to attract the fly into the sticky trap BUT THAT DOES NOT WORK except in a very minimal ineffectual manner. Seriously! For what this costs to only catch THREE flies in FIVE days is unacceptable. I did better putting out a dish of vinegar with sugar as an attractant but put a tbsp of Dawn dish soap in the bowl - that attraxts the fly and they drown. I'm sending it back for a full refund. I also bought a box of refills and that goes back to Amazon. BADLY DONE! 1 star is too high a rating

title: Useless
review: Completely useless. I set it up on the most infested area of the kitchen. Left it there for two weeks. Checked the trap, only one fly on the sticky stuff. One!!! Back to my own homemade waaay cheaper traps of apple cider vinegar and a drop of dish soap. The flies love it! Don't waste your money on this.

title: These are worthless. Do not buy them.
review: DO NOT waste your money on this product. I have had two of these since September. The picture is after 6 months. There is nothing but cat hair. I always have an issue when I bring home fruit. I usually wash it but that still does not guarantee no gnats. The best way to get rid of gnats is this. I get a quart bottle of cider vinegar. I put 2tbs of sugar, and 5 drops of dish detergent in the bottle. The detergent changes the viscosity of the mix so once they get in they can't get out. Put a piece of saran wrap on the top and hold it in place with a rubber band. Poke 3 or 4 holes in the top and leave it next to the source or close to the area that is infested with gnats. I thought these would be great as my wife hates the vinegar smell. But they do nothing. It's a great night light, but I have fairy lights for night lights. Don't waste your time or money on this product if you are trying to kill gnats. I don't know how this product works with mosquitoes, as I have no mosquito problem in the house.

title: Doesn’t Work!
review: DO NOT waste your money…doesn’t work! Had it plugged in for a 2 weeks during the height of fruit fly & pantry moth season. The flies/moths were all over my kitchen. When I attempted to return the product because it didn’t work as advertised, I was told that no refund would be issued *because* I had tried using it. This creates an impossible situation - you can’t know the product doesn’t work without trying it, but once you’ve tried it, you’re apparently stuck with it. My wife contacted Zevo and complained about the poor performance. They said it should really be plugged in in the kitchen, as the flies are (supposed to be) attracted to the blue light. Not quite sure why you would want to draw flies to the kitchen, where the food is prepared. Anyway, we changed the sticky insert and plugged it in beside the kitchen sink. Nearly 3 (yes, three) weeks later, it had caught one (yes, 1) fly. The other flies killed in the kitchen had to be hunted down with a flyswatter. Seems to be OK with gnats, but beyond that it's a waste of money. We do not recommend.

review: Okay. Last I reviewed these or similar as I have used both Zevo lamps and stickers and off-brand lamps and stickers. No matter what you use, brand name or non-brand name, or in any combination, this product is 4 stars for fruit flies / gnats and about 2.75 - 3.0 stars for any other flying insects. It attracts and catches all - mosquitoes, flies, gnats / fruit flies, and other unknown flying insects however, gnats are its specialty. Clearly, my personal experience is stated here. I have a 2 story with about 1,000sf on the ground floor. With 2 units in the kitchen, 2 around my plants, and another in the bedroom I have a flying bug free environment. I use and highly recommend any. Although I have noticed side-by-side the Zevo lamps are a bit brighter but I can tell no difference in the amount of insects trapped with off-brand. Also, as stated (at least by Zevo) they work best when entire rooms can be darkened for the lamp to have the most effect. I suppose lastly - don’t know recommended change interval but I go 6 months before change and have no problems with diminished capacity for trapping.

The traps are placed strategically, but the performance is consistently underwhelming—it's definitely not a strong enough deterrent or attractor to effectively reduce the overall number of gnats, mosquitos or flies. If you need a powerful solution, this isn't it. They are okay, but for the price and the description, I expected much better results.

title: Attracts some but not all species. Liquid bait traps are better.
review: About a month ago I suddenly and inexplicably noticed dozens of tiny little bugs flying around in my kitchen. Absolutely disgusting. Neurotic cleaning ensued, and, eventually, the flies dissipated, but not as quickly as I would have liked. I decided to purchase some fly traps to put my thumb on the scale. These light traps appeared to be working at first. They were definitely catching some flies, but the total number of flies was not visibly decreasing. Then I noticed that the flies stuck on the trap looked different than the ones still flying around. The light was definitely attracting one species of fly, but another species seemed completely unaffected. They were a lighter color, whereas the flies in the trap were darker. After a few days, the darker flies were gone, and the lighter flies appeared to have expanded their population to take advantage of their absence. So anyways, I suppose whether these traps work for you will depend on what species of fly you’re dealing with. For me, these traps were ineffective. I then purchased some of those liquid bait traps that look like tiny little apples, and they worked incredibly well. The liquid comes in a tiny little bottle and cannot be purchased separately, which is asinine, but apple cider vinegar with a little dish soap appears to work just as well as the bait that comes with the trap. I tried using apple cider vinegar with dish soap in a DIY trap before purchasing some traps, but this was not effective. I think it was too difficult for the flies to get to the bait. The premade traps with DIY bait appears to be the best of both worlds.

Maybe I am just cheap, but that is very expensive for something that I see needing to be replaced somewhat frequently to keep its effectiveness up. I love the product but I believe for most people the cost would not be worth it at all, and it very much lowers my hopes for it. ps. it is pretty much the same price to purchase the device again, with the 3 additional traps.

review: I don't know how to rate this product. I had a pretty significant fruit fly infestation for about a week. I cleaned and dried and moved anything resembling food into the fridge. The fruit flies persisted. They were even in my junk mail bin! I bought this, plugged it in, and... you guessed it, the fruit flies continued to hang around! On day one of use, the device caught 2 fruit flies, and on day 2, both fruit flies were gone! No longer stuck to the sticky backing! And more so odd, the infestation ceased! Fruit flies no where to be found! Perhaps they are scared of the devices appearance, or maybe the two escapees informed the general community that a dangerous trap had been installed? I don't know. I almost hope the fruit flies return so I can continue to entertain you with updates. All that said, and yes, I would buy this again. Better safe than sorry.

They are literally flying 15-20 inches from this and ignore it. I'm truly sure this is good for some things. Has to be, cool light and all that should attract bugs. Sad as I was told this was the key weapon for these particular pests, but Umm... Nope. For the record, I've turned off every light in the house but this unit, I've also tried subdued lighting in the house as it seems these things settle in and sleep if it's dark. I put a piece of white paper behind it to really reflect the light better. No joy. Seems whatever I have, are really only motivated by food smells. Not lights, not wine or vinegar, I truly cannot find what (organic matter" they are reproducing in. Which obviously is the base issue. I'm going mad with these things. Pheromones or the 65 dollar floor drain flush are next to try I guess. Never seen these things in my life haha... I move from the inner city to the suburbs, and here we are. lol
